1.29.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
idānīṃ śrotumicchāmi purā dāruvane vibho
pravṛttaṃ tadvanasthānāṃ tapasā bhāvitātmanām //
1.29.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
इदानीं श्रोतुमिच्छामि पुरा दारुवने विभो
प्रवृत्तं तद्वनस्थानां तपसा भावितात्मनाम् ॥
1.29.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Now, O lord, I wish to hear what happened of old in the pine forest / to the dwellers in that forest whose minds were purified by asceticism.

1.29.s:
kathaṃ dāruvanaṃ prāpto bhagavānnīlalohitaḥ
vikṛtaṃ rūpamāsthāya cordhvaretā digambaraḥ //
1.29.d:
कथं दारुवनं प्राप्तो भगवान्नीललोहितः
विकृतं रूपमास्थाय चोर्ध्वरेता दिगम्बरः ॥
1.29.m: How did the lord Nīlalohita reach the pine forest, / having assumed a deformed appearance, celibate and sky-clad?

1.29.s:
kiṃ pravṛttaṃ vane tasmin rudrasya paramātmanaḥ
vaktumarhasi tattvena devadevasya ceṣṭitam //
1.29.d:
किं प्रवृत्तं वने तस्मिन् रुद्रस्य परमात्मनः
वक्तुमर्हसि तत्त्वेन देवदेवस्य चेष्टितम् ॥
1.29.m: What happened in that forest regarding Rudra, the Supreme Self? / You ought to recount accurately the deed of the god of gods.

1.29.s:
sūta uvāca
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā śrutisāravidāṃ varaḥ
śilādasūnurbhagavān prāha kiṃcidbhavaṃ hasan //
1.29.d:
सूत उवाच
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा श्रुतिसारविदां वरः
शिलादसूनुर्भगवान् प्राह किंचिद्भवं हसन् ॥
1.29.m: Sūta said: / Having heard his speech, the son of Śilāda, the lord, best among knowers of the essence of the Śruti, / smiling slightly at Bhava, spoke.

1.29.s:
śailādiruvāca
munayo dārugahane tapastepuḥ sudāruṇam
tuṣṭyarthaṃ devadevasya sadāratanayāgnayaḥ //
1.29.d:
शैलादिरुवाच
मुनयो दारुगहने तपस्तेपुः सुदारुणम्
तुष्ट्यर्थं देवदेवस्य सदारतनयाग्नयः ॥
1.29.m: Śailādi said: / Sages performed very severe asceticism in the thick pine forest / for the pleasure of the god of gods, always maintaining their sons and sacred fires.

1.29.s:
tuṣṭo rudro jagannāthaś cekitāno vṛṣadhvajaḥ
dhūrjaṭiḥ parameśāno bhagavānnīlalohitaḥ //
1.29.d:
तुष्टो रुद्रो जगन्नाथश् चेकितानो वृषध्वजः
धूर्जटिः परमेशानो भगवान्नीललोहितः ॥
1.29.m: Pleased was Rudra, the lord of the world, omniscient, Vṛṣadhvaja, / Dhūrjaṭi, the supreme ruler, the lord Nīlalohita.

1.29.s:
pravṛttilakṣaṇaṃ jñānaṃ jñātuṃ dāruvanaukasām
parīkṣārthaṃ jagannāthaḥ śraddhayā krīḍayā ca saḥ //
1.29.d:
प्रवृत्तिलक्षणं ज्ञानं ज्ञातुं दारुवनौकसाम्
परीक्षार्थं जगन्नाथः श्रद्धया क्रीडया च सः ॥
1.29.m: To ascertain the knowledge characterized by worldly engagement among the dwellers in the pine forest, / the lord of the world, for the sake of testing them, in faith and in play,

1.29.s:
nivṛttilakṣaṇajñānapratiṣṭhārthaṃ ca śaṅkaraḥ
devadāruvanasthānāṃ pravṛttijñānacetasām //
1.29.d:
निवृत्तिलक्षणज्ञानप्रतिष्ठार्थं च शङ्करः
देवदारुवनस्थानां प्रवृत्तिज्ञानचेतसाम् ॥
1.29.m: and to establish the knowledge characterized by renunciation / among those residing in the Devadāru forest whose minds were fixed on knowledge characterized by worldly engagement, Śaṅkara,

1.29.s:
vikṛtaṃ rūpamāsthāya digvāsā viṣamekṣaṇaḥ
mugdho dvihastaḥ kṛṣṇāṅgo divyaṃ dāruvanaṃ yayau //
1.29.d:
विकृतं रूपमास्थाय दिग्वासा विषमेक्षणः
मुग्धो द्विहस्तः कृष्णाङ्गो दिव्यं दारुवनं ययौ ॥
1.29.m: assuming a deformed appearance, sky-clad, with an odd number of eyes, / charming, two-armed, with dark limbs, went to the divine pine forest.

1.29.s:
mandasmitaṃ ca bhagavān strīṇāṃ manasijodbhavam
bhrūvilāsaṃ ca gānaṃ ca cakārātīva suṃdaraḥ //
1.29.d:
मन्दस्मितं च भगवान् स्त्रीणां मनसिजोद्भवम्
भ्रूविलासं च गानं च चकारातीव सुंदरः ॥
1.29.m: The lord smiled gently, awakening love in the women, / and displayed playful brow movements and song, being exceedingly handsome.

1.29.s:
saṃprokṣya nārīvṛndaṃ vai muhurmuhuranaṅgahā
anaṅgavṛddhim akarod atīva madhurākṛtiḥ //
1.29.d:
संप्रोक्ष्य नारीवृन्दं वै मुहुर्मुहुरनङ्गहा
अनङ्गवृद्धिम् अकरोद् अतीव मधुराकृतिः ॥
1.29.m: Constantly casting glances at the assembly of women, the slayer of Anaṅga / increased their love, being exceedingly sweet in form.

1.29.s:
vane taṃ puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā vikṛtaṃ nīlalohitam
striyaḥ pativratāścāpi tamevānvayurādarāt //
1.29.d:
वने तं पुरुषं दृष्ट्वा विकृतं नीललोहितम्
स्त्रियः पतिव्रताश्चापि तमेवान्वयुरादरात् ॥
1.29.m: Seeing that deformed man, Nīlalohita, in the forest, / even women devoted to their husbands followed him with respect.

1.29.s:
vanoṭajadvāragatāś ca nāryo visrastavastrābharaṇā viceṣṭāḥ
labdhvā smitaṃ tasya mukhāravindād drumālayasthās tam athānvayustāḥ //
1.29.d:
वनोटजद्वारगताश् च नार्यो विस्रस्तवस्त्राभरणा विचेष्टाः
लब्ध्वा स्मितं तस्य मुखारविन्दाद् द्रुमालयस्थास् तम् अथान्वयुस्ताः ॥
1.29.m: And the women who had reached the doorways of their forest huts, their clothes and ornaments slipping off, bewildered, / having received a smile from his lotus-face, followed him as they stood near the trees.

1.29.s:
dṛṣṭvā kāścidbhavaṃ nāryo madaghūrṇitalocanāḥ
vilāsabāhyāstāścāpi bhrūvilāsaṃ pracakrire //
1.29.d:
दृष्ट्वा काश्चिद्भवं नार्यो मदघूर्णितलोचनाः
विलासबाह्यास्ताश्चापि भ्रूविलासं प्रचक्रिरे ॥
1.29.m: Seeing Bhava, some women, their eyes rolling with passion, / though inexperienced in coquetry, made playful gestures with their brows.

1.29.s:
atha dṛṣṭvāparā nāryaḥ kiṃcit prahasitānanāḥ
kiṃcid visrastavasanāḥ srastakāñcīguṇā jaguḥ //
1.29.d:
अथ दृष्ट्वापरा नार्यः किंचित् प्रहसिताननाः
किंचिद् विस्रस्तवसनाः स्रस्तकाञ्चीगुणा जगुः ॥
1.29.m: Then, seeing him, other women, their faces slightly smiling, / their garments slightly slipping down, with the cords of their girdles loosened, sang.

1.29.s:
kāścittadā taṃ vipine tu dṛṣṭvā viprāṅganāḥ srastanavāṃśukaṃ vā
svānsvānvicitrān valayānpravidhya madānvitā bandhujanāṃś ca jagmuḥ //
1.29.d:
काश्चित्तदा तं विपिने तु दृष्ट्वा विप्राङ्गनाः स्रस्तनवांशुकं वा
स्वान्स्वान्विचित्रान् वलयान्प्रविध्य मदान्विता बन्धुजनांश् च जग्मुः ॥
1.29.m: Then some wives of Brahmins, seeing him in the forest with loosened fresh garments, / flung away their varied bracelets and, filled with passion, abandoned their kin and went.

1.29.s:
kācittadā taṃ na viveda dṛṣṭvā vivāsanā srastamahāṃśukā ca
śākhāvicitrān viṭapānprasiddhān madānvitā bandhujanāṃstathānyāḥ //
1.29.d:
काचित्तदा तं न विवेद दृष्ट्वा विवासना स्रस्तमहांशुका च
शाखाविचित्रान् विटपान्प्रसिद्धान् मदान्विता बन्धुजनांस्तथान्याः ॥
1.29.m: One woman, seeing him then, lost her senses, naked, her fine garment slipped off, / while others, filled with passion, clung to well-known boughs with varied branches or to their kin.

1.29.s:
kāścijjagustaṃ nanṛtur nipetuś ca dharātale
niṣedurgajavaccānyā provāca dvijapuṅgavāḥ //
1.29.d:
काश्चिज्जगुस्तं ननृतुर् निपेतुश् च धरातले
निषेदुर्गजवच्चान्या प्रोवाच द्विजपुङ्गवाः ॥
1.29.m: Some sang to him, some danced, some fell down on the earth, / and others sat like elephants; he spoke, O best of the twice-born.

1.29.s:
anyonyaṃ sasmitaṃ prekṣya cāliliṅguḥ samantataḥ
nirudhya mārgaṃ rudrasya naipuṇāni pracakrire //
1.29.d:
अन्योन्यं सस्मितं प्रेक्ष्य चालिलिङ्गुः समन्ततः
निरुध्य मार्गं रुद्रस्य नैपुणानि प्रचक्रिरे ॥
1.29.m: Looking at one another with smiles, they embraced him from all sides; / blocking Rudra's path, they displayed their clever arts.

1.29.s:
ko bhavāniti cāhustaṃ āsyatāmiti cāparāḥ
kutretyatha prasīdeti jajalpuḥ prītamānasāḥ //
1.29.d:
को भवानिति चाहुस्तं आस्यतामिति चापराः
कुत्रेत्यथ प्रसीदेति जजल्पुः प्रीतमानसाः ॥
1.29.m: “Who are you?” they asked him; “Please sit,” said others; / “Where [are you going]?” and then “Be gracious!” they prattled, their minds delighted.

1.29.s:
viparītā nipeturvai visrastāṃśukamūrdhajāḥ
pativratāḥ patīnāṃ tu saṃnidhau bhavamāyayā //
1.29.d:
विपरीता निपेतुर्वै विस्रस्तांशुकमूर्धजाः
पतिव्रताः पतीनां तु संनिधौ भवमायया ॥
1.29.m: Turned upside down, their clothes and hair dishevelled, / women devoted to their husbands fell in the very presence of their husbands through Bhava's māyā.

1.29.s:
dṛṣṭvā śrutvā bhavastāsāṃ ceṣṭāvākyāni cāvyayaḥ
śubhaṃ vāpyaśubhaṃ vāpi noktavānparameśvaraḥ //
1.29.d:
दृष्ट्वा श्रुत्वा भवस्तासां चेष्टावाक्यानि चाव्ययः
शुभं वाप्यशुभं वापि नोक्तवान्परमेश्वरः ॥
1.29.m: Seeing and hearing their actions and words, Bhava, the imperishable, / the supreme ruler, said nothing, whether auspicious or inauspicious.

1.29.s:
dṛṣṭvā nārīkulaṃ viprās tathābhūtaṃ ca śaṅkaram
atīva paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ jajalpuste munīśvarāḥ //
1.29.d:
दृष्ट्वा नारीकुलं विप्रास् तथाभूतं च शङ्करम्
अतीव परुषं वाक्यं जजल्पुस्ते मुनीश्वराः ॥
1.29.m: Seeing the assembly of women and Śaṅkara in such a state, the Brahmins, / those lords of sages, uttered exceedingly harsh words.

1.29.s:
tapāṃsi teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pratyāhanyanta śaṅkare
yathādityaprakāśena tārakā nabhasi sthitāḥ //
1.29.d:
तपांसि तेषां सर्वेषां प्रत्याहन्यन्त शङ्करे
यथादित्यप्रकाशेन तारका नभसि स्थिताः ॥
1.29.m: The ascetic merits of all of them were struck back upon encountering Śaṅkara, / just as stars standing in the sky are [dimmed] by the light of the sun.

1.29.s:
śrūyate ṛṣiśāpena brahmaṇastu mahātmanaḥ
samṛddhaśreyasāṃ yonir yajñā vai nāśamāptavān //
1.29.d:
श्रूयते ऋषिशापेन ब्रह्मणस्तु महात्मनः
समृद्धश्रेयसां योनिर् यज्ञा वै नाशमाप्तवान् ॥
1.29.m: It is heard that by a sage's curse the sacrifice of the great-souled Brahmā, / which was the source of abundant blessings, came to destruction.

1.29.s:
bhṛgor api ca śāpena viṣṇuḥ paramavīryavān
prādurbhāvāndaśa prāpto duḥkhitaś ca sadā kṛtaḥ //
1.29.d:
भृगोर् अपि च शापेन विष्णुः परमवीर्यवान्
प्रादुर्भावान्दश प्राप्तो दुःखितश् च सदा कृतः ॥
1.29.m: And by Bhṛgu's curse, Viṣṇu of supreme valour / underwent ten manifestations and was perpetually subjected to grief.

1.29.s:
indrasyāpi ca dharmajña chinnaṃ savṛṣaṇaṃ purā
ṛṣiṇā gautamenorvyāṃ kruddhena vinipātitam //
1.29.d:
इन्द्रस्यापि च धर्मज्ञ छिन्नं सवृषणं पुरा
ऋषिणा गौतमेनोर्व्यां क्रुद्धेन विनिपातितम् ॥
1.29.m: Even Indra's [organ] was severed of old, O knower of righteousness, along with his testicles, / cast down upon the earth by the angry sage Gautama.

1.29.s:
garbhavāso vasūnāṃ ca śāpena vihitas tathā
ṛṣīṇāṃ caiva śāpena nahuṣaḥ sarpatāṃ gataḥ //
1.29.d:
गर्भवासो वसूनां च शापेन विहितस् तथा
ऋषीणां चैव शापेन नहुषः सर्पतां गतः ॥
1.29.m: And dwelling in the womb was ordained for the Vasus by a curse; / and by the curse of sages, Nahuṣa was turned into a serpent.

1.29.s:
kṣīrodaś ca samudro 'sau nivāsaḥ sarvadā hareḥ
dvitīyaścāmṛtādhāro hy apeyo brāhmaṇaiḥ kṛtaḥ //
1.29.d:
क्षीरोदश् च समुद्रो ऽसौ निवासः सर्वदा हरेः
द्वितीयश्चामृताधारो ह्य् अपेयो ब्राह्मणैः कृतः ॥
1.29.m: And the Ocean of Milk, the perpetual dwelling of Hari / and second vessel of nectar, was rendered unfit to drink by Brahmins.

1.29.s:
avimukteśvaraṃ prāpya vārāṇasyāṃ janārdanaḥ
kṣīreṇa cābhiṣicyeśaṃ devadevaṃ triyaṃbakam //
1.29.d:
अविमुक्तेश्वरं प्राप्य वाराणस्यां जनार्दनः
क्षीरेण चाभिषिच्येशं देवदेवं त्रियंबकम् ॥
1.29.m: Having reached Avimukteśvara in Vārāṇasī, Janārdana / anointed the lord, the god of gods, the three-eyed one, with milk;

1.29.s:
śraddhayā parayā yukto dehāśleṣāmṛtena vai
niṣiktena svayaṃ devaḥ kṣīreṇa madhusūdanaḥ //
1.29.d:
श्रद्धया परया युक्तो देहाश्लेषामृतेन वै
निषिक्तेन स्वयं देवः क्षीरेण मधुसूदनः ॥
1.29.m: filled with supreme faith, the lord Madhusūdana / himself poured milk, which was nectar through contact with his body;

1.29.s:
secayitvātha bhagavān brahmaṇā munibhiḥ samam
kṣīrodaṃ pūrvavaccakre nivāsaṃ cātmanaḥ prabhuḥ //
1.29.d:
सेचयित्वाथ भगवान् ब्रह्मणा मुनिभिः समम्
क्षीरोदं पूर्ववच्चक्रे निवासं चात्मनः प्रभुः ॥
1.29.m: having thus anointed him, the glorious lord, together with Brahmā and the sages, / restored the Ocean of Milk as before to be his own abode.

1.29.s:
dharmaścaiva tathā śapto māṇḍavyena mahātmanā
vṛṣṇayaścaiva kṛṣṇena durvāsādyairmahātmabhiḥ //
1.29.d:
धर्मश्चैव तथा शप्तो माण्डव्येन महात्मना
वृष्णयश्चैव कृष्णेन दुर्वासाद्यैर्महात्मभिः ॥
1.29.m: Dharma too was cursed by the great-souled Māṇḍavya, / and the Vṛṣṇis, along with Kṛṣṇa, by the great-souled Durvāsas and others.

1.29.s:
rāghavaḥ sānujaś cāpi durvāsena mahātmanā
śrīvatsaś ca muneḥ pāda patanāttasya dhīmataḥ //
1.29.d:
राघवः सानुजश् चापि दुर्वासेन महात्मना
श्रीवत्सश् च मुनेः पाद पतनात्तस्य धीमतः ॥
1.29.m: Rāghava along with his younger brother [was cursed] by the great-souled Durvāsas; / and the Śrīvatsa mark [on Viṣṇu's chest came] from the fall of that wise sage's foot.

1.29.s:
ete cānye ca bahavo viprāṇāṃ vaśamāgatāḥ
varjayitvā virūpākṣaṃ devadevamumāpatim //
1.29.d:
एते चान्ये च बहवो विप्राणां वशमागताः
वर्जयित्वा विरूपाक्षं देवदेवमुमापतिम् ॥
1.29.m: These and many others came under the power of the Brahmins, / except for Virūpākṣa, the god of gods, the lord of Umā.

1.29.s:
evaṃ hi mohitāstena nāvabudhyanta śaṅkaram
atyugravacanaṃ procuś cogro 'pyantaradhīyata //
1.29.d:
एवं हि मोहितास्तेन नावबुध्यन्त शङ्करम्
अत्युग्रवचनं प्रोचुश् चोग्रो ऽप्यन्तरधीयत ॥
1.29.m: Deluded thus by him, they did not recognize Śaṅkara; / they spoke very fierce words, and the fierce one vanished.

1.29.s:
te 'pi dāruvanāttasmāt prātaḥ saṃvignamānasāḥ
pitāmahaṃ mahātmānam āsīnaṃ paramāsane //
1.29.d:
ते ऽपि दारुवनात्तस्मात् प्रातः संविग्नमानसाः
पितामहं महात्मानम् आसीनं परमासने ॥
1.29.m: They too, from that pine forest in the morning, their minds agitated, / went to the great-souled Pitāmaha seated on his supreme throne,

1.29.s:
gatvā vijñāpayāmāsuḥ pravṛttamakhilaṃ vibhoḥ
śubhe dāruvane tasmin munayaḥ kṣīṇacetasaḥ //
1.29.d:
गत्वा विज्ञापयामासुः प्रवृत्तमखिलं विभोः
शुभे दारुवने तस्मिन् मुनयः क्षीणचेतसः ॥
1.29.m: and the sages, disheartened, reported everything that had happened regarding the lord / in that auspicious pine forest.

1.29.s:
so 'pi saṃcintya manasā kṣaṇādeva pitāmahaḥ
teṣāṃ pravṛttamakhilaṃ puṇye dāruvane purā //
1.29.d:
सो ऽपि संचिन्त्य मनसा क्षणादेव पितामहः
तेषां प्रवृत्तमखिलं पुण्ये दारुवने पुरा ॥
1.29.m: He too, Pitāmaha, reflecting in his mind in an instant / upon all that had happened to them of old in the holy pine forest,

1.29.s:
utthāya prāñjalirbhūtvā praṇipatya bhavāya ca
uvāca satvaraṃ brahmā munīndāruvanālayān //
1.29.d:
उत्थाय प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा प्रणिपत्य भवाय च
उवाच सत्वरं ब्रह्मा मुनीन्दारुवनालयान् ॥
1.29.m: stood up, joined his hands in reverence, prostrated to Bhava, / and Brahmā spoke swiftly to the sages dwelling in the pine forest:

1.29.s:
dhig yuṣmān prāptanidhanān mahānidhim anuttamam
vṛthākṛtaṃ yato viprā yuṣmābhir bhāgyavarjitaiḥ //
1.29.d:
धिग् युष्मान् प्राप्तनिधनान् महानिधिम् अनुत्तमम्
वृथाकृतं यतो विप्रा युष्माभिर् भाग्यवर्जितैः ॥
1.29.m: “Fie upon you, who have met ruin, for an unexcelled great treasure / has been rendered futile by you, O Brahmins, bereft of good fortune!

1.29.s:
yastu dāruvane tasmiṃl liṅgī dṛṣṭo 'pyaliṅgibhiḥ
yuṣmābhir vikṛtākāraḥ sa eva parameśvaraḥ //
1.29.d:
यस्तु दारुवने तस्मिंल् लिङ्गी दृष्टो ऽप्यलिङ्गिभिः
युष्माभिर् विकृताकारः स एव परमेश्वरः ॥
1.29.m: He who was seen in that pine forest as an ascetic possessing the liṅga by you who lacked the liṅga, / deformed in appearance, was none other than the supreme ruler.”

1.29.s:
gṛhasthaiś ca na nindyāstu sadā hyatithayo dvijāḥ
virūpāś ca surūpāś ca malināścāpyapaṇḍitāḥ //
1.29.d:
गृहस्थैश् च न निन्द्यास्तु सदा ह्यतिथयो द्विजाः
विरूपाश् च सुरूपाश् च मलिनाश्चाप्यपण्डिताः ॥
1.29.m: Householders must never despise guests who are Brahmins, / whether misshapen or handsome, soiled or unlearned.

1.29.s:
sudarśanena muninā kālamṛtyurapi svayam
purā bhūmau dvijāgryeṇa jito hyatithipūjayā //
1.29.d:
सुदर्शनेन मुनिना कालमृत्युरपि स्वयम्
पुरा भूमौ द्विजाग्र्येण जितो ह्यतिथिपूजया ॥
1.29.m: Long ago on earth, even Time and Death was conquered / by the sage Sudarśana, best of Brahmins, through hospitality to guests.

1.29.s:
anyathā nāsti saṃtartuṃ gṛhasthaiś ca dvijottamaiḥ
tyaktvā cātithipūjāṃ tām ātmano bhuvi śodhanam //
1.29.d:
अन्यथा नास्ति संतर्तुं गृहस्थैश् च द्विजोत्तमैः
त्यक्त्वा चातिथिपूजां ताम् आत्मनो भुवि शोधनम् ॥
1.29.m: There is no other way for householders, best of Brahmins, to cross over / if they abandon the worship of guests, which purifies oneself on earth.

1.29.s:
gṛhastho 'pi purā jetuṃ sudarśana iti śrutaḥ
pratijñāmakarojjāyāṃ bhāryāmāha pativratām //
1.29.d:
गृहस्थो ऽपि पुरा जेतुं सुदर्शन इति श्रुतः
प्रतिज्ञामकरोज्जायां भार्यामाह पतिव्रताम् ॥
1.29.m: Long ago, Sudarśana, renowned as a householder, / made a vow in order to conquer [death], and said to his faithful wife:

1.29.s:
suvrate subhru subhage śṛṇu sarvaṃ prayatnataḥ
tvayā vai nāvamantavyā gṛhe hyatithayaḥ sadā //
1.29.d:
सुव्रते सुभ्रु सुभगे शृणु सर्वं प्रयत्नतः
त्वया वै नावमन्तव्या गृहे ह्यतिथयः सदा ॥
1.29.m: “O woman of good vows, fair-browed and blessed one, listen attentively to everything: / you must never disrespect guests in our home.

1.29.s:
sarva eva svayaṃ sākṣād atithiryatpinākadhṛk
tasmādatithaye dattvā ātmānamapi pūjaya //
1.29.d:
सर्व एव स्वयं साक्षाद् अतिथिर्यत्पिनाकधृक्
तस्मादतिथये दत्त्वा आत्मानमपि पूजय ॥
1.29.m: For every guest is directly the Pināka-bearer himself; / therefore, having offered yourself to the guest, worship him!”

1.29.s:
evamuktvātha saṃtaptā vivaśā sā pativratā
patimāha rudantī ca kimuktaṃ bhavatā prabho //
1.29.d:
एवमुक्त्वाथ संतप्ता विवशा सा पतिव्रता
पतिमाह रुदन्ती च किमुक्तं भवता प्रभो ॥
1.29.m: Having been spoken to thus, the faithful wife, distressed and helpless, / weeping, said to her husband: “What have you said, my lord?”

1.29.s:
tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā punaḥ prāha sudarśanaḥ
deyaṃ sarvaṃ śivāyārye śiva evātithiḥ svayam //
1.29.d:
तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा पुनः प्राह सुदर्शनः
देयं सर्वं शिवायार्ये शिव एवातिथिः स्वयम् ॥
1.29.m: Hearing her words, Sudarśana spoke again: / “Everything must be given to Śiva, noble lady; Śiva himself is the guest.

1.29.s:
tasmātsarve pūjanīyāḥ sarve 'pyatithayaḥ sadā
evamuktā tadā bhartrā bhāryā tasya pativratā //
1.29.d:
तस्मात्सर्वे पूजनीयाः सर्वे ऽप्यतिथयः सदा
एवमुक्ता तदा भर्त्रा भार्या तस्य पतिव्रता ॥
1.29.m: Therefore, all guests are always to be worshipped.” / Being thus addressed by her husband, his faithful wife

1.29.s:
śeṣāmivājñāmādāya mūrdhnā sā prācarattadā
parīkṣituṃ tathā śraddhāṃ tayoḥ sākṣād dvijottamāḥ //
1.29.d:
शेषामिवाज्ञामादाय मूर्ध्ना सा प्राचरत्तदा
परीक्षितुं तथा श्रद्धां तयोः साक्षाद् द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
1.29.m: placed his command upon her head like a leftover offering and acted accordingly. / Then, O best of Brahmins, to test the faith of the two of them,

1.29.s:
dharmo dvijottamo bhūtvā jagāmātha munergṛham
taṃ dṛṣṭvā cārcayāmāsa sārghyādyairanaghā dvijam //
1.29.d:
धर्मो द्विजोत्तमो भूत्वा जगामाथ मुनेर्गृहम्
तं दृष्ट्वा चार्चयामास सार्घ्याद्यैरनघा द्विजम् ॥
1.29.m: Dharma assumed the form of an excellent Brahmin and went to the sage’s house. / Seeing him, the sinless woman worshipped the Brahmin with water for guest-offering and the like.

1.29.s:
sampūjitastayā tāṃ tu prāha dharmo dvijaḥ svayam
bhadre kutaḥ patirdhīmāṃs tava bhartā sudarśanaḥ //
1.29.d:
सम्पूजितस्तया तां तु प्राह धर्मो द्विजः स्वयम्
भद्रे कुतः पतिर्धीमांस् तव भर्ता सुदर्शनः ॥
1.29.m: Worshipped by her, Dharma himself, [in the form of] a Brahmin, said to her: / “Auspicious lady, where has your wise husband Sudarśana gone?

1.29.s:
annādyairalamadyārye svaṃ dātumiha cārhasi
sā ca lajjāvṛtā nārī smarantī kathitaṃ purā //
1.29.d:
अन्नाद्यैरलमद्यार्ये स्वं दातुमिह चार्हसि
सा च लज्जावृता नारी स्मरन्ती कथितं पुरा ॥
1.29.m: Enough of food and the like today, noble lady; you should give yourself here.” / Overcome with shame, the woman remembered what had been said earlier

1.29.s:
bhartrā nyamīlayannetre cacāla ca pativratā
kiṃcetyāha punastaṃ vai dharme cakre ca sā matim //
1.29.d:
भर्त्रा न्यमीलयन्नेत्रे चचाल च पतिव्रता
किंचेत्याह पुनस्तं वै धर्मे चक्रे च सा मतिम् ॥
1.29.m: by her husband, closed her eyes, and trembled, faithful to her vows. / Saying, “What else?”, she then fixed her mind on Dharma,

1.29.s:
nivedituṃ kilātmānaṃ tasmai patyurihājñayā
etasminnantare bhartā tasyā nāryāḥ sudarśanaḥ //
1.29.d:
निवेदितुं किलात्मानं तस्मै पत्युरिहाज्ञया
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे भर्ता तस्या नार्याः सुदर्शनः ॥
1.29.m: in order to offer herself to him by her husband’s command. / Meanwhile, the husband of that woman, the wise Sudarśana,

1.29.s:
gṛhadvāraṃ gato dhīmāṃs tāmuvāca mahāmuniḥ
ehyehi kva gatā bhadre tamuvācātithiḥ svayam //
1.29.d:
गृहद्वारं गतो धीमांस् तामुवाच महामुनिः
एह्येहि क्व गता भद्रे तमुवाचातिथिः स्वयम् ॥
1.29.m: the great sage, came to the door of the house and said to her: / “Come, come! Where have you gone, blessed lady?” The guest himself said to him:

1.29.s:
bhāryayā tvanayā sārdhaṃ maithunastho 'hamadya vai
sudarśana mahābhāga kiṃ kartavyamihocyatām //
1.29.d:
भार्यया त्वनया सार्धं मैथुनस्थो ऽहमद्य वै
सुदर्शन महाभाग किं कर्तव्यमिहोच्यताम् ॥
1.29.m: “I am engaged in intercourse with this wife of yours today; / O illustrious Sudarśana, tell me what should be done here!

1.29.s:
suratāntastu viprendra saṃtuṣṭo 'haṃ dvijottama
sudarśanastataḥ prāha suprahṛṣṭo dvijottamaḥ //
1.29.d:
सुरतान्तस्तु विप्रेन्द्र संतुष्टो ऽहं द्विजोत्तम
सुदर्शनस्ततः प्राह सुप्रहृष्टो द्विजोत्तमः ॥
1.29.m: I am satisfied, O best of Brahmins, at the conclusion of pleasure.” / Then Sudarśana, the excellent Brahmin, exceedingly delighted, said:

1.29.s:
bhuṅkṣva caināṃ yathākāmaṃ gamiṣye 'haṃ dvijottama
hṛṣṭo 'tha darśayāmāsa svātmānaṃ dharmarāṭ svayam //
1.29.d:
भुङ्क्ष्व चैनां यथाकामं गमिष्ये ऽहं द्विजोत्तम
हृष्टो ऽथ दर्शयामास स्वात्मानं धर्मराट् स्वयम् ॥
1.29.m: “Enjoy her as you desire; I will depart, O best of Brahmins!” / Then the King of Dharma, delighted, revealed his true self

1.29.s:
pradadau cepsitaṃ sarvaṃ tamāha ca mahādyutiḥ
eṣā na bhuktā viprendra manasāpi suśobhanā //
1.29.d:
प्रददौ चेप्सितं सर्वं तमाह च महाद्युतिः
एषा न भुक्ता विप्रेन्द्र मनसापि सुशोभना ॥
1.29.m: and granted all that was desired. The one of great splendour said to him: / “This very lovely woman has not been enjoyed by me even in thought,

1.29.s:
mayā caiṣā na saṃdehaḥ śraddhāṃ jñātumihāgataḥ
jito vai yastvayā mṛtyur dharmeṇaikena suvrata //
1.29.d:
मया चैषा न संदेहः श्रद्धां ज्ञातुमिहागतः
जितो वै यस्त्वया मृत्युर् धर्मेणैकेन सुव्रत ॥
1.29.m: without doubt; I came here to test your faith. / Since death was conquered by you through righteousness alone, O you of good vows,

1.29.s:
aho 'sya tapaso vīryam ityuktvā prayayau ca saḥ
tasmāttathā pūjanīyāḥ sarve hyatithayaḥ sadā //
1.29.d:
अहो ऽस्य तपसो वीर्यम् इत्युक्त्वा प्रययौ च सः
तस्मात्तथा पूजनीयाः सर्वे ह्यतिथयः सदा ॥
1.29.m: ah, the power of his asceticism!” Having said this, he departed. / Therefore, all guests should always be worshipped in this manner.

1.29.s:
bahunātra kimuktena bhāgyahīnā dvijottamāḥ
tameva śaraṇaṃ tūrṇaṃ gantumarhatha śaṅkaram //
1.29.d:
बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन भाग्यहीना द्विजोत्तमाः
तमेव शरणं तूर्णं गन्तुमर्हथ शङ्करम् ॥
1.29.m: What is the use of saying more here? O unfortunate Brahmins, / you should swiftly take refuge in that very Śaṅkara!”

1.29.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā brahmaṇo brāhmaṇarṣabhāḥ
brahmāṇamabhivandyārtāḥ procurākulitekṣaṇāḥ //
1.29.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मणो ब्राह्मणर्षभाः
ब्रह्माणमभिवन्द्यार्ताः प्रोचुराकुलितेक्षणाः ॥
1.29.m: Hearing these words of Brahmā, the foremost of Brahmins / bowed down to Brahmā, afflicted, and with agitated eyes spoke.

1.29.s:
brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ
nāpekṣitaṃ mahābhāga jīvitaṃ vikṛtāḥ striyaḥ
dṛṣṭo 'smābhir mahādevo nindito yastvaninditaḥ //
1.29.d:
ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः
नापेक्षितं महाभाग जीवितं विकृताः स्त्रियः
दृष्टो ऽस्माभिर् महादेवो निन्दितो यस्त्वनिन्दितः ॥
1.29.m: The Brahmins said: / “O illustrious one, we have no regard for life; our wives are disfigured; / Mahādeva was seen by us, and he who is blameless was reviled!

1.29.s:
śaptaś ca sarvagaḥ śūlī pinākī nīlalohitaḥ
ajñānācchāpajā śaktiḥ kuṇṭhitāsyanirīkṣaṇāt //
1.29.d:
शप्तश् च सर्वगः शूली पिनाकी नीललोहितः
अज्ञानाच्छापजा शक्तिः कुण्ठितास्यनिरीक्षणात् ॥
1.29.m: The all-pervading trident-holder, the Pināka-bearer, Nīlalohita, was cursed; / out of ignorance, the power of our curse became blunted upon looking at his face!

1.29.s:
vaktumarhasi deveśa saṃnyāsaṃ vai krameṇa tu
draṣṭuṃ vai devadeveśam ugraṃ bhīmaṃ kapardinam //
1.29.d:
वक्तुमर्हसि देवेश संन्यासं वै क्रमेण तु
द्रष्टुं वै देवदेवेशम् उग्रं भीमं कपर्दिनम् ॥
1.29.m: You ought to tell us, O Lord of gods, the gradual path of renunciation, / so that we may see the Lord of the god of gods, the fierce, terrifying Kapardin.”

1.29.s:
pitāmaha uvāca
ādau vedānadhītyaiva śraddhayā ca guroḥ sadā
vicāryārthaṃ munerdharmān pratijñāya dvijottamāḥ //
1.29.d:
पितामह उवाच
आदौ वेदानधीत्यैव श्रद्धया च गुरोः सदा
विचार्यार्थं मुनेर्धर्मान् प्रतिज्ञाय द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
1.29.m: Pitāmaha said: / “Having first studied the Vedas with faith under a teacher at all times, / having investigated their meaning, and undertaken the duties of a sage, O best of Brahmins,

1.29.s:
grahaṇāntaṃ hi vā vidvān atha dvādaśavārṣikam
snātvāhṛtya ca dārānvai putrānutpādya suvratān //
1.29.d:
ग्रहणान्तं हि वा विद्वान् अथ द्वादशवार्षिकम्
स्नात्वाहृत्य च दारान्वै पुत्रानुत्पाद्य सुव्रतान् ॥
1.29.m: either until they are grasped or for twelve years, the learned man / should take the ritual bath, take a wife, and father sons of good vows.

1.29.s:
vṛttibhiścānurūpābhis tān vibhajya sutānmuniḥ
agniṣṭomādibhiśceṣṭvā yajñairyajñeśvaraṃ vibhum //
1.29.d:
वृत्तिभिश्चानुरूपाभिस् तान् विभज्य सुतान्मुनिः
अग्निष्टोमादिभिश्चेष्ट्वा यज्ञैर्यज्ञेश्वरं विभुम् ॥
1.29.m: The sage, having apportioned appropriate livelihoods to those sons / and worshipped the all-pervading Lord of sacrifices with Agniṣṭoma and other sacrifices,

1.29.s:
pūjayet paramātmānaṃ prāpyāraṇyaṃ vibhāvasau
munirdvādaśavarṣaṃ vā varṣamātram athāpi vā //
1.29.d:
पूजयेत् परमात्मानं प्राप्यारण्यं विभावसौ
मुनिर्द्वादशवर्षं वा वर्षमात्रम् अथापि वा ॥
1.29.m: should reach the forest and worship the Supreme Self in the fire. / The sage should, for twelve years, or for a single year,

1.29.s:
pakṣadvādaśakaṃ vāpi dinadvādaśakaṃ tu vā
kṣīrabhuk saṃyutaḥ śāntaḥ sarvān sampūjayetsurān //
1.29.d:
पक्षद्वादशकं वापि दिनद्वादशकं तु वा
क्षीरभुक् संयुतः शान्तः सर्वान् सम्पूजयेत्सुरान् ॥
1.29.m: or for twelve fortnights, or even for twelve days, / subsisting on milk, restrained, and calm, worship all the gods.

1.29.s:
iṣṭvaivaṃ juhuyādagnau yajñapātrāṇi mantrataḥ
apsu vai pārthivaṃ nyasya gurave taijasāni tu //
1.29.d:
इष्ट्वैवं जुहुयादग्नौ यज्ञपात्राणि मन्त्रतः
अप्सु वै पार्थिवं न्यस्य गुरवे तैजसानि तु ॥
1.29.m: Having thus sacrificed, he should offer the sacrificial vessels into the fire with mantras; / casting earthenware into the water, but metal ones to his teacher,

1.29.s:
svadhanaṃ sakalaṃ caiva brāhmaṇebhyo viśaṅkayā
praṇipatya guruṃ bhūmau viraktaḥ saṃnyasedyatiḥ //
1.29.d:
स्वधनं सकलं चैव ब्राह्मणेभ्यो विशङ्कया
प्रणिपत्य गुरुं भूमौ विरक्तः संन्यसेद्यतिः ॥
1.29.m: and all his wealth to Brahmins without hesitation, / prostrating to the teacher on the ground, detached, the ascetic should renounce.

1.29.s:
nikṛtya keśān saśikhān upavītaṃ visṛjya ca
pañcabhir juhuyād apsu bhūḥ svāheti vicakṣaṇaḥ //
1.29.d:
निकृत्य केशान् सशिखान् उपवीतं विसृज्य च
पञ्चभिर् जुहुयाद् अप्सु भूः स्वाहेति विचक्षणः ॥
1.29.m: Cutting off the hair including the tuft, and casting off the sacred thread, / the wise man should offer into the waters with five mantras, saying: ‘Svāhā to the earth!’

1.29.s:
tataścordhvaṃ caredevaṃ yatiḥ śivavimuktaye
vratenānaśanenāpi toyavṛttyāpi vā punaḥ //
1.29.d:
ततश्चोर्ध्वं चरेदेवं यतिः शिवविमुक्तये
व्रतेनानशनेनापि तोयवृत्त्यापि वा पुनः ॥
1.29.m: Thereafter, the ascetic should conduct himself in this manner for liberation in Śiva: / by means of vows, by fasting, or by subsisting on water,

1.29.s:
parṇavṛttyā payovṛttyā phalavṛttyāpi vā yatiḥ
evaṃ jīvanmṛto no cet ṣaṇmāsādvatsarāttu vā //
1.29.d:
पर्णवृत्त्या पयोवृत्त्या फलवृत्त्यापि वा यतिः
एवं जीवन्मृतो नो चेत् षण्मासाद्वत्सरात्तु वा ॥
1.29.m: or the ascetic may subsist on leaves, on milk, or on fruit. / If he is not dead while living in this way after six months or a year,

1.29.s:
prasthānādikamāyāsaṃ svadehasya caredyatiḥ
śivasāyujyamāpnoti karmaṇāpyevamācaran //
1.29.d:
प्रस्थानादिकमायासं स्वदेहस्य चरेद्यतिः
शिवसायुज्यमाप्नोति कर्मणाप्येवमाचरन् ॥
1.29.m: the ascetic should undertake the final departure and exertion of his body. / Acting in this manner through ritual action, he attains complete union with Śiva.

1.29.s: sadyo 'pi labhate muktiṃ bhaktiyukto dṛḍhavratāḥ //
1.29.d: सद्यो ऽपि लभते मुक्तिं भक्तियुक्तो दृढव्रताः ॥
1.29.m: One endowed with devotion, steadfast in vows, attains liberation even instantly.

1.29.s:
tyāgena vā kiṃ vidhināpy anena bhaktasya rudrasya śubhairvrataiśca
yajñaiś ca dānairvividhaiś ca homair labdhaiścaśāstrairvividhaiś ca vedaiḥ //
1.29.d:
त्यागेन वा किं विधिनाप्य् अनेन भक्तस्य रुद्रस्य शुभैर्व्रतैश्च
यज्ञैश् च दानैर्विविधैश् च होमैर् लब्धैश्चशास्त्रैर्विविधैश् च वेदैः ॥
1.29.m: What need is there of renunciation or of this rule for a devotee of Rudra with auspicious vows, / with sacrifices, various gifts, oblations, acquired treatises, and various Vedas?

1.29.s:
śvetenaivaṃ jito mṛtyur bhavabhaktyā mahātmanā
vo 'stu bhaktirmahādeve śaṅkare paramātmani //
1.29.d:
श्वेतेनैवं जितो मृत्युर् भवभक्त्या महात्मना
वो ऽस्तु भक्तिर्महादेवे शङ्करे परमात्मनि ॥
1.29.m: In this manner, death was conquered by the great-souled Śweta through devotion to Bhava. / May there be devotion in you toward Mahādeva, Śaṅkara, the Supreme Self!”

1.30.s:
śailādiruvāca
evamuktāstadā tena brahmaṇā brāhmaṇarṣabhāḥ
śvetasya ca kathāṃ puṇyām apṛcchan paramarṣayaḥ //
1.30.d:
शैलादिरुवाच
एवमुक्तास्तदा तेन ब्रह्मणा ब्राह्मणर्षभाः
श्वेतस्य च कथां पुण्याम् अपृच्छन् परमर्षयः ॥
1.30.m: Śailādi said: / Being thus addressed at that time by Brahmā, the foremost of Brahmins, / the supreme sages asked about the holy story of Śveta.

1.30.s:
pitāmaha uvāca
śveto nāma muniḥ śrīmān gatāyurgirigahvare
sakto hyabhyarcya yadbhaktyā tuṣṭāva ca maheśvaram //
1.30.d:
पितामह उवाच
श्वेतो नाम मुनिः श्रीमान् गतायुर्गिरिगह्वरे
सक्तो ह्यभ्यर्च्य यद्भक्त्या तुष्टाव च महेश्वरम् ॥
1.30.m: Pitāmaha said: / “A glorious sage named Śveta, whose life had expired, / devotedly worshipped and praised Maheśvara in a mountain cave

1.30.s:
rudrādhyāyena puṇyena namastetyādinā dvijāḥ
tataḥ kālo mahātejāḥ kālaprāptaṃ dvijottamam //
1.30.d:
रुद्राध्यायेन पुण्येन नमस्तेत्यादिना द्विजाः
ततः कालो महातेजाः कालप्राप्तं द्विजोत्तमम् ॥
1.30.m: with the sacred Rudrādhyāya beginning with ‘Salutations!’, O Brahmins. / Then Time, possessed of great splendour, thinking to lead away

1.30.s:
netuṃ saṃcintya viprendrāḥ sānnidhyamakaronmuneḥ
śveto 'pi dṛṣṭvā taṃ kālaṃ kālaprāpto 'pi śaṅkaram //
1.30.d:
नेतुं संचिन्त्य विप्रेन्द्राः सान्निध्यमकरोन्मुनेः
श्वेतो ऽपि दृष्ट्वा तं कालं कालप्राप्तो ऽपि शङ्करम् ॥
1.30.m: the best of Brahmins whose time had come, approached the sage, O foremost of Brahmins. / Śveta also, seeing that Time, even though his time had come, worshipped Śaṅkara,

1.30.s:
pūjayāmāsa puṇyātmā triyaṃbakamanusmaran
triyaṃbakaṃ yajedevaṃ sugandhiṃ puṣṭivardhanam //
1.30.d:
पूजयामास पुण्यात्मा त्रियंबकमनुस्मरन्
त्रियंबकं यजेदेवं सुगन्धिं पुष्टिवर्धनम् ॥
1.30.m: the holy-souled one, recollecting Triyambaka: / ‘One should sacrifice to Triyambaka, fragrant and increaser of nourishment…’”

1.30.s:
kiṃ kariṣyati me mṛtyur mṛtyormṛtyurahaṃ yataḥ
taṃ dṛṣṭvā sasmitaṃ prāha śvetaṃ lokabhayaṃkaraḥ //
1.30.d:
किं करिष्यति मे मृत्युर् मृत्योर्मृत्युरहं यतः
तं दृष्ट्वा सस्मितं प्राह श्वेतं लोकभयंकरः ॥
1.30.m:
"What will Death do to me, since I am the death of Death?"
Seeing him, the Terrifier of the Worlds said with a smile to Śveta:

1.30.s:
ehyehi śveta cānena vidhinā kiṃ phalaṃ tava
rudro vā bhagavān viṣṇur brahmā vā jagadīśvaraḥ //
1.30.d:
एह्येहि श्वेत चानेन विधिना किं फलं तव
रुद्रो वा भगवान् विष्णुर् ब्रह्मा वा जगदीश्वरः ॥
1.30.m:
"Come, come, Śveta! What is the fruit of this rite for you?
Whether Rudra, the Lord Viṣṇu, or Brahmā, the Lord of the Universe,

1.30.s:
kaḥ samarthaḥ paritrātuṃ mayā grastaṃ dvijottama
anena mama kiṃ vipra raudreṇa vidhinā prabhoḥ //
1.30.d:
कः समर्थः परित्रातुं मया ग्रस्तं द्विजोत्तम
अनेन मम किं विप्र रौद्रेण विधिना प्रभोः ॥
1.30.m:
who is capable of saving one seized by me, O best of the twice-born?
What is this fierce rite of the Lord to me, O vipra?

1.30.s:
netuṃ yasyotthitaścāhaṃ yamalokaṃ kṣaṇena vai
yasmādgatāyustvaṃ tasmān mune netumihodyataḥ //
1.30.d:
नेतुं यस्योत्थितश्चाहं यमलोकं क्षणेन वै
यस्माद्गतायुस्त्वं तस्मान् मुने नेतुमिहोद्यतः ॥
1.30.m:
For I have arisen to carry you off to Yama's world in an instant.
Because your life has expired, O sage, I have therefore risen here to take you."

1.30.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā bhairavaṃ dharmamiśritam
hā rudra rudra rudreti lalāpa munipuṅgavaḥ //
1.30.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा भैरवं धर्ममिश्रितम्
हा रुद्र रुद्र रुद्रेति ललाप मुनिपुङ्गवः ॥
1.30.m:
Hearing that terrible utterance of his, mixed with righteousness,
the bull among sages wailed, "Ah Rudra, Rudra, Rudra!"

1.30.s:
taṃ prāha ca mahādevaṃ kālaṃ samprekṣya vai dṛśā
netreṇa bāṣpamiśreṇa saṃbhrāntena samākulaḥ //
1.30.d:
तं प्राह च महादेवं कालं सम्प्रेक्ष्य वै दृशा
नेत्रेण बाष्पमिश्रेण संभ्रान्तेन समाकुलः ॥
1.30.m:
He spoke to Mahādeva, gazing upon Kāla with his eye,
bewildered and agitated, with an eye full of tears:

1.30.s:
śveta uvāca
tvayā kiṃ kāla no nāthaś cāsti ceddhi vṛṣadhvajaḥ
liṅge 'smin śaṅkaro rudraḥ sarvadevabhavodbhavaḥ //
1.30.d:
श्वेत उवाच
त्वया किं काल नो नाथश् चास्ति चेद्धि वृषध्वजः
लिङ्गे ऽस्मिन् शङ्करो रुद्रः सर्वदेवभवोद्भवः ॥
1.30.m:
Śveta said:
"O Kāla, do we not have a protector if Vṛṣadhvaja is here?
Śaṅkara, Rudra, the source of the origin of all gods, is in this liṅga.

1.30.s:
atīva bhavabhaktānāṃ madvidhānāṃ mahātmanām
vidhinā kiṃ mahābāho gaccha gaccha yathāgatam //
1.30.d:
अतीव भवभक्तानां मद्विधानां महात्मनाम्
विधिना किं महाबाहो गच्छ गच्छ यथागतम् ॥
1.30.m:
For great souls like me who are exceedingly devoted to Bhava,
what use is your rule, O mighty-armed one? Go, go back the way you came!"

1.30.s:
tato niśamya kupitas tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭro bhayaṅkaraḥ
śrutvā śvetasya tadvākyaṃ pāśahasto bhayāvahaḥ //
1.30.d:
ततो निशम्य कुपितस् तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रो भयङ्करः
श्रुत्वा श्वेतस्य तद्वाक्यं पाशहस्तो भयावहः ॥
1.30.m:
Then, hearing that speech of Śveta, enraged,
the sharp-fanged, terrifying, noose-handed, fearful one,

1.30.s:
siṃhanādaṃ mahatkṛtvā cāsphāṭya ca muhurmuhuḥ
babandha ca muniṃ kālaḥ kālaprāptaṃ tamāha ca //
1.30.d:
सिंहनादं महत्कृत्वा चास्फाट्य च मुहुर्मुहुः
बबन्ध च मुनिं कालः कालप्राप्तं तमाह च ॥
1.30.m:
having uttered a great lion's roar and repeatedly slapping his arms,
Kāla bound the sage whose time had come and said to him:

1.30.s:
mayā baddho 'si viprarṣe śvetaṃ netuṃ yamālayam
adya vai devadevena tava rudreṇa kiṃ kṛtam //
1.30.d:
मया बद्धो ऽसि विप्रर्षे श्वेतं नेतुं यमालयम्
अद्य वै देवदेवेन तव रुद्रेण किं कृतम् ॥
1.30.m:
"You have been bound by me, O royal sage among vipras, so that Śveta may be taken to Yama's abode.
Today, what has been done by your Rudra, the God of gods?

1.30.s:
kva śarvastava bhaktiś ca kva pūjā pūjayā phalam
kva cāhaṃ kva ca me bhītiḥ śveta baddho 'si vai mayā //
1.30.d:
क्व शर्वस्तव भक्तिश् च क्व पूजा पूजया फलम्
क्व चाहं क्व च मे भीतिः श्वेत बद्धो ऽसि वै मया ॥
1.30.m:
Where is your Śarva, and where is devotion? Where is the worship, and the fruit from worship?
And where am I, and where is my fear? Śveta, you are truly bound by me!

1.30.s:
liṅge 'smin saṃsthitaḥ śveta tava rudro maheśvaraḥ
niśceṣṭo 'sau mahādevaḥ kathaṃ pūjyo maheśvaraḥ //
1.30.d:
लिङ्गे ऽस्मिन् संस्थितः श्वेत तव रुद्रो महेश्वरः
निश्चेष्टो ऽसौ महादेवः कथं पूज्यो महेश्वरः ॥
1.30.m:
Śveta, your Rudra, Maheśvara, resides in this liṅga;
this Mahādeva is motionless—how is Maheśvara to be worshipped?"

1.30.s:
tataḥ sadāśivaḥ svayaṃ dvijaṃ nihantumāgatam
nihantumantakaṃ smayan smarāriyajñahā haraḥ //
1.30.d:
ततः सदाशिवः स्वयं द्विजं निहन्तुमागतम्
निहन्तुमन्तकं स्मयन् स्मरारियज्ञहा हरः ॥
1.30.m:
Then Sadāśiva himself, the enemy of Smara and destroyer of the sacrifice, Hara, smiling,
in order to slay Death who had arrived to slay the twice-born,

1.30.s:
tvaran vinirgataḥ paraḥ śivaḥ svayaṃ trilocanaḥ
triyaṃbako 'mbayā samaṃ sanandinā gaṇeśvaraiḥ //
1.30.d:
त्वरन् विनिर्गतः परः शिवः स्वयं त्रिलोचनः
त्रियंबको ऽम्बया समं सनन्दिना गणेश्वरैः ॥
1.30.m:
hastening, went forth, the supreme Śiva himself, the three-eyed one,
Triyambaka, along with the Mother, with Nandin, and the lords of the gaṇas.

1.30.s:
sasarja jīvitaṃ kṣaṇād bhavaṃ nirīkṣya vai bhayāt
papāta cāśu vai balī munestu saṃnidhau dvijāḥ //
1.30.d:
ससर्ज जीवितं क्षणाद् भवं निरीक्ष्य वै भयात्
पपात चाशु वै बली मुनेस्तु संनिधौ द्विजाः ॥
1.30.m:
Beholding Bhava, [Death] in an instant surrendered his life out of fear,
and the mighty one swiftly fell near the sage, O twice-born!

1.30.s:
nanāda cordhvamuccadhīr nirīkṣya cāntakāntakam
nirīkṣaṇena vai mṛtaṃ bhavasya viprapuṅgavāḥ //
1.30.d:
ननाद चोर्ध्वमुच्चधीर् निरीक्ष्य चान्तकान्तकम्
निरीक्षणेन वै मृतं भवस्य विप्रपुङ्गवाः ॥
1.30.m:
The high-minded one roared aloud upon seeing the ender of the End,
who had died by the mere glance of Bhava, O bulls among vipras!

1.30.s:
vineduruccamīśvarāḥ sureśvarā maheśvaram
praṇemuraṃbikāmumāṃ munīśvarāstu harṣitāḥ //
1.30.d:
विनेदुरुच्चमीश्वराः सुरेश्वरा महेश्वरम्
प्रणेमुरंबिकामुमां मुनीश्वरास्तु हर्षिताः ॥
1.30.m:
The sovereign lords of the gods shouted loudly to Maheśvara;
and the lords among sages, filled with joy, bowed down to the Mother Umā.

1.30.s:
sasarjur asya mūrdhni vai munerbhavasya khecarāḥ
suśobhanaṃ suśītalaṃ supuṣpavarṣamaṃbarāt //
1.30.d:
ससर्जुर् अस्य मूर्ध्नि वै मुनेर्भवस्य खेचराः
सुशोभनं सुशीतलं सुपुष्पवर्षमंबरात् ॥
1.30.m:
The sky-dwellers poured down from the sky upon the head of the sage and of Bhava
a very beautiful, very cooling shower of fine flowers.

1.30.s:
aho nirīkṣya cāntakaṃ mṛtaṃ tadā suvismitaḥ
śilāśanātmajo 'vyayaṃ śivaṃ praṇamya śaṅkaram //
1.30.d:
अहो निरीक्ष्य चान्तकं मृतं तदा सुविस्मितः
शिलाशनात्मजो ऽव्ययं शिवं प्रणम्य शङ्करम् ॥
1.30.m:
"Ah!" Having seen the End deceased, the son of Śilāśana,
exceedingly amazed, bowing to the imperishable Śiva, Śaṅkara,

1.30.s:
uvāca bāladhīrmṛtaḥ prasīda ceti vai muneḥ
maheśvaraṃ maheśvara-sya cānugo gaṇeśvaraḥ //
1.30.d:
उवाच बालधीर्मृतः प्रसीद चेति वै मुनेः
महेश्वरं महेश्वर-स्य चानुगो गणेश्वरः ॥
1.30.m:
that lord of gaṇas, the follower of Maheśvara, spoken of as having a childish mind,
said to Maheśvara, "The dead one of the sage... be pleased!"

1.30.s:
tato viveśa bhagavān anugṛhya dvijottamam
kṣaṇādgūḍhaśarīraṃ hi dhvastaṃ dṛṣṭvāntakaṃ kṣaṇāt //
1.30.d:
ततो विवेश भगवान् अनुगृह्य द्विजोत्तमम्
क्षणाद्गूढशरीरं हि ध्वस्तं दृष्ट्वान्तकं क्षणात् ॥
1.30.m:
Then the Lord, having blessed the best of the twice-born,
entered his hidden body in an instant, seeing the End destroyed in an instant.

1.30.s:
tasmānmṛtyuñjayaṃ caiva bhaktyā sampūjaye dvijāḥ
muktidaṃ bhuktidaṃ caiva sarveṣāmapi śaṅkaram //
1.30.d:
तस्मान्मृत्युञ्जयं चैव भक्त्या सम्पूजये द्विजाः
मुक्तिदं भुक्तिदं चैव सर्वेषामपि शङ्करम् ॥
1.30.m:
Therefore, O twice-born, one should worship Mṛtyuñjaya with devotion,
Śaṅkara, who grants liberation and worldly enjoyment to all.

1.30.s:
bahunā kiṃ pralāpena saṃnyasyābhyarcya vai bhavam
bhaktyā cāparayā tasmin viśokā vai bhaviṣyatha //
1.30.d:
बहुना किं प्रलापेन संन्यस्याभ्यर्च्य वै भवम्
भक्त्या चापरया तस्मिन् विशोका वै भविष्यथ ॥
1.30.m:
What is the use of much talk? Having renounced and having worshipped Bhava
with supreme devotion to him, you will indeed become free from grief.

1.30.s:
śailādiruvāca
evamuktāstadā tena brahmaṇā brahmavādinaḥ
prasīda bhaktirdeveśe bhavedrudre pinākini //
1.30.d:
शैलादिरुवाच
एवमुक्तास्तदा तेन ब्रह्मणा ब्रह्मवादिनः
प्रसीद भक्तिर्देवेशे भवेद्रुद्रे पिनाकिनि ॥
1.30.m:
The son of Śilāda said:
Having been addressed thus at that time by that Brahmā, the expounders of the Veda said:
"Be pleased! How may devotion arise toward the Lord of gods, Rudra Pinākin?

1.30.s:
kena vā tapasā deva yajñenāpyatha kena vā
vratairvā bhagavadbhaktā bhaviṣyanti dvijātayaḥ //
1.30.d:
केन वा तपसा देव यज्ञेनाप्यथ केन वा
व्रतैर्वा भगवद्भक्ता भविष्यन्ति द्विजातयः ॥
1.30.m:
Or by what austerity, O Lord, or by what sacrifice,
or by what observances will the twice-born become devotees of the Lord?"

1.30.s:
pitāmaha uvāca
na dānena muniśreṣṭhās tapasā ca na vidyayā
yajñair homair vratair vedair yogaśāstrair nirodhanaiḥ //
1.30.d:
पितामह उवाच
न दानेन मुनिश्रेष्ठास् तपसा च न विद्यया
यज्ञैर् होमैर् व्रतैर् वेदैर् योगशास्त्रैर् निरोधनैः ॥
1.30.m:
Pitāmaha said:
"Not by gift, O best of sages, and not by austerity, nor by learning,
not by sacrifices, offerings, observances, the Vedas, yoga treatises, or restraints,

1.30.s:
prasāde naiva sā bhaktiḥ śive paramakāraṇe
atha tasya vacaḥ śrutvā sarve te paramarṣayaḥ //
1.30.d:
प्रसादे नैव सा भक्तिः शिवे परमकारणे
अथ तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सर्वे ते परमर्षयः ॥
1.30.m:
only by grace does that devotion toward Śiva, the supreme cause, arise."
Then, having heard his word, all those supreme sages,

1.30.s:
sadāratanayāḥ śrāntāḥ praṇemuś ca pitāmaham
tasmātpāśupatī bhaktir dharmakāmārthasiddhidā //
1.30.d:
सदारतनयाः श्रान्ताः प्रणेमुश् च पितामहम्
तस्मात्पाशुपती भक्तिर् धर्मकामार्थसिद्धिदा ॥
1.30.m:
weary, ever devoted to jewels, bowed to Pitāmaha.
Therefore, Pāśupata devotion grants the attainment of righteousness, pleasure, and wealth;

1.30.s:
muner vijayadā caiva sarvamṛtyujayapradā
dadhīcastu purā bhaktyā hariṃ jitvāmarairvibhum //
1.30.d:
मुनेर् विजयदा चैव सर्वमृत्युजयप्रदा
दधीचस्तु पुरा भक्त्या हरिं जित्वामरैर्विभुम् ॥
1.30.m:
it grants victory to the sage and grants victory over all death.
Indeed, Dadhīca in ancient times, having conquered the omnipresent Hari along with the immortals through devotion,

1.30.s:
kṣayaṃ jaghāna pādena vajrāsthitvaṃ ca labdhavān
mayāpi nirjito mṛtyur mahādevasya kīrtanāt //
1.30.d:
क्षयं जघान पादेन वज्रास्थित्वं च लब्धवान्
मयापि निर्जितो मृत्युर् महादेवस्य कीर्तनात् ॥
1.30.m:
struck ruin with his foot and obtained the nature of adamantine bones.
By me too was death conquered through glorifying Mahādeva,

1.30.s:
śvetenāpi gatenāsyaṃ mṛtyormunivareṇa tu
mahādevaprasādena jito mṛtyuryathā mayā //
1.30.d:
श्वेतेनापि गतेनास्यं मृत्योर्मुनिवरेण तु
महादेवप्रसादेन जितो मृत्युर्यथा मया ॥
1.30.m:
as well as by Śveta, the best of sages, who had entered the mouth of Death;
through the grace of Mahādeva, death was conquered just as by me."

1.31.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
kathaṃ bhavaprasādena devadāruvanaukasaḥ
prapannāḥ śaraṇaṃ devaṃ vaktumarhasi me prabho //
1.31.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
कथं भवप्रसादेन देवदारुवनौकसः
प्रपन्नाः शरणं देवं वक्तुमर्हसि मे प्रभो ॥
1.31.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
"How, through the grace of Bhava, did the dwellers of the Devadāru forest
take refuge in the God? You ought to tell me, O Lord."

1.31.s:
śailādiruvāca
tānuvāca mahābhāgān bhagavān ātmabhūḥ svayam
devadāruvanasthāṃstu tapasā pāvakaprabhān //
1.31.d:
शैलादिरुवाच
तानुवाच महाभागान् भगवान् आत्मभूः स्वयम्
देवदारुवनस्थांस्तु तपसा पावकप्रभान् ॥
1.31.m:
The son of Śilāda said:
To those illustrious ones residing in the Devadāru forest, blazing like fire through their austerity,
the Lord, the Self-born one himself, spoke.

1.31.s:
pitāmaha uvāca
eṣa devo mahādevo vijñeyastu maheśvaraḥ
na tasmātparamaṃ kiṃcit padaṃ samadhigamyate //
1.31.d:
पितामह उवाच
एष देवो महादेवो विज्ञेयस्तु महेश्वरः
न तस्मात्परमं किंचित् पदं समधिगम्यते ॥
1.31.m:
Pitāmaha said:
"This God is Mahādeva; he is to be known as Maheśvara.
No state higher than him is attained.

1.31.s:
devānāṃ ca ṛṣīnāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ caiva sa prabhuḥ
sahasrayugaparyante pralaye sarvadehinaḥ //
1.31.d:
देवानां च ऋषीनां च पितॄणां चैव स प्रभुः
सहस्रयुगपर्यन्ते प्रलये सर्वदेहिनः ॥
1.31.m:
He is the Lord of the gods, the sages, and the ancestors.
At the end of a thousand yugas, at the cosmic dissolution of all embodied beings,

1.31.s:
saṃharatyeṣa bhagavān kālo bhūtvā maheśvaraḥ
eṣa caiva prajāḥ sarvāḥ sṛjatyekaḥ svatejasā //
1.31.d:
संहरत्येष भगवान् कालो भूत्वा महेश्वरः
एष चैव प्रजाः सर्वाः सृजत्येकः स्वतेजसा ॥
1.31.m:
this Lord, having become Time, Maheśvara, dissolves [them].
And he alone creates all creatures by his own splendour.

1.31.s:
eṣa cakrī ca vajrī ca śrīvatsakṛtalakṣaṇaḥ
yogī kṛtayuge caiva tretāyāṃ kratur ucyate //
1.31.d:
एष चक्री च वज्री च श्रीवत्सकृतलक्षणः
योगी कृतयुगे चैव त्रेतायां क्रतुर् उच्यते ॥
1.31.m:
He is the bearer of the discus and the thunderbolt, marked by the Śrīvatsa;
he is the yogin in the Kṛta yuga, and in the Tretā he is called the sacrifice;

1.31.s:
dvāpare caiva kālāgnir dharmaketuḥ kalau smṛtaḥ
rudrasya mūrtayastvetā ye 'bhidhyāyanti paṇḍitāḥ //
1.31.d:
द्वापरे चैव कालाग्निर् धर्मकेतुः कलौ स्मृतः
रुद्रस्य मूर्तयस्त्वेता ये ऽभिध्यायन्ति पण्डिताः ॥
1.31.m:
in the Dvāpara he is the fire of Time, and in the Kali he is remembered as Dharmaketu.
These are the forms of Rudra that the wise contemplate.

1.31.s:
caturasraṃ bahiścāntar aṣṭāsraṃ piṇḍikāśraye
vṛttaṃ sudarśanaṃ yogyam evaṃ liṅgaṃ prapūjayet //
1.31.d:
चतुरस्रं बहिश्चान्तर् अष्टास्रं पिण्डिकाश्रये
वृत्तं सुदर्शनं योग्यम् एवं लिङ्गं प्रपूजयेत् ॥
1.31.m:
Square on the outside and octagonal inside the base,
round, beautiful to behold, and fitting—thus one should worship the liṅga.

1.31.s:
tamo hyagnī rajo brahmā sattvaṃ viṣṇuḥ prakāśakam
mūrtirekā sthitā cāsya mūrtayaḥ parikīrtitāḥ //
1.31.d:
तमो ह्यग्नी रजो ब्रह्मा सत्त्वं विष्णुः प्रकाशकम्
मूर्तिरेका स्थिता चास्य मूर्तयः परिकीर्तिताः ॥
1.31.m:
For tamas is Agni, rajas is Brahmā, and sattva is Viṣṇu the illuminator;
his single form exists [thus], and [these] are proclaimed as his forms.

1.31.s:
yatra tiṣṭhati tadbrahma yogena tu samanvitam
tasmāddhi devadeveśam īśānaṃ prabhumavyayam //
1.31.d:
यत्र तिष्ठति तद्ब्रह्म योगेन तु समन्वितम्
तस्माद्धि देवदेवेशम् ईशानं प्रभुमव्ययम् ॥
1.31.m:
Where that Brahman resides, united with yoga—
therefore, the bulls among vipras, with anger conquered and senses restrained,

1.31.s:
ārādhayanti viprendrā jitakrodhā jitendriyāḥ
liṅgaṃ kṛtvā yathānyāyaṃ sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutam //
1.31.d:
आराधयन्ति विप्रेन्द्रा जितक्रोधा जितेन्द्रियाः
लिङ्गं कृत्वा यथान्यायं सर्वलक्षणसंयुतम् ॥
1.31.m:
worship the Lord of the gods of gods, Īśāna, the imperishable Lord,
having made the liṅga according to rule, endowed with all auspicious marks,

1.31.s:
aṅguṣṭhamātraṃ suśubhaṃ suvṛttaṃ sarvasaṃmatam
samanābhaṃ tathāṣṭāsraṃ ṣoḍaśāsram athāpi vā //
1.31.d:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रं सुशुभं सुवृत्तं सर्वसंमतम्
समनाभं तथाष्टास्रं षोडशास्रम् अथापि वा ॥
1.31.m: measuring a thumb in size, very auspicious, perfectly round, approved by all, / evenly proportioned, and eight-sided, or sixteen-sided."

1.31.s:
suvṛttaṃ maṇḍalaṃ divyaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradam
vedikā dviguṇā tasya samā vā sarvasaṃmatā //
1.31.d:
सुवृत्तं मण्डलं दिव्यं सर्वकामफलप्रदम्
वेदिका द्विगुणा तस्य समा वा सर्वसंमता ॥
1.31.m:
a well-rounded, divine circle, granting the fruits of all desires.
Its altar should be twice as large, or equal, as agreed by all,

1.31.s:
gomukhī ca tribhāgaikā vedyā lakṣaṇasaṃyutā
paṭṭikā ca samantādvai yavamātrā dvijottamāḥ //
1.31.d:
गोमुखी च त्रिभागैका वेद्या लक्षणसंयुता
पट्टिका च समन्ताद्वै यवमात्रा द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
1.31.m:
with a cow-mouth measuring one third, endowed with the marks of an altar,
and with a rim all around measuring one barleycorn, O best of the twice-born.

1.31.s:
sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ śailaṃ kṛtvā tāmramayaṃ tathā
vedikāyāś ca vistāraṃ triguṇaṃ vai samantataḥ //
1.31.d:
सौवर्णं राजतं शैलं कृत्वा ताम्रमयं तथा
वेदिकायाश् च विस्तारं त्रिगुणं वै समन्ततः ॥
1.31.m:
Having made it of gold, silver, stone, or copper,
the width of the altar should indeed be three times all around.

1.31.s:
vartulaṃ caturasraṃ vā ṣaḍasraṃ vā trirasrakam
samantānnirvraṇaṃ śubhraṃ lakṣaṇaistat sulakṣitam //
1.31.d:
वर्तुलं चतुरस्रं वा षडस्रं वा त्रिरस्रकम्
समन्तान्निर्व्रणं शुभ्रं लक्षणैस्तत् सुलक्षितम् ॥
1.31.m: Round or four-cornered, or six-cornered or three-cornered, / unblemished all around, bright, and well marked with the auspicious signs,

1.31.s:
pratiṣṭhāpya yathānyāyaṃ pūjālakṣaṇasaṃyutam
kalaśaṃ sthāpayettasya vedimadhye tathā dvijāḥ //
1.31.d:
प्रतिष्ठाप्य यथान्यायं पूजालक्षणसंयुतम्
कलशं स्थापयेत्तस्य वेदिमध्ये तथा द्विजाः ॥
1.31.m: having installed [it] according to rule, endowed with the marks for worship, / one should place a water-pot in the middle of its altar, O twice-born.

1.31.s:
sahiraṇyaṃ sabījaṃ ca brahmabhiś cābhimantritam
secayecca tato liṅgaṃ pavitraiḥ pañcabhiḥ śubhaiḥ //
1.31.d:
सहिरण्यं सबीजं च ब्रह्मभिश् चाभिमन्त्रितम्
सेचयेच्च ततो लिङ्गं पवित्रैः पञ्चभिः शुभैः ॥
1.31.m: Containing gold, containing seeds, and consecrated with the Brahma-mantras, / one should then bathe the liṅga with the five auspicious, sacred [substances].

1.31.s:
pūjayecca yathālābhaṃ tataḥ siddhimavāpsyatha
samāhitāḥ pūjayadhvaṃ saputrāḥ saha bandhubhiḥ //
1.31.d:
पूजयेच्च यथालाभं ततः सिद्धिमवाप्स्यथ
समाहिताः पूजयध्वं सपुत्राः सह बन्धुभिः ॥
1.31.m: And one should worship according to what is obtained; then you will attain perfection. / Worship with concentrated minds, along with your sons and kin.

1.31.s:
sarve prāñjalayo bhūtvā śūlapāṇiṃ prapadyata
tato drakṣyatha deveśaṃ durdarśamakṛtātmabhiḥ //
1.31.d:
सर्वे प्राञ्जलयो भूत्वा शूलपाणिं प्रपद्यत
ततो द्रक्ष्यथ देवेशं दुर्दर्शमकृतात्मभिः ॥
1.31.m: All joining hands in reverence, take refuge in the Trident-bearer; / then you will behold the Lord of gods, hard to be seen by the unrefined.

1.31.s:
yaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvamajñānam adharmaś ca praṇaśyati
tataḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā brahmāṇamamitaujasam //
1.31.d:
यं दृष्ट्वा सर्वमज्ञानम् अधर्मश् च प्रणश्यति
ततः प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा ब्रह्माणममितौजसम् ॥
1.31.m: Having seen whom, all ignorance and unrighteousness perish.” / Then, having circumambulated Brahmā of immeasurable splendor,

1.31.s:
samprasthitā vanaukāste devadāruvanaṃ tataḥ
ārādhayitumārabdhā brahmaṇā kathitaṃ yathā //
1.31.d:
सम्प्रस्थिता वनौकास्ते देवदारुवनं ततः
आराधयितुमारब्धा ब्रह्मणा कथितं यथा ॥
1.31.m: those forest-dwellers set out then for the Devadāru forest; / they began to worship as was spoken by Brahmā:

1.31.s:
sthaṇḍileṣu vicitreṣu parvatānāṃ guhāsu ca
nadīnāṃ ca vivikteṣu pulineṣu śubheṣu ca //
1.31.d:
स्थण्डिलेषु विचित्रेषु पर्वतानां गुहासु च
नदीनां च विविक्तेषु पुलिनेषु शुभेषु च ॥
1.31.m: on variegated bare grounds and in mountain caves, / and on the solitary, auspicious sandbanks of rivers.

1.31.s:
śaivālaśobhanāḥ kecit kecidantarjaleśayāḥ
keciddarbhāvakāśāstu pādāṅguṣṭhāgradhiṣṭhitāḥ //
1.31.d:
शैवालशोभनाः केचित् केचिदन्तर्जलेशयाः
केचिद्दर्भावकाशास्तु पादाङ्गुष्ठाग्रधिष्ठिताः ॥
1.31.m: Some adorned with moss, some lying inside the water, / others resting on Darbha grass, standing on the tips of their big toes,

1.31.s:
dantolūkhalinastvanye aśmakuṭṭās tathā pare
sthānavīrāsanāstvanye mṛgacaryāratāḥ pare //
1.31.d:
दन्तोलूखलिनस्त्वन्ये अश्मकुट्टास् तथा परे
स्थानवीरासनास्त्वन्ये मृगचर्यारताः परे ॥
1.31.m: others using their teeth as a mortar, and others crushing [food] with stones, / others in stationary and heroic postures, others engaged in deer-like conduct,

1.31.s:
kālaṃ nayanti tapasā pūjayā ca mahādhiyaḥ
evaṃ saṃvatsare pūrṇe vasante samupasthite //
1.31.d:
कालं नयन्ति तपसा पूजया च महाधियः
एवं संवत्सरे पूर्णे वसन्ते समुपस्थिते ॥
1.31.m: those of great intellect spent their time in asceticism and worship. / Thus, when a full year had passed and spring had arrived,

1.31.s:
tatasteṣāṃ prasādārthaṃ bhaktānām anukampayā
devaḥ kṛtayuge tasmin girau himavataḥ śubhe //
1.31.d:
ततस्तेषां प्रसादार्थं भक्तानाम् अनुकम्पया
देवः कृतयुगे तस्मिन् गिरौ हिमवतः शुभे ॥
1.31.m: then, for the sake of their grace, out of compassion for His devotees, / the God, in that Kṛta Yuga, on the auspicious mountain of Himavat,

1.31.s:
devadāruvanaṃ prāptaḥ prasannaḥ parameśvaraḥ
bhasmapāṃsūpadigdhāṅgo nagno vikṛtalakṣaṇaḥ //
1.31.d:
देवदारुवनं प्राप्तः प्रसन्नः परमेश्वरः
भस्मपांसूपदिग्धाङ्गो नग्नो विकृतलक्षणः ॥
1.31.m: the gracious Supreme Lord arrived at the Devadāru forest, / His limbs smeared with ash and dust, naked, with deformed features,

1.31.s:
ulmukavyagrahastaś ca raktapiṅgalalocanaḥ
kvacicca hasate raudraṃ kvacidgāyati vismitaḥ //
1.31.d:
उल्मुकव्यग्रहस्तश् च रक्तपिङ्गललोचनः
क्वचिच्च हसते रौद्रं क्वचिद्गायति विस्मितः ॥
1.31.m: holding a burning brand in His hand, with red and tawny eyes. / Somewhere He laughs dreadfully, somewhere He sings in wonder;

1.31.s:
kvacinnṛtyati śṛṅgāraṃ kvacidrauti muhurmuhuḥ
āśrame hyaṭate bhaikṣyaṃ yācate ca punaḥ punaḥ //
1.31.d:
क्वचिन्नृत्यति शृङ्गारं क्वचिद्रौति मुहुर्मुहुः
आश्रमे ह्यटते भैक्ष्यं याचते च पुनः पुनः ॥
1.31.m: somewhere He dances erotically, somewhere He wails again and again; / He wanders in the hermitage and begs repeatedly for alms.

1.31.s:
māyāṃ kṛtvā tathārūpāṃ devastadvanam āgataḥ
tataste munayaḥ sarve tuṣṭuvuś ca samāhitāḥ //
1.31.d:
मायां कृत्वा तथारूपां देवस्तद्वनम् आगतः
ततस्ते मुनयः सर्वे तुष्टुवुश् च समाहिताः ॥
1.31.m: Having assumed such a form by His māyā, the God came to that forest. / Then all those sages, with concentrated minds, praised Him,

1.31.s:
adbhir vividhamālyaiś ca dhūpairgandhaistathaiva ca
sapatnīkā mahābhāgāḥ saputrāḥ saparicchadāḥ //
1.31.d:
अद्भिर् विविधमाल्यैश् च धूपैर्गन्धैस्तथैव च
सपत्नीका महाभागाः सपुत्राः सपरिच्छदाः ॥
1.31.m: with water and various garlands, and likewise with incenses and perfumes, / those fortunate ones along with their wives, sons, and belongings.

1.31.s:
munayaste tathā vāgbhir īśvaraṃ cedam abruvan
ajñānāddevadeveśa yadasmābhir anuṣṭhitam //
1.31.d:
मुनयस्ते तथा वाग्भिर् ईश्वरं चेदम् अब्रुवन्
अज्ञानाद्देवदेवेश यदस्माभिर् अनुष्ठितम् ॥
1.31.m: Those sages spoke thus to the Lord with words: / “Whatever has been done by us out of ignorance, O God of the gods,

1.31.s:
karmaṇā manasā vācā tatsarvaṃ kṣantumarhasi
caritāni vicitrāṇi guhyāni gahanāni ca //
1.31.d:
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा तत्सर्वं क्षन्तुमर्हसि
चरितानि विचित्राणि गुह्यानि गहनानि च ॥
1.31.m: in deed, thought, or speech—you ought to forgive all that. / Your deeds are marvelous, secret, and unfathomable;

1.31.s:
brahmādīnāṃ ca devānāṃ durvijñeyāni te hara
agatiṃ te na jānīmo gatiṃ naiva ca naiva ca //
1.31.d:
ब्रह्मादीनां च देवानां दुर्विज्ञेयानि ते हर
अगतिं ते न जानीमो गतिं नैव च नैव च ॥
1.31.m: they are hard to comprehend even for the gods beginning with Brahmā, O Hara! / We do not know Your origin, nor indeed Your course at all.

1.31.s:
viśveśvara mahādeva yo 'si so 'si namo 'stu te
stuvanti tvāṃ mahātmāno devadevaṃ maheśvaram //
1.31.d:
विश्वेश्वर महादेव यो ऽसि सो ऽसि नमो ऽस्तु ते
स्तुवन्ति त्वां महात्मानो देवदेवं महेश्वरम् ॥
1.31.m: O Lord of the universe, Mahādeva, whoever You are, homage be to You! / The great-souled ones praise You, the God of gods, Maheśvara.

1.31.s:
namo bhavāya bhavyāya bhāvanāyodbhavāya ca
anantabalavīryāya bhūtānāṃ pataye namaḥ //
1.31.d:
नमो भवाय भव्याय भावनायोद्भवाय च
अनन्तबलवीर्याय भूतानां पतये नमः ॥
1.31.m: Homage to Bhava, to the auspicious, to the creator and the source of being; / homage to the Lord of beings, possessed of endless strength and valor.

1.31.s:
saṃhartre ca piśaṅgāya avyayāya vyayāya ca
gaṅgāsaliladhārāya ādhārāya guṇātmane //
1.31.d:
संहर्त्रे च पिशङ्गाय अव्ययाय व्ययाय च
गङ्गासलिलधाराय आधाराय गुणात्मने ॥
1.31.m: To the destroyer and the tawny one, to the imperishable and the perishable, / to the bearer of the waters of the Gaṅgā, to the support, whose self is the guṇas.

1.31.s:
tryaṃbakāya trinetrāya triśūlavaradhāriṇe
kandarpāya hutāśāya namo 'stu paramātmane //
1.31.d:
त्र्यंबकाय त्रिनेत्राय त्रिशूलवरधारिणे
कन्दर्पाय हुताशाय नमो ऽस्तु परमात्मने ॥
1.31.m: To Tryambaka, to the three-eyed one, to the bearer of the excellent trident, / to the god of love, to the fire, homage be to the Supreme Self.

1.31.s:
śaṅkarāya vṛṣāṅkāya gaṇānāṃ pataye namaḥ
daṇḍahastāya kālāya pāśahastāya vai namaḥ //
1.31.d:
शङ्कराय वृषाङ्काय गणानां पतये नमः
दण्डहस्ताय कालाय पाशहस्ताय वै नमः ॥
1.31.m: To Śaṅkara, whose banner is the bull, homage to the lord of the gaṇas; / to the staff-handed one, to Time, homage indeed to the noose-handed one.

1.31.s:
vedamantrapradhānāya śatajihvāya vai namaḥ
bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca yat //
1.31.d:
वेदमन्त्रप्रधानाय शतजिह्वाय वै नमः
भूतं भव्यं भविष्यं च स्थावरं जङ्गमं च यत् ॥
1.31.m: To the chief of Vedic mantras, homage indeed to the hundred-tongued one. / Whatever was, is, and will be, stationary and moving,

1.31.s:
tava dehātsamutpannaṃ deva sarvamidaṃ jagat
pāsi haṃsi ca bhadraṃ te prasīda bhagavaṃstataḥ //
1.31.d:
तव देहात्समुत्पन्नं देव सर्वमिदं जगत्
पासि हंसि च भद्रं ते प्रसीद भगवंस्ततः ॥
1.31.m: all this universe has arisen from Your body, O God! / You protect and You destroy; hail to You, be pleased, therefore, O Blessed One!

1.31.s:
ajñānādyadi vijñānād yat kiṃcit kurute naraḥ
tatsarvaṃ bhagavāneva kurute yogamāyayā //
1.31.d:
अज्ञानाद्यदि विज्ञानाद् यत् किंचित् कुरुते नरः
तत्सर्वं भगवानेव कुरुते योगमायया ॥
1.31.m: Whether out of ignorance or out of knowledge, whatever a man does, / it is the Blessed One alone who does all that by His yoga-māyā.”

1.31.s:
evaṃ stutvā tu munayaḥ prahṛṣṭairantarātmabhiḥ
yācanta tapasā yuktāḥ paśyāmastvāṃ yathāpurā //
1.31.d:
एवं स्तुत्वा तु मुनयः प्रहृष्टैरन्तरात्मभिः
याचन्त तपसा युक्ताः पश्यामस्त्वां यथापुरा ॥
1.31.m: Having thus praised Him with delighted inner selves, / the sages, endowed with asceticism, begged: “May we see You as You were before.”

1.31.s:
tato devaḥ prasannātmā svamevāsthāya śaṅkaraḥ
rūpaṃ tryakṣaṃ ca saṃdraṣṭuṃ divyaṃ cakṣuradātprabhuḥ //
1.31.d:
ततो देवः प्रसन्नात्मा स्वमेवास्थाय शङ्करः
रूपं त्र्यक्षं च संद्रष्टुं दिव्यं चक्षुरदात्प्रभुः ॥
1.31.m: Then the God, Śaṅkara, His mind pleased, assuming His own / three-eyed form, the Lord granted them divine vision in order to behold Him.

1.31.s:
labdhadṛṣṭyā tayā dṛṣṭvā devadevaṃ triyaṃbakam
punastuṣṭuvurīśānaṃ devadāruvanaukasaḥ //
1.31.d:
लब्धदृष्ट्या तया दृष्ट्वा देवदेवं त्रियंबकम्
पुनस्तुष्टुवुरीशानं देवदारुवनौकसः ॥
1.31.m: Having seen the God of gods, Tryambaka, with that vision obtained, / the dwellers of the Devadāru forest praised Īśāna once again.

1.32.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
namo digvāsase nityaṃ kṛtāntāya triśūline
vikaṭāya karālāya karālavadanāya ca //
1.32.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
नमो दिग्वाससे नित्यं कृतान्ताय त्रिशूलिने
विकटाय करालाय करालवदनाय च ॥
1.32.m: The sages said: / “Homage constantly to the sky-clad one, to the end-maker, to the trident-bearer, / to the monstrous, to the terrifying, and to the one with a terrifying face.

1.32.s:
arūpāya surūpāya viśvarūpāya te namaḥ
kaṭaṅkaṭāya rudrāya svāhākārāya vai namaḥ //
1.32.d:
अरूपाय सुरूपाय विश्वरूपाय ते नमः
कटङ्कटाय रुद्राय स्वाहाकाराय वै नमः ॥
1.32.m: To the formless, to the beautiful-formed, homage to You whose form is the universe; / to Kaṭaṅkaṭa, to Rudra, homage indeed to the exclamation Svāhā.

1.32.s:
sarvapraṇatadehāya svayaṃ ca praṇatātmane
nityaṃ nīlaśikhaṇḍāya śrīkaṇṭhāya namonamaḥ //
1.32.d:
सर्वप्रणतदेहाय स्वयं च प्रणतात्मने
नित्यं नीलशिखण्डाय श्रीकण्ठाय नमोनमः ॥
1.32.m: To the one before whom all bodies bow, and who Himself bows to the Self, / to the one who always has a dark crest, homage, homage to Śrīkaṇṭha.

1.32.s:
nīlakaṇṭhāya devāya citābhasmāṅgadhāriṇe
tvaṃ brahmā sarvadevānāṃ rudrāṇāṃ nīlalohitaḥ //
1.32.d:
नीलकण्ठाय देवाय चिताभस्माङ्गधारिणे
त्वं ब्रह्मा सर्वदेवानां रुद्राणां नीललोहितः ॥
1.32.m: To the blue-throated God, to the one who wears funeral ash on His limbs. / You are Brahmā among all gods, Nīlalohita among the Rudras,

1.32.s:
ātmā ca sarvabhūtānāṃ sāṃkhyaiḥ puruṣa ucyate
parvatānāṃ mahāmerur nakṣatrāṇāṃ ca candramāḥ //
1.32.d:
आत्मा च सर्वभूतानां सांख्यैः पुरुष उच्यते
पर्वतानां महामेरुर् नक्षत्राणां च चन्द्रमाः ॥
1.32.m: and the Self of all beings; You are called Puruṣa by the Sāṃkhyas. / Of mountains You are the great Meru, and of constellations the moon;

1.32.s:
ṛṣīṇāṃ ca vasiṣṭhas tvaṃ devānāṃ vāsavas tathā
oṅkāraḥ sarvavedānāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sāma ca sāmasu //
1.32.d:
ऋषीणां च वसिष्ठस् त्वं देवानां वासवस् तथा
ओङ्कारः सर्ववेदानां श्रेष्ठं साम च सामसु ॥
1.32.m: and of sages You are Vasiṣṭha, and among the gods, Vāsava; / the syllable Oṃ among all Vedas, and the best Sāman among Sāmans;

1.32.s:
āraṇyānāṃ paśūnāṃ ca siṃhastvaṃ parameśvaraḥ
grāmyāṇāmṛṣabhaścāsi bhagavāṃllokapūjitaḥ //
1.32.d:
आरण्यानां पशूनां च सिंहस्त्वं परमेश्वरः
ग्राम्याणामृषभश्चासि भगवांल्लोकपूजितः ॥
1.32.m: and of wild beasts You are the lion, O Supreme Lord; / and of domestic ones You are the bull, the Blessed One revered by the world.

1.32.s:
sarvathā vartamāno 'pi yo yo bhāvo bhaviṣyati
tvāmeva tatra paśyāmo brahmaṇā kathitaṃ tathā //
1.32.d:
सर्वथा वर्तमानो ऽपि यो यो भावो भविष्यति
त्वामेव तत्र पश्यामो ब्रह्मणा कथितं तथा ॥
1.32.m: In whatever state one exists in every way, whatever being shall arise, / You alone we behold there, as was stated by Brahmā.

1.32.s:
kāmaḥ krodhaś ca lobhaś ca viṣādo mada eva ca
etad icchāmahe boddhuṃ prasīda parameśvara //
1.32.d:
कामः क्रोधश् च लोभश् च विषादो मद एव च
एतद् इच्छामहे बोद्धुं प्रसीद परमेश्वर ॥
1.32.m: Desire, anger, greed, despondency, and intoxication— / this we wish to understand; be pleased, O Supreme Lord!

1.32.s:
mahāsaṃharaṇe prāpte tvayā deva kṛtātmanā
karaṃ lalāṭe saṃvidhya vahnirutpāditastvayā //
1.32.d:
महासंहरणे प्राप्ते त्वया देव कृतात्मना
करं ललाटे संविध्य वह्निरुत्पादितस्त्वया ॥
1.32.m: When the great dissolution arrived, by You, O God of disciplined nature, / placing Your hand on Your forehead, fire was produced by You.

1.32.s:
tenāgninā tadā lokā arcirbhiḥ sarvato vṛtāḥ
tasmādagnisamā hyete bahavo vikṛtāgnayaḥ //
1.32.d:
तेनाग्निना तदा लोका अर्चिर्भिः सर्वतो वृताः
तस्मादग्निसमा ह्येते बहवो विकृताग्नयः ॥
1.32.m: By that fire then the worlds were surrounded on all sides with flames. / Therefore, these multiple unnatural fires are indeed like fire:

1.32.s:
kāmaḥ krodhaś ca lobhaś ca moho dambha upadravaḥ
yāni cānyāni bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca //
1.32.d:
कामः क्रोधश् च लोभश् च मोहो दम्भ उपद्रवः
यानि चान्यानि भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च ॥
1.32.m: desire, anger, greed, delusion, hypocrisy, and distress; / and whatever other beings there are, stationary and moving,

1.32.s:
dahyante prāṇinaste tu tvatsamutthena vahninā
asmākaṃ dahyamānānāṃ trātā bhava sureśvara //
1.32.d:
दह्यन्ते प्राणिनस्ते तु त्वत्समुत्थेन वह्निना
अस्माकं दह्यमानानां त्राता भव सुरेश्वर ॥
1.32.m: those creatures are burned by the fire that has arisen from You. / Be the protector of us who are being burned, O Lord of gods!

1.32.s:
tvaṃ ca lokahitārthāya bhūtāni pariṣiñcasi
maheśvara mahābhāga prabho śubhanirīkṣaka //
1.32.d:
त्वं च लोकहितार्थाय भूतानि परिषिञ्चसि
महेश्वर महाभाग प्रभो शुभनिरीक्षक ॥
1.32.m: And for the welfare of the world, You sprinkle the beings, / O Maheśvara of great fortune, O Lord who beholds what is auspicious!

1.32.s:
ājñāpaya vayaṃ nātha kartāro vacanaṃ tava
bhūtakoṭisahasreṣu rūpakoṭiśateṣu ca //
1.32.d:
आज्ञापय वयं नाथ कर्तारो वचनं तव
भूतकोटिसहस्रेषु रूपकोटिशतेषु च ॥
1.32.m: Command [us], O Lord; we shall carry out Your word! / Among thousands of crores of beings, and in hundreds of crores of forms,

1.32.s: antaṃ gantuṃ na śaktāḥ sma devadeva namo 'stu te //
1.32.d: अन्तं गन्तुं न शक्ताः स्म देवदेव नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
1.32.m: we are not able to reach the end; O God of gods, homage be to You!”

1.33.s:
nandyuvāca
tatastutoṣa bhagavān anugṛhya maheśvaraḥ
stutiṃ śrutvā stutasteṣām idaṃ vacanamabravīt //
1.33.d:
नन्द्युवाच
ततस्तुतोष भगवान् अनुगृह्य महेश्वरः
स्तुतिं श्रुत्वा स्तुतस्तेषाम् इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
1.33.m: Nandin said: / Then the Blessed One, Maheśvara, was pleased; showing favor / upon hearing the praise of those by whom He was praised, He spoke this word:

1.33.s:
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi yuṣmābhiḥ kīrtitaṃ stavam
śrāvayedvā dvijānvipro gāṇapatyamavāpnuyāt //
1.33.d:
यः पठेच्छृणुयाद्वापि युष्माभिः कीर्तितं स्तवम्
श्रावयेद्वा द्विजान्विप्रो गाणपत्यमवाप्नुयात् ॥
1.33.m:
Whoever reads or hears the hymn recited by you,
or a twice-born who recites it to the twice-born, shall attain the state of a gana-leader.

1.33.s:
vakṣyāmi vo hitaṃ puṇyaṃ bhaktānāṃ munipuṅgavāḥ
strīliṅgamakhilaṃ devī prakṛtirmama dehajā //
1.33.d:
वक्ष्यामि वो हितं पुण्यं भक्तानां मुनिपुङ्गवाः
स्त्रीलिङ्गमखिलं देवी प्रकृतिर्मम देहजा ॥
1.33.m:
I will tell you, best of sages, what is beneficial and meritorious for devotees:
every feminine gender is the Goddess, the Prakṛti born of my body;

1.33.s:
puṃlliṅgaṃ puruṣo viprā mama dehasamudbhavaḥ
ubhābhyāmeva vai sṛṣṭir mama viprā na saṃśayaḥ //
1.33.d:
पुंल्लिङ्गं पुरुषो विप्रा मम देहसमुद्भवः
उभाभ्यामेव वै सृष्टिर् मम विप्रा न संशयः ॥
1.33.m:
the masculine gender, O twice-born ones, is the Puruṣa, arisen from my body.
Indeed, from both of these is creation, O twice-born ones; of this there is no doubt.

1.33.s:
na nindedyatinaṃ tasmād digvāsasamanuttamam
bālonmattaviceṣṭaṃ tu matparaṃ brahmavādinam //
1.33.d:
न निन्देद्यतिनं तस्माद् दिग्वाससमनुत्तमम्
बालोन्मत्तविचेष्टं तु मत्परं ब्रह्मवादिनम् ॥
1.33.m:
Therefore, one should not revile the supreme ascetic who is clad in the quarters (naked),
acting like a child or a madman, devoted to me, an expounder of Brahman.

1.33.s:
ye hi māṃ bhasmaniratā bhasmanā dagdhakilbiṣāḥ
yathoktakāriṇo dāntā viprā dhyānaparāyaṇāḥ //
1.33.d:
ये हि मां भस्मनिरता भस्मना दग्धकिल्बिषाः
यथोक्तकारिणो दान्ता विप्रा ध्यानपरायणाः ॥
1.33.m:
For those who are devoted to sacred ash, their sins burned away by sacred ash,
who act as prescribed, self-controlled, twice-born ones intent on meditation,

1.33.s:
mahādevaparā nityaṃ caranto hyūrdhvaretasaḥ
arcayanti mahādevaṃ vāṅmanaḥkāyasaṃyatāḥ //
1.33.d:
महादेवपरा नित्यं चरन्तो ह्यूर्ध्वरेतसः
अर्चयन्ति महादेवं वाङ्मनःकायसंयताः ॥
1.33.m:
ever devoted to Mahādeva, wandering as celibates of drawn-up seed,
who worship Mahādeva with speech, mind, and body restrained—

1.33.s:
rudralokamanuprāpya na nivartanti te punaḥ
tasmādetadvrataṃ divyam avyaktaṃ vyaktaliṅginaḥ //
1.33.d:
रुद्रलोकमनुप्राप्य न निवर्तन्ति ते पुनः
तस्मादेतद्व्रतं दिव्यम् अव्यक्तं व्यक्तलिङ्गिनः ॥
1.33.m:
they reach the world of Rudra and do not return again.
Therefore this divine observance is unmanifest for those with manifest marks;

1.33.s:
bhasmavratāś ca muṇḍāś ca vratino viśvarūpiṇaḥ
na tānparivadedvidvān na caitānnābhilaṅghayet //
1.33.d:
भस्मव्रताश् च मुण्डाश् च व्रतिनो विश्वरूपिणः
न तान्परिवदेद्विद्वान् न चैतान्नाभिलङ्घयेत् ॥
1.33.m:
observant of the sacred ash, shaven-headed, practitioners of vows, assuming all forms—
a wise man should not speak ill of them, nor should he ever transgress them,

1.33.s:
na hasennāpriyaṃ brūyād amutreha hitārthavān
yastānnindati mūḍhātmā mahādevaṃ sa nindati //
1.33.d:
न हसेन्नाप्रियं ब्रूयाद् अमुत्रेह हितार्थवान्
यस्तान्निन्दति मूढात्मा महादेवं स निन्दति ॥
1.33.m:
nor laugh at them, nor speak unpleasant words to them, if he desires what is beneficial here and hereafter.
The foolish person who reviles them reviles Mahādeva.

1.33.s:
yas tvetān pūjayen nityaṃ sa pūjayati śaṅkaram
evameṣa mahādevo lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā //
1.33.d:
यस् त्वेतान् पूजयेन् नित्यं स पूजयति शङ्करम्
एवमेष महादेवो लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥
1.33.m:
And he who constantly worships them worships Śaṅkara.
Thus this Mahādeva, out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds,

1.33.s:
yuge yuge mahāyogī krīḍate bhasmaguṇṭhitaḥ
evaṃ carata bhadraṃ vas tataḥ siddhimavāpsyatha //
1.33.d:
युगे युगे महायोगी क्रीडते भस्मगुण्ठितः
एवं चरत भद्रं वस् ततः सिद्धिमवाप्स्यथ ॥
1.33.m:
as the great yogin smeared with sacred ash, plays in yuga after yuga.
Conduct yourselves thus; may good betide you; then you shall attain perfection."

1.33.s:
atulamiha mahābhayapraṇāśahetuṃ śivakathitaṃ paramaṃ padaṃ viditvā
vyapagatabhavalobhamohacittāḥ praṇipatitāḥ sahasā śirobhir ugram //
1.33.d:
अतुलमिह महाभयप्रणाशहेतुं शिवकथितं परमं पदं विदित्वा
व्यपगतभवलोभमोहचित्ताः प्रणिपतिताः सहसा शिरोभिर् उग्रम् ॥
1.33.m:
Having known the peerless supreme state proclaimed by Śiva, which causes the destruction of great fear here,
with their minds freed from worldly existence, greed, and delusion, they quickly bowed their heads to the terrible Ugra.

1.33.s:
tataḥ pramuditā viprāḥ śrutvaivaṃ kathitaṃ tadā
gandhodakaiḥ suśuddhaiś ca kuśapuṣpavimiśritaiḥ //
1.33.d:
ततः प्रमुदिता विप्राः श्रुत्वैवं कथितं तदा
गन्धोदकैः सुशुद्धैश् च कुशपुष्पविमिश्रितैः ॥
1.33.m:
Then the twice-born ones rejoiced, having thus heard what was spoken then.
With very pure fragrant waters mixed with kuśa grass and flowers,

1.33.s:
snāpayanti mahākumbhair adbhir eva maheśvaram
gāyanti vividhairguhyair huṃkāraiścāpi susvaraiḥ //
1.33.d:
स्नापयन्ति महाकुम्भैर् अद्भिर् एव महेश्वरम्
गायन्ति विविधैर्गुह्यैर् हुंकारैश्चापि सुस्वरैः ॥
1.33.m:
they bathed Maheśvara with great water-jars filled with water;
and they sang with various esoteric syllables of 'huṃ' and melodious tones:

1.33.s:
namo devādhidevāya mahādevāya vai namaḥ
ardhanārīśarīrāya sāṃkhyayogapravartine //
1.33.d:
नमो देवाधिदेवाय महादेवाय वै नमः
अर्धनारीशरीराय सांख्ययोगप्रवर्तिने ॥
1.33.m:
"Homage to the supreme god of gods, homage indeed to Mahādeva,
whose body is half woman, who set in motion Sāṃkhya and yoga,

1.33.s:
meghavāhanakṛṣṇāya gajacarmanivāsine
kṛṣṇājinottarīyāya vyālayajñopavītine //
1.33.d:
मेघवाहनकृष्णाय गजचर्मनिवासिने
कृष्णाजिनोत्तरीयाय व्यालयज्ञोपवीतिने ॥
1.33.m:
who has clouds for a vehicle, who is dark, who wears an elephant hide,
who has a black antilope skin for an upper garment, who wears a serpent for a sacred thread,

1.33.s:
suracitasuvicitrakuṇḍalāya suracitamālyavibhūṣaṇāya tubhyam
mṛgapativaracarmavāsase ca prathitayaśase namo 'stu śaṅkarāya //
1.33.d:
सुरचितसुविचित्रकुण्डलाय सुरचितमाल्यविभूषणाय तुभ्यम्
मृगपतिवरचर्मवाससे च प्रथितयशसे नमो ऽस्तु शङ्कराय ॥
1.33.m:
who has well-fashioned, marvelous earrings, who is adorned with well-crafted garlands,
and who is clad in the excellent skin of the lord of beasts (the lion/tiger), of renowned fame—homage be to Śaṅkara!"

1.33.s:
tatas tān sa munīn prītaḥ pratyuvāca maheśvaraḥ
prīto 'smi tapasā yuṣmān varaṃ vṛṇuta suvratāḥ //
1.33.d:
ततस् तान् स मुनीन् प्रीतः प्रत्युवाच महेश्वरः
प्रीतो ऽस्मि तपसा युष्मान् वरं वृणुत सुव्रताः ॥
1.33.m:
Then Maheśvara, pleased, replied to those sages:
"I am pleased with your asceticism; choose a boon, O you of noble vows!"

1.33.s:
tataste munayaḥ sarve praṇipatya maheśvaram
bhṛgvaṅgirā vasiṣṭhaś ca viśvāmitrastathaiva ca //
1.33.d:
ततस्ते मुनयः सर्वे प्रणिपत्य महेश्वरम्
भृग्वङ्गिरा वसिष्ठश् च विश्वामित्रस्तथैव च ॥
1.33.m:
Then all those sages, having bowed to Maheśvara—
Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Vasiṣṭha, and likewise Viśvāmitra,

1.33.s:
gautamo 'triḥ sukeśaś ca pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ
marīciḥ kaśyapaḥ kaṇvaḥ saṃvartaś ca mahātapāḥ //
1.33.d:
गौतमो ऽत्रिः सुकेशश् च पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः
मरीचिः कश्यपः कण्वः संवर्तश् च महातपाः ॥
1.33.m:
Gautama, Atri, Sukeśa, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu,
Marīci, Kaśyapa, Kaṇva, and Saṃvarta of great asceticism—

1.33.s:
te praṇamya mahādevam idaṃ vacanamabruvan
bhasmasnānaṃ ca nagnatvaṃ vāmatvaṃ pratilomatā //
1.33.d:
ते प्रणम्य महादेवम् इदं वचनमब्रुवन्
भस्मस्नानं च नग्नत्वं वामत्वं प्रतिलोमता ॥
1.33.m:
having bowed to Mahādeva, they spoke these words:
"Bathing in sacred ash, nakedness, contrariety, and going against the grain,

1.33.s:
sevyāsevyatvamevaṃ ca hy etadicchāma veditum
tatasteṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā bhagavānparameśvaraḥ //
1.33.d:
सेव्यासेव्यत्वमेवं च ह्य् एतदिच्छाम वेदितुम्
ततस्तेषां वचः श्रुत्वा भगवान्परमेश्वरः ॥
1.33.m:
and likewise what is to be served and what is not to be served: we wish to know this."
Then, having heard their words, the Lord, the supreme sovereign,

1.33.s: sasmitaṃ prāha samprekṣya sarvānmunivarāṃstadā //
1.33.d: सस्मितं प्राह सम्प्रेक्ष्य सर्वान्मुनिवरांस्तदा ॥
1.33.m: looked upon all the best sages and spoke with a smile:

1.34.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca
etadvaḥ sampravakṣyāmi kathā sarvasvamadya vai
agnirhyahaṃ somakartā somaścāgnimupāśritaḥ //
1.34.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
एतद्वः सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि कथा सर्वस्वमद्य वै
अग्निर्ह्यहं सोमकर्ता सोमश्चाग्निमुपाश्रितः ॥
1.34.m:
The Blessed Lord said:
"I will proclaim this to you today, the quintessence of the sacred discourse.
For I am Agni, the maker of Soma, and Soma is dependent on Agni.

1.34.s:
kṛtametadvahatyagnir bhūyo lokasamāśrayāt
asakṛttvagninā dagdhaṃ jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam //
1.34.d:
कृतमेतद्वहत्यग्निर् भूयो लोकसमाश्रयात्
असकृत्त्वग्निना दग्धं जगत् स्थावरजङ्गमम् ॥
1.34.m:
Agni carries this accomplished [offering] repeatedly because it is the refuge of the worlds.
For the universe, both stationary and moving, has been repeatedly consumed by fire,

1.34.s:
bhasmasādvihitaṃ sarvaṃ pavitramidamuttamam
bhasmanā vīryamāsthāya bhūtāni pariṣiñcati //
1.34.d:
भस्मसाद्विहितं सर्वं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम्
भस्मना वीर्यमास्थाय भूतानि परिषिञ्चति ॥
1.34.m:
and turned entirely into sacred ash; this is the highest purifier.
Having infused his virile potency into the sacred ash, he sprinkles the beings.

1.34.s:
agnikāryaṃ ca yaḥ kṛtvā kariṣyati triyāyuṣam
bhasmanā mama vīryeṇa mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ //
1.34.d:
अग्निकार्यं च यः कृत्वा करिष्यति त्रियायुषम्
भस्मना मम वीर्येण मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः ॥
1.34.m:
Whoever, having performed the fire ritual, will make the three marks (triyāyuṣa)
with sacred ash, which is my virile potency, is freed from all sins.

1.34.s:
bhāsata ityeva yadbhasma śubhaṃ bhāvayate ca yat
bhakṣaṇāt sarvapāpānāṃ bhasmeti parikīrtitam //
1.34.d:
भासत इत्येव यद्भस्म शुभं भावयते च यत्
भक्षणात् सर्वपापानां भस्मेति परिकीर्तितम् ॥
1.34.m:
Because it shines (bhāsate), it is called bhasman, and because it causes auspiciousness to arise (bhāvayate);
and because it devours (bhakṣaṇāt) all sins, it is proclaimed as bhasman.

1.34.s:
ūṣmapāḥ pitaro jñeyā devā vai somasaṃbhavāḥ
agnīṣomātmakaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam //
1.34.d:
ऊष्मपाः पितरो ज्ञेया देवा वै सोमसंभवाः
अग्नीषोमात्मकं सर्वं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् ॥
1.34.m:
The ancestors are known to be drinkers of steam; the gods are born of Soma.
The entire universe, both stationary and moving, has the nature of Agni and Soma.

1.34.s:
ahamagnirmahātejāḥ somaścaiṣā mahāṃbikā
ahamagniś ca somaś ca prakṛtyā puruṣaḥ svayam //
1.34.d:
अहमग्निर्महातेजाः सोमश्चैषा महांबिका
अहमग्निश् च सोमश् च प्रकृत्या पुरुषः स्वयम् ॥
1.34.m:
I am Agni of great splendour, and this great Mother is Soma.
I myself am both Agni and Soma, and by nature the Puruṣa.

1.34.s:
tasmādbhasma mahābhāgā madvīryamiti cocyate
svavīryaṃ vapuṣā caiva dhārayāmīti vai sthitiḥ //
1.34.d:
तस्माद्भस्म महाभागा मद्वीर्यमिति चोच्यते
स्ववीर्यं वपुषा चैव धारयामीति वै स्थितिः ॥
1.34.m:
Therefore, O fortunate ones, sacred ash is called my virile potency;
and the established rule is that I bear my own virile potency with my body.

1.34.s:
tadāprabhṛti lokeṣu rakṣārthamaśubheṣu ca
bhasmanā kriyate rakṣā sūtikānāṃ gṛheṣu ca //
1.34.d:
तदाप्रभृति लोकेषु रक्षार्थमशुभेषु च
भस्मना क्रियते रक्षा सूतिकानां गृहेषु च ॥
1.34.m:
Ever since then in the worlds, for protection and amidst inauspicious things,
protection is made with sacred ash, and in the rooms of women in childbirth.

1.34.s:
bhasmasnānaviśuddhātmā jitakrodho jitendriyaḥ
matsamīpaṃ samāgamya na bhūyo vinivartate //
1.34.d:
भस्मस्नानविशुद्धात्मा जितक्रोधो जितेन्द्रियः
मत्समीपं समागम्य न भूयो विनिवर्तते ॥
1.34.m:
Purified in soul by bathing in sacred ash, with anger conquered and senses subdued,
having approached my presence, one does not return again.

1.34.s:
vrataṃ pāśupataṃ yogaṃ kāpilaṃ caiva nirmitam
pūrvaṃ pāśupataṃ hyetan nirmitaṃ tadanuttamam //
1.34.d:
व्रतं पाशुपतं योगं कापिलं चैव निर्मितम्
पूर्वं पाशुपतं ह्येतन् निर्मितं तदनुत्तमम् ॥
1.34.m:
The Pāśupata observance, yoga, and the system of Kapila were instituted [by me].
For this peerless Pāśupata was instituted first;

1.34.s:
śeṣāścāśramiṇaḥ sarve paścātsṛṣṭāḥ svayaṃbhuvā
sṛṣṭireṣā mayā sṛṣṭā lajjāmohabhayātmikā //
1.34.d:
शेषाश्चाश्रमिणः सर्वे पश्चात्सृष्टाः स्वयंभुवा
सृष्टिरेषा मया सृष्टा लज्जामोहभयात्मिका ॥
1.34.m:
all the other life-stages were created afterward by the Self-born.
This creation created by me has the nature of shame, delusion, and fear.

1.34.s:
nagnā eva hi jāyante devatā munayas tathā
ye cānye mānavā loke sarve jāyantyavāsasaḥ //
1.34.d:
नग्ना एव हि जायन्ते देवता मुनयस् तथा
ये चान्ये मानवा लोके सर्वे जायन्त्यवाससः ॥
1.34.m:
For gods are born naked, and likewise sages;
and whatever other mortals there are in the world, all are born unclothed.

1.34.s:
indriyairajitairnagno dukūlenāpi saṃvṛtaḥ
taireva saṃvṛtairgupto na vastraṃ kāraṇaṃ smṛtam //
1.34.d:
इन्द्रियैरजितैर्नग्नो दुकूलेनापि संवृतः
तैरेव संवृतैर्गुप्तो न वस्त्रं कारणं स्मृतम् ॥
1.34.m:
One with unsubdued senses is naked even when covered with fine silk;
one whose senses are concealed and guarded by them alone—clothing is not considered the cause.

1.34.s:
kṣamā dhṛtirahiṃsā ca vairāgyaṃ caiva sarvaśaḥ
tulyau mānāvamānau ca tadāvaraṇamuttamam //
1.34.d:
क्षमा धृतिरहिंसा च वैराग्यं चैव सर्वशः
तुल्यौ मानावमानौ च तदावरणमुत्तमम् ॥
1.34.m:
Forbearance, firmness, non-violence, and total dispassion in every respect,
and honor and dishonor viewed as equal: that is the supreme covering.

1.34.s:
bhasmasnānena digdhāṅgo dhyāyate manasā bhavam
yadyakāryasahasrāṇi kṛtvā yaḥ snāti bhasmanā //
1.34.d:
भस्मस्नानेन दिग्धाङ्गो ध्यायते मनसा भवम्
यद्यकार्यसहस्राणि कृत्वा यः स्नाति भस्मना ॥
1.34.m:
One whose limbs are smeared by bathing in sacred ash meditates with his mind on Bhava.
Even if one has committed thousands of improper deeds, he who bathes in sacred ash—

1.34.s:
tatsarvaṃ dahate bhasma yathāgnistejasā vanam
tasmād yatnaparo bhūtvā trikālamapi yaḥ sadā //
1.34.d:
तत्सर्वं दहते भस्म यथाग्निस्तेजसा वनम्
तस्माद् यत्नपरो भूत्वा त्रिकालमपि यः सदा ॥
1.34.m:
the sacred ash burns all of that away, just as fire burns a forest with its splendour.
Therefore, having become diligent, he who always bathes with sacred ash

1.34.s:
bhasmanā kurute snānaṃ gāṇapatyaṃ sa gacchati
samāhṛtya kratūn sarvān gṛhītvā vratamuttamam //
1.34.d:
भस्मना कुरुते स्नानं गाणपत्यं स गच्छति
समाहृत्य क्रतून् सर्वान् गृहीत्वा व्रतमुत्तमम् ॥
1.34.m:
at the three junctures of the day, attains the status of a gana-leader.
Collecting all sacrifices, undertaking the supreme observance,

1.34.s:
dhyāyanti ye mahādevaṃ līlāsadbhāvabhāvitāḥ
uttareṇāryapanthānaṃ te 'mṛtatvamavāpnuyuḥ //
1.34.d:
ध्यायन्ति ये महादेवं लीलासद्भावभाविताः
उत्तरेणार्यपन्थानं ते ऽमृतत्वमवाप्नुयुः ॥
1.34.m:
those who meditate on Mahādeva, filled with the reality of divine play,
shall attain immortality by the northern path of the noble.

1.34.s:
dakṣiṇena ca panthānaṃ ye śmaśānāni bhejire
aṇimā garimā caiva laghimā prāptireva ca //
1.34.d:
दक्षिणेन च पन्थानं ये श्मशानानि भेजिरे
अणिमा गरिमा चैव लघिमा प्राप्तिरेव च ॥
1.34.m:
And by the southern path, those who have resorted to cremation grounds
[attain] minuteness, heaviness, lightness, and acquisition,

1.34.s:
icchā kāmāvasāyitvaṃ tathā prākāmyameva ca
īkṣaṇena ca panthānaṃ ye śmaśānāni bhejire
aṇimā garimā caiva laghimā prāptireva ca //
1.34.d:
इच्छा कामावसायित्वं तथा प्राकाम्यमेव च
ईक्षणेन च पन्थानं ये श्मशानानि भेजिरे
अणिमा गरिमा चैव लघिमा प्राप्तिरेव च ॥
1.34.m:
will, dominion over desire, and irrepressible will—
and by the path of vision, those who have resorted to cremation grounds
[attain] minuteness, heaviness, lightness, and acquisition.

1.34.s:
indrādayas tathā devāḥ kāmikavratamāsthitāḥ
aiśvaryaṃ paramaṃ prāpya sarve prathitatejasaḥ //
1.34.d:
इन्द्रादयस् तथा देवाः कामिकव्रतमास्थिताः
ऐश्वर्यं परमं प्राप्य सर्वे प्रथिततेजसः ॥
1.34.m:
Likewise the gods headed by Indra, who undertook the observance of the desired goal,
having attained supreme sovereignty, are all of renowned splendour.

1.34.s:
vyapagatamadamohamuktarāgas tamorajodoṣavivarjitasvabhāvaḥ
paribhavamidamuttamaṃ viditvā paśupatiyogaparo bhavetsadaiva //
1.34.d:
व्यपगतमदमोहमुक्तरागस् तमोरजोदोषविवर्जितस्वभावः
परिभवमिदमुत्तमं विदित्वा पशुपतियोगपरो भवेत्सदैव ॥
1.34.m:
Free from intoxication and delusion, released from passion, with a nature devoid of the faults of tamas and rajas,
having realized this supreme transcendence, one should always be intent on the yoga of the Lord of Cattle.

1.34.s:
imaṃ pāśupataṃ dhyāyan sarvapāpapraṇāśanam
yaḥ paṭhecca śucirbhūtvā śraddadhāno jitendriyaḥ //
1.34.d:
इमं पाशुपतं ध्यायन् सर्वपापप्रणाशनम्
यः पठेच्च शुचिर्भूत्वा श्रद्दधानो जितेन्द्रियः ॥
1.34.m:
Meditating on this Pāśupata [teaching] which destroys all sins,
whoever reads it, having become pure, faithful, and with subdued senses...

1.34.s:
sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā rudralokaṃ sa gacchati
te sarve munayaḥ śrutvā vasiṣṭhādyā dvijottamāḥ //
1.34.d:
सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा रुद्रलोकं स गच्छति
ते सर्वे मुनयः श्रुत्वा वसिष्ठाद्या द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
1.34.m: With his soul purified of all sins, he goes to the world of Rudra. / Having heard this, all those sages, Vasiṣṭha and the other best of brahmins,

1.34.s:
bhasmapāṇḍuradigdhāṅgā babhūvurvigataspṛhāḥ
rudralokāya kalpānte saṃsthitāḥ śivatejasā //
1.34.d:
भस्मपाण्डुरदिग्धाङ्गा बभूवुर्विगतस्पृहाः
