मन्त्रब्राह्मणविन्यासैः स्वरवर्णविपर्ययैः ॥
1.39.m: Then divisions are made by the sons of sages through delusions of vision, / through arrangements of mantras and brāhmaṇas, and inversions of accents and syllables.'

1.39.s:
saṃhitā ṛgyajuḥsāmnāṃ saṃhanyante manīṣibhiḥ
sāmānyā vaikṛtāścaiva draṣṭṛbhistaiḥ pṛthakpṛthak //
1.39.d:
संहिता ऋग्यजुःसाम्नां संहन्यन्ते मनीषिभिः
सामान्या वैकृताश्चैव द्रष्टृभिस्तैः पृथक्पृथक् ॥
1.39.m: The Saṃhitās of the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma Vedas were compiled by the wise; / the general and modified forms were arranged separately by those seers.

1.39.s:
brāhmaṇaṃ kalpasūtrāṇi mantrapravacanāni ca
anye tu prasthitāstānvai kecittānpratyavasthitāḥ //
1.39.d:
ब्राह्मणं कल्पसूत्राणि मन्त्रप्रवचनानि च
अन्ये तु प्रस्थितास्तान्वै केचित्तान्प्रत्यवस्थिताः ॥
1.39.m: The Brāhmaṇa, the Kalpasūtras, and the expositions of the mantras— / some scholars supported them, while others opposed them.

1.39.s:
itihāsapurāṇāni bhidyante kālagauravāt
brāhmaṃ pādmaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ ca śaivaṃ bhāgavataṃ tathā //
1.39.d:
इतिहासपुराणानि भिद्यन्ते कालगौरवात्
ब्राह्मं पाद्मं वैष्णवं च शैवं भागवतं तथा ॥
1.39.m: The Itihāsas and Purāṇas became divided through the weight of time: / the Brāhma, the Pādma, the Vaiṣṇava, the Śaiva, and likewise the Bhāgavata;

1.39.s:
bhaviṣyaṃ nāradīyaṃ ca mārkaṇḍeyamataḥ param
āgneyaṃ brahmavaivartaṃ laiṅgaṃ vārāhameva ca //
1.39.d:
भविष्यं नारदीयं च मार्कण्डेयमतः परम्
आग्नेयं ब्रह्मवैवर्तं लैङ्गं वाराहमेव च ॥
1.39.m: the Bhaviṣya, the Nāradīya, and next the Mārkaṇḍeya; / the Āgneya, the Brahmavaivarta, the Laiṅga, and also the Vārāha;

1.39.s:
vāmanākhyaṃ tataḥ kūrmaṃ mātsyaṃ gāruḍameva ca
skāndaṃ tathā ca brahmāṇḍaṃ teṣāṃ bhedaḥ prakathyate //
1.39.d:
वामनाख्यं ततः कूर्मं मात्स्यं गारुडमेव च
स्कान्दं तथा च ब्रह्माण्डं तेषां भेदः प्रकथ्यते ॥
1.39.m: then the one named Vāmana, the Kūrma, the Mātsya, and the Gāruḍa; / likewise the Skānda and the Brahmāṇḍa. Their division is recounted [as follows]:

1.39.s:
laiṅgam ekādaśavidhaṃ prabhinnaṃ dvāpare śubham
manvatriviṣṇuhārītayājñavalkyośano 'ṅgirāḥ //
1.39.d:
लैङ्गम् एकादशविधं प्रभिन्नं द्वापरे शुभम्
मन्वत्रिविष्णुहारीतयाज्ञवल्क्योशनो ऽङ्गिराः ॥
1.39.m: The auspicious Laiṅga was divided into eleven parts in Dvāpara. / Manu, Atri, Viṣṇu, Hārīta, Yājñavalkya, Uśanas, Aṅgiras,

1.39.s:
yamāpastambasaṃvartāḥ kātyāyanabṛhaspatī
parāśaravyāsaśaṅkhalikhitā dakṣagautamau //
1.39.d:
यमापस्तम्बसंवर्ताः कात्यायनबृहस्पती
पराशरव्यासशङ्खलिखिता दक्षगौतमौ ॥
1.39.m: Yama, Āpastamba, Saṃvarta, Kātyāyana, Bṛhaspati, / Parāśara, Vyāsa, Śaṅkha, Likhita, Dakṣa, Gautama,

1.39.s:
śātātapo vasiṣṭhaś ca evamādyaiḥ sahasraśaḥ
avṛṣṭirmaraṇaṃ caiva tathā vyādhyādyupadravāḥ //
1.39.d:
शातातपो वसिष्ठश् च एवमाद्यैः सहस्रशः
अवृष्टिर्मरणं चैव तथा व्याध्याद्युपद्रवाः ॥
1.39.m: Śātātapa, and Vasiṣṭha—through these and thousands of others, [smṛtis were taught]. / Drought, death, and afflictions such as diseases [arise];

1.39.s:
vāṅmanaḥkarmajair duḥkhair nirvedo jāyate tataḥ
nirvedājjāyate teṣāṃ duḥkhamokṣavicāraṇā //
1.39.d:
वाङ्मनःकर्मजैर् दुःखैर् निर्वेदो जायते ततः
निर्वेदाज्जायते तेषां दुःखमोक्षविचारणा ॥
1.39.m: then, from sorrows born of speech, mind, and action, world-weariness is born. / From world-weariness arises their inquiry into release from sorrow.

1.39.s:
vicāraṇācca vairāgyaṃ vairāgyāddoṣadarśanam
doṣāṇāṃ darśanāccaiva dvāpare jñānasaṃbhavaḥ //
1.39.d:
विचारणाच्च वैराग्यं वैराग्याद्दोषदर्शनम्
दोषाणां दर्शनाच्चैव द्वापरे ज्ञानसंभवः ॥
1.39.m: From inquiry comes detachment, from detachment the perception of defects, / and from the perception of defects, knowledge arises in the Dvāpara [yuga].

1.39.s:
eṣā rajastamoyuktā vṛttir vai dvāpare smṛtā
ādye kṛte tu dharmo 'sti sa tretāyāṃ pravartate //
1.39.d:
एषा रजस्तमोयुक्ता वृत्तिर् वै द्वापरे स्मृता
आद्ये कृते तु धर्मो ऽस्ति स त्रेतायां प्रवर्तते ॥
1.39.m: This way of life is remembered as endowed with rajas and tamas in Dvāpara. / In the first [yuga], Kṛta, dharma is present; it proceeds in Tretā;

1.39.s: dvāpare vyākulībhūtvā praṇaśyati kalau yuge //
1.39.d: द्वापरे व्याकुलीभूत्वा प्रणश्यति कलौ युगे ॥
1.39.m: becoming perturbed in Dvāpara, it perishes in the Kali yuga.

1.40.s:
śakra uvāca
tiṣye māyāmasūyāṃ ca vadhaṃ caiva tapasvinām
sādhayanti narāstatra tamasā vyākulendriyāḥ //
1.40.d:
शक्र उवाच
तिष्ये मायामसूयां च वधं चैव तपस्विनाम्
साधयन्ति नरास्तत्र तमसा व्याकुलेन्द्रियाः ॥
1.40.m: Śakra said: / In the Kali [age], men whose senses are perturbed by tamas practice / deceit, malice, and the murder of ascetics.

1.40.s:
kalau pramādako rogaḥ satataṃ kṣudbhayāni ca
anāvṛṣṭibhayaṃ ghoraṃ deśānāṃ ca viparyayaḥ //
1.40.d:
कलौ प्रमादको रोगः सततं क्षुद्भयानि च
अनावृष्टिभयं घोरं देशानां च विपर्ययः ॥
1.40.m: In Kali, there is constant pestilence, disease, fear of starvation, / the terrible fear of drought, and ruin of lands.

1.40.s:
na prāmāṇyaṃ śruterasti nṛṇāṃ cādharmasevanam
adhārmikāstvanācārā mahākopālpacetasaḥ //
1.40.d:
न प्रामाण्यं श्रुतेरस्ति नृणां चाधर्मसेवनम्
अधार्मिकास्त्वनाचारा महाकोपाल्पचेतसः ॥
1.40.m: There is no authority in the Veda, and men engage in unrighteousness; / they become unrighteous, ill-behaved, highly wrathful, and small-minded.

1.40.s:
anṛtaṃ bruvate lubdhās tiṣye jātāś ca duṣprajāḥ
duriṣṭairduradhītaiś ca durācārairdurāgamaiḥ //
1.40.d:
अनृतं ब्रुवते लुब्धास् तिष्ये जाताश् च दुष्प्रजाः
दुरिष्टैर्दुरधीतैश् च दुराचारैर्दुरागमैः ॥
1.40.m: Born in the Kali [age], greedy and wicked people speak falsehood; / with improper sacrifices, improper study, bad conduct, and false doctrines,

1.40.s:
viprāṇāṃ karma doṣeṇa prajānāṃ jāyate bhayam
nādhīyante tadā vedān na yajanti dvijātayaḥ //
1.40.d:
विप्राणां कर्म दोषेण प्रजानां जायते भयम्
नाधीयन्ते तदा वेदान् न यजन्ति द्विजातयः ॥
1.40.m: through the flawed deeds of the brāhmaṇas, fear arises among the subjects. / Then the twice-born do not study the Vedas, nor do they sacrifice.

1.40.s:
utsīdanti narāścaiva kṣatriyāś ca viśaḥ kramāt
śūdrāṇāṃ mantrayogena saṃbandho brāhmaṇaiḥ saha //
1.40.d:
उत्सीदन्ति नराश्चैव क्षत्रियाश् च विशः क्रमात्
शूद्राणां मन्त्रयोगेन संबन्धो ब्राह्मणैः सह ॥
1.40.m: Men fall into ruin, the kṣatriyas and vaiśyas in turn; / an association of śūdras with brāhmaṇas by means of mantras

1.40.s:
bhavatīha kalau tasmiñ śayanāsanabhojanaiḥ
rājānaḥ śūdrabhūyiṣṭhā brāhmaṇān bādhayanti te //
1.40.d:
भवतीह कलौ तस्मिञ् शयनासनभोजनैः
राजानः शूद्रभूयिष्ठा ब्राह्मणान् बाधयन्ति ते ॥
1.40.m: takes place here in that Kali, in sharing beds, seats, and food. / The kings are mostly śūdras; they oppress the brāhmaṇas.

1.40.s:
bhrūṇahatyā vīrahatyā prajāyante prajāsu vai
śūdrāś ca brāhmaṇācārāḥ śūdrācārāś ca brāhmaṇāḥ //
1.40.d:
भ्रूणहत्या वीरहत्या प्रजायन्ते प्रजासु वै
शूद्राश् च ब्राह्मणाचाराः शूद्राचाराश् च ब्राह्मणाः ॥
1.40.m: Destruction of embryos and killing of heroes arise among the people. / Śūdras take up the conduct of brāhmaṇas, and brāhmaṇas the conduct of śūdras.

1.40.s:
rājavṛttisthitāś caurāś caurācārāś ca pārthivāḥ
ekapatnyo na śiṣyanti vardhiṣyantyabhisārikāḥ //
1.40.d:
राजवृत्तिस्थिताश् चौराश् चौराचाराश् च पार्थिवाः
एकपत्न्यो न शिष्यन्ति वर्धिष्यन्त्यभिसारिकाः ॥
1.40.m: Thieves abide in the conduct of kings, and rulers adopt the conduct of thieves. / Faithful wives will not remain; courtesans will increase.

1.40.s:
varṇāśramapratiṣṭhāno jāyate nṛṣu sarvataḥ
tadā svalpaphalā bhūmiḥ kvaciccāpi mahāphalā //
1.40.d:
वर्णाश्रमप्रतिष्ठानो जायते नृषु सर्वतः
तदा स्वल्पफला भूमिः क्वचिच्चापि महाफला ॥
1.40.m: The [destruction of the] stability of the classes and life-stages occurs everywhere among men. / Then the earth yields little fruit, though in some places it yields great fruit.

1.40.s:
arakṣitāro hartāraḥ pārthivāś ca śilāśana
śūdrā vai jñāninaḥ sarve brāhmaṇairabhivanditāḥ //
1.40.d:
अरक्षितारो हर्तारः पार्थिवाश् च शिलाशन
शूद्रा वै ज्ञानिनः सर्वे ब्राह्मणैरभिवन्दिताः ॥
1.40.m: The rulers are no protectors, but plundering thieves, O Śilāśana! / Śūdras become all-knowing, saluted by brāhmaṇas.

1.40.s:
akṣatriyāś ca rājāno viprāḥ śūdropajīvinaḥ
āsanasthā dvijāndṛṣṭvā na calantyalpabuddhayaḥ //
1.40.d:
अक्षत्रियाश् च राजानो विप्राः शूद्रोपजीविनः
आसनस्था द्विजान्दृष्ट्वा न चलन्त्यल्पबुद्धयः ॥
1.40.m: Non-kṣatriyas become kings, and brāhmaṇas live at the expense of śūdras. / Sitting upon their seats, the foolish ones do not rise when seeing the twice-born.

1.40.s:
tāḍayanti dvijendrāṃś ca śūdrā vai svalpabuddhayaḥ
āsye nidhāya vai hastaṃ karṇaṃ śūdrasya vai dvijāḥ //
1.40.d:
ताडयन्ति द्विजेन्द्रांश् च शूद्रा वै स्वल्पबुद्धयः
आस्ये निधाय वै हस्तं कर्णं शूद्रस्य वै द्विजाः ॥
1.40.m: Indeed, foolish śūdras beat the chief twice-born. / Placing a hand over their mouths, the twice-born into the ear of a śūdra,

1.40.s:
nīcasyeva tadā vākyaṃ vadanti vinayena tam
uccāsanasthān śūdrāṃś ca dvijamadhye dvijarṣabha //
1.40.d:
नीचस्येव तदा वाक्यं वदन्ति विनयेन तम्
उच्चासनस्थान् शूद्रांश् च द्विजमध्ये द्विजर्षभ ॥
1.40.m: as though speaking to a low-born man, address words to him with humility. / When śūdras sit upon high seats in the midst of twice-born, O best of the twice-born,

1.40.s:
jñātvā na hiṃsate rājā kalau kālavaśena tu
puṣpaiś ca vāsitaiścaiva tathānyair maṅgalaiḥ śubhaiḥ //
1.40.d:
ज्ञात्वा न हिंसते राजा कलौ कालवशेन तु
पुष्पैश् च वासितैश्चैव तथान्यैर् मङ्गलैः शुभैः ॥
1.40.m: the king, knowing this, does not punish them in Kali, under the sway of time. / With fragrant flowers and other auspicious, beneficial things,

1.40.s:
śūdrānabhyarcayantyalpaśrutabhāgyabalānvitāḥ
na prekṣante garvitāś ca śūdrā dvijavarān dvija //
1.40.d:
शूद्रानभ्यर्चयन्त्यल्पश्रुतभाग्यबलान्विताः
न प्रेक्षन्ते गर्विताश् च शूद्रा द्विजवरान् द्विज ॥
1.40.m: those possessed of little learning, fortune, and strength worship śūdras. / Arrogant śūdras do not look upon the best of twice-born, O twice-born one!

1.40.s:
sevāvasaram ālokya dvāre tiṣṭhanti vai dvijāḥ
vāhanasthān samāvṛtya śūdrāñśūdropajīvinaḥ //
1.40.d:
सेवावसरम् आलोक्य द्वारे तिष्ठन्ति वै द्विजाः
वाहनस्थान् समावृत्य शूद्राञ्शूद्रोपजीविनः ॥
1.40.m: Waiting for an opportunity to serve, the twice-born stand at the door. / Gathering around those seated in vehicles, the brāhmaṇas there serve the śūdras,

1.40.s:
sevante brāhmaṇāstatra stuvanti stutibhiḥ kalau
tapoyajñaphalānāṃ ca vikretāro dvijottamāḥ //
1.40.d:
सेवन्ते ब्राह्मणास्तत्र स्तुवन्ति स्तुतिभिः कलौ
तपोयज्ञफलानां च विक्रेतारो द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
1.40.m: and those who live at the expense of śūdras praise them with hymns in Kali. / The foremost twice-born become sellers of the fruits of austerities and sacrifices.

1.40.s:
yatayaś ca bhaviṣyanti bahavo 'sminkalau yuge
puruṣālpaṃ bahustrīkaṃ yugānte samupasthite //
1.40.d:
यतयश् च भविष्यन्ति बहवो ऽस्मिन्कलौ युगे
पुरुषाल्पं बहुस्त्रीकं युगान्ते समुपस्थिते ॥
1.40.m: Many ascetics will arise in this Kali yuga. / When the end of the yuga approaches, men will be few and women many.

1.40.s:
nindanti vedavidyāṃ ca dvijāḥ karmāṇi vai kalau
kalau devo mahādevaḥ śaṅkaro nīlalohitaḥ //
1.40.d:
निन्दन्ति वेदविद्यां च द्विजाः कर्माणि वै कलौ
कलौ देवो महादेवः शङ्करो नीललोहितः ॥
1.40.m: In Kali, the twice-born revile Vedic knowledge and rituals. / In Kali, God Mahādeva, Śaṅkara, Nīlalohita,

1.40.s:
prakāśate pratiṣṭhārthaṃ dharmasya vikṛtākṛtiḥ
ye taṃ viprā niṣevante yena kenāpi śaṅkaram //
1.40.d:
प्रकाशते प्रतिष्ठार्थं धर्मस्य विकृताकृतिः
ये तं विप्रा निषेवन्ते येन केनापि शङ्करम् ॥
1.40.m: appears in a deformed guise for the sake of establishing dharma. / Whichever brāhmaṇas worship that Śaṅkara by any means whatever,

1.40.s:
kalidoṣān vinirjitya prayānti paramaṃ padam
śvāpadaprabalatvaṃ ca gavāṃ caiva parikṣayaḥ //
1.40.d:
कलिदोषान् विनिर्जित्य प्रयान्ति परमं पदम्
श्वापदप्रबलत्वं च गवां चैव परिक्षयः ॥
1.40.m: they overcome the evils of Kali and reach the supreme state. / The prevalence of wild beasts and the destruction of cows,

1.40.s:
sādhūnāṃ vinivṛttiś ca vedyā tasminyugakṣaye
tadā sūkṣmo mahodarko durlabho dānamūlavān //
1.40.d:
साधूनां विनिवृत्तिश् च वेद्या तस्मिन्युगक्षये
तदा सूक्ष्मो महोदर्को दुर्लभो दानमूलवान् ॥
1.40.m: and the departure of good men are to be known at the destruction of that yuga. / Then dharma, subtle, of great future result, difficult to attain, and rooted in giving,

1.40.s:
cāturāśramaśaithilye dharmaḥ praticaliṣyati
arakṣitāro hartāro balibhāgasya pārthivāḥ //
1.40.d:
चातुराश्रमशैथिल्ये धर्मः प्रतिचलिष्यति
अरक्षितारो हर्तारो बलिभागस्य पार्थिवाः ॥
1.40.m: will falter when the four life-stages become lax. / Failing to protect, taking the share of tax,

1.40.s:
yugānteṣu bhaviṣyanti svarakṣaṇaparāyaṇāḥ
aṭṭaśūlā janapadāḥ śivaśūlāścatuṣpathāḥ //
1.40.d:
युगान्तेषु भविष्यन्ति स्वरक्षणपरायणाः
अट्टशूला जनपदाः शिवशूलाश्चतुष्पथाः ॥
1.40.m: rulers at the end of the yuga will be devoted only to self-preservation. / The provinces will have storehouses for weapons; crossroads will have tridents of Śiva;

1.40.s:
pramadāḥ keśaśūlinyo bhaviṣyanti kalau yuge
citravarṣī tadā devo yadā prāhuryugakṣayam //
1.40.d:
प्रमदाः केशशूलिन्यो भविष्यन्ति कलौ युगे
चित्रवर्षी तदा देवो यदा प्राहुर्युगक्षयम् ॥
1.40.m: women will use their hair as weapons in the Kali yuga. / When they speak of the destruction of the yuga, the sky-god rains variably;

1.40.s:
sarve vaṇigjanāścāpi bhaviṣyantyadhame yuge
kuśīlacaryāḥ pāṣaṇḍair vṛthārūpaiḥ samāvṛtāḥ //
1.40.d:
सर्वे वणिग्जनाश्चापि भविष्यन्त्यधमे युगे
कुशीलचर्याः पाषण्डैर् वृथारूपैः समावृताः ॥
1.40.m: all people will become traders in that base yuga, / actors in conduct, surrounded by hypocrites devoid of virtue.

1.40.s:
bahuyājanako loko bhaviṣyati parasparam
nāvyāhṛtakrūravākyo nārjavī nānasūyakaḥ //
1.40.d:
बहुयाजनको लोको भविष्यति परस्परम्
नाव्याहृतक्रूरवाक्यो नार्जवी नानसूयकः ॥
1.40.m: People will mutually officiate at sacrifices for many; / no one will leave cruel words unsaid, no one will be straightforward, no one free from envy.

1.40.s:
na kṛte pratikartā ca yugakṣīṇe bhaviṣyati
nindakāścaiva patitā yugāntasya ca lakṣaṇam //
1.40.d:
न कृते प्रतिकर्ता च युगक्षीणे भविष्यति
निन्दकाश्चैव पतिता युगान्तस्य च लक्षणम् ॥
1.40.m: When the yuga declines, there will be no one who returns a favor. / Slanderers and fallen men are the hallmark of the end of the yuga.

1.40.s:
nṛpaśūnyā vasumatī na ca dhānyadhanāvṛtā
maṇḍalāni bhaviṣyanti deśeṣu nagareṣu ca //
1.40.d:
नृपशून्या वसुमती न च धान्यधनावृता
मण्डलानि भविष्यन्ति देशेषु नगरेषु च ॥
1.40.m: The earth will be bereft of kings and devoid of grain and wealth; / factions will form in provinces and cities.

1.40.s:
alpodakā cālpaphalā bhaviṣyati vasuṃdharā
goptāraścāpyagoptāraḥ sambhaviṣyantyaśāsanāḥ //
1.40.d:
अल्पोदका चाल्पफला भविष्यति वसुंधरा
गोप्तारश्चाप्यगोप्तारः सम्भविष्यन्त्यशासनाः ॥
1.40.m: The earth will have little water and little fruit. / Protectors will become non-protectors, lawless.

1.40.s:
hartāraḥ paravittānāṃ paradārapradharṣakāḥ
kāmātmāno durātmāno hy adhamāḥ sāhasapriyāḥ //
1.40.d:
हर्तारः परवित्तानां परदारप्रधर्षकाः
कामात्मानो दुरात्मानो ह्य् अधमाः साहसप्रियाः ॥
1.40.m: Robbers of others' wealth, violators of others' wives, / lustful, wicked-souled, base, fond of reckless deeds,

1.40.s:
pranaṣṭaceṣṭanāḥ puṃso muktakeśāś ca śūlinaḥ
janāḥ ṣoḍaśavarṣāś ca prajāyante yugakṣaye //
1.40.d:
प्रनष्टचेष्टनाः पुंसो मुक्तकेशाश् च शूलिनः
जनाः षोडशवर्षाश् च प्रजायन्ते युगक्षये ॥
1.40.m: men will lose their natural endeavors, with disheveled hair, bearing tridents; / people will produce offspring at sixteen years of age at the end of the yuga.

1.40.s:
śukladantājinākṣāś ca muṇḍāḥ kāṣāyavāsasaḥ
śūdrā dharmaṃ cariṣyanti yugānte samupasthite //
1.40.d:
शुक्लदन्ताजिनाक्षाश् च मुण्डाः काषायवाससः
शूद्रा धर्मं चरिष्यन्ति युगान्ते समुपस्थिते ॥
1.40.m: Showing white teeth, wearing deerskins and spectacles, shaven-headed, clad in red garments, / śūdras will practice dharma when the end of the yuga has arrived.

1.40.s:
sasyacaurā bhaviṣyanti dṛḍhacailābhilāṣiṇaḥ
caurāścorasvahartāro harturhartā tathāparaḥ //
1.40.d:
सस्यचौरा भविष्यन्ति दृढचैलाभिलाषिणः
चौराश्चोरस्वहर्तारो हर्तुर्हर्ता तथापरः ॥
1.40.m: Men will be thieves of grain, desiring durable clothing. / Thieves will steal thieves' wealth, and another will rob the robber.

1.40.s:
yogyakarmaṇyuparate loke niṣkriyatāṃ gate
kīṭamūṣakasarpāś ca dharṣayiṣyanti mānavān //
1.40.d:
योग्यकर्मण्युपरते लोके निष्क्रियतां गते
कीटमूषकसर्पाश् च धर्षयिष्यन्ति मानवान् ॥
1.40.m: When proper work ceases and the world has fallen into inactivity, / insects, mice, and snakes will attack humans.

1.40.s:
subhikṣaṃ kṣemamārogyaṃ sāmarthyaṃ durlabhaṃ tadā
kauśikīṃ pratipatsyante deśānkṣudbhayapīḍitāḥ //
1.40.d:
सुभिक्षं क्षेममारोग्यं सामर्थ्यं दुर्लभं तदा
कौशिकीं प्रतिपत्स्यन्ते देशान्क्षुद्भयपीडिताः ॥
1.40.m: Abundance, safety, health, and strength will then be hard to find; / afflicted by hunger and fear, they will flee to the regions around the Kauśikī.

1.40.s:
duḥkhenābhiplutānāṃ ca paramāyuḥ śataṃ tadā
dṛśyante na ca dṛśyante vedāḥ kaliyuge 'khilāḥ //
1.40.d:
दुःखेनाभिप्लुतानां च परमायुः शतं तदा
दृश्यन्ते न च दृश्यन्ते वेदाः कलियुगे ऽखिलाः ॥
1.40.m: And for those overwhelmed by suffering, the maximum lifespan will then be a hundred years; / in the Kali yuga, the Vedas in their entirety are both seen and not seen.

1.40.s:
utsīdanti tadā yajñāḥ kevalādharmapīḍitāḥ
kāṣāyiṇo 'pyanirgranthāḥ kāpālībahulāstviha //
1.40.d:
उत्सीदन्ति तदा यज्ञाः केवलाधर्मपीडिताः
काषायिणो ऽप्यनिर्ग्रन्थाः कापालीबहुलास्त्विह ॥
1.40.m: Sacrifices then decay, overwhelmed entirely by unrighteousness; / there are those wearing ochre robes though not unattached, and skull-bearing ascetics abound here.

1.40.s:
vedavikrayiṇaścānye tīrthavikrayiṇaḥ pare
varṇāśramāṇāṃ ye cānye pāṣaṇḍāḥ paripanthinaḥ //
1.40.d:
वेदविक्रयिणश्चान्ये तीर्थविक्रयिणः परे
वर्णाश्रमाणां ये चान्ये पाषण्डाः परिपन्थिनः ॥
1.40.m: Others sell the Vedas, and yet others sell sacred bathing sites; / and there are other heretics who obstruct the social classes and life stages.

1.40.s:
utpadyante tadā te vai samprāpte tu kalau yuge
adhīyante tadā vedāñ śūdrā dharmārthakovidāḥ //
1.40.d:
उत्पद्यन्ते तदा ते वै सम्प्राप्ते तु कलौ युगे
अधीयन्ते तदा वेदाञ् शूद्रा धर्मार्थकोविदाः ॥
1.40.m: They indeed arise when the Kali yuga arrives; / then Śūdras, skilled in the meaning of righteousness, study the Vedas.

1.40.s:
yajante cāśvamedhena rājānaḥ śūdrayonayaḥ
strībālagovadhaṃ kṛtvā hatvā caiva parasparam //
1.40.d:
यजन्ते चाश्वमेधेन राजानः शूद्रयोनयः
स्त्रीबालगोवधं कृत्वा हत्वा चैव परस्परम् ॥
1.40.m: And kings of Śūdra origin perform the horse sacrifice; / having killed women, children, and cows, and having slain one another,

1.40.s:
upadravāṃstathānyonyaṃ sādhayanti tadā prajāḥ
duḥkhaprabhūtamalpāyur dehotsādaḥ sarogatā //
1.40.d:
उपद्रवांस्तथान्योन्यं साधयन्ति तदा प्रजाः
दुःखप्रभूतमल्पायुर् देहोत्सादः सरोगता ॥
1.40.m: the subjects then inflict afflictions on each other. / Full of suffering, with short lifespans, their bodies waste away, beset by diseases.

1.40.s:
adharmābhiniveśitvāt tamovṛttaṃ kalau smṛtam
prajāsu brahmahatyādi tadā vai sampravartate //
1.40.d:
अधर्माभिनिवेशित्वात् तमोवृत्तं कलौ स्मृतम्
प्रजासु ब्रह्महत्यादि तदा वै सम्प्रवर्तते ॥
1.40.m: Because of dedication to unrighteousness, conduct in the Kali [yuga] is known to be governed by tamas; / then indeed the slaying of brāhmaṇas and other [crimes] proceed among the subjects.

1.40.s:
tasmādāyurbalaṃ rūpaṃ kaliṃ prāpya prahīyate
tadā tvalpena kālena siddhiṃ gacchanti mānavāḥ //
1.40.d:
तस्मादायुर्बलं रूपं कलिं प्राप्य प्रहीयते
तदा त्वल्पेन कालेन सिद्धिं गच्छन्ति मानवाः ॥
1.40.m: Therefore, upon reaching Kali, lifespan, strength, and beauty decline; / yet in a short time men then attain perfection.

1.40.s:
dhanyā dharmaṃ cariṣyanti yugānte dvijasattamāḥ
śrutismṛtyuditaṃ dharmaṃ ye carantyanasūyakāḥ //
1.40.d:
धन्या धर्मं चरिष्यन्ति युगान्ते द्विजसत्तमाः
श्रुतिस्मृत्युदितं धर्मं ये चरन्त्यनसूयकाः ॥
1.40.m: At the end of the yuga, fortunate ones will practice righteousness, O best of the twice-born; / those who, free from malice, practice the righteousness taught by Śruti and Smṛti,

1.40.s:
tretāyāṃ vārṣiko dharmo dvāpare māsikaḥ smṛtaḥ
yathākleśaṃ caranprājñas tadahnā prāpnute kalau //
1.40.d:
त्रेतायां वार्षिको धर्मो द्वापरे मासिकः स्मृतः
यथाक्लेशं चरन्प्राज्ञस् तदह्ना प्राप्नुते कलौ ॥
1.40.m: righteousness requiring a year in the Tretā is said to require a month in the Dvāpara; / practicing it according to his capacity, a wise man attains it in a single day in the Kali.

1.40.s:
eṣā kaliyugāvasthā saṃdhyāṃśaṃ tu nibodha me
yuge yuge ca hīyante trīṃstrīnpādāṃstu siddhayaḥ //
1.40.d:
एषा कलियुगावस्था संध्यांशं तु निबोध मे
युगे युगे च हीयन्ते त्रींस्त्रीन्पादांस्तु सिद्धयः ॥
1.40.m: This is the state of the Kali yuga; now learn from me the dusk twilight. / In yuga after yuga, perfections decline by three quarters at a time.

1.40.s:
yugasvabhāvāḥ saṃdhyāstu tiṣṭhantīha tu pādaśaḥ
saṃdhyāsvabhāvāḥ svāṃśeṣu pādaśaste pratiṣṭhitāḥ //
1.40.d:
युगस्वभावाः संध्यास्तु तिष्ठन्तीह तु पादशः
संध्यास्वभावाः स्वांशेषु पादशस्ते प्रतिष्ठिताः ॥
1.40.m: The characteristics of the yugas abide quarter by quarter in the dawn twilights; / the characteristics of the dawn twilights are established quarter by quarter in their dusk twilights.

1.40.s:
evaṃ saṃdhyāṃśake kāle samprāpte tu yugāntike
teṣāṃ śāstā hyasādhūnāṃ bhūtānāṃ nidhanotthitaḥ //
1.40.d:
एवं संध्यांशके काले सम्प्राप्ते तु युगान्तिके
तेषां शास्ता ह्यसाधूनां भूतानां निधनोत्थितः ॥
1.40.m: Thus, when the time of the dusk twilight arrives at the end of the yuga, / a punisher of those wicked creatures arises at their destruction.

1.40.s:
gotre 'sminvai candramaso nāmnā pramitirucyate
mānavasya tu so 'ṃśena pūrvaṃ svāyaṃbhuve 'ntare //
1.40.d:
गोत्रे ऽस्मिन्वै चन्द्रमसो नाम्ना प्रमितिरुच्यते
मानवस्य तु सो ऽंशेन पूर्वं स्वायंभुवे ऽन्तरे ॥
1.40.m: In this lineage of Candramas, he is called Pramiti by name; / formerly, in the Svāyambhuva manvantara, [he was born] from a portion of Manu.

1.40.s:
samāḥ sa viṃśatiḥ pūrṇāḥ paryaṭanvai vasuṃdharām
anukarṣan sa vai senāṃ savājirathakuñjarām //
1.40.d:
समाः स विंशतिः पूर्णाः पर्यटन्वै वसुंधराम्
अनुकर्षन् स वै सेनां सवाजिरथकुञ्जराम् ॥
1.40.m: Wandering indeed over the earth for twenty full years, / he led an army endowed with horses, chariots, and elephants.

1.40.s:
pragṛhītāyudhairvipraiḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
sa tadā taiḥ parivṛto mlecchān hanti sahasraśaḥ //
1.40.d:
प्रगृहीतायुधैर्विप्रैः शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः
स तदा तैः परिवृतो म्लेच्छान् हन्ति सहस्रशः ॥
1.40.m: With brāhmaṇas holding weapons by the hundreds and thousands, / surrounded by them then, he slays barbarians by the thousands.

1.40.s:
sa hatvā sarvaśaścaiva rājñastāñśūdrayonijān
pākhaṇḍāṃstu tataḥ sarvān niḥśeṣaṃ kṛtavān prabhuḥ //
1.40.d:
स हत्वा सर्वशश्चैव राज्ञस्ताञ्शूद्रयोनिजान्
पाखण्डांस्तु ततः सर्वान् निःशेषं कृतवान् प्रभुः ॥
1.40.m: Having slain those kings born of Śūdra wombs on all sides, / the lord then completely eliminated all the heretics.

1.40.s:
nātyarthaṃ dhārmikā ye ca tān sarvān hanti sarvataḥ
varṇavyatyāsajātāś ca ye ca tānanujīvinaḥ //
1.40.d:
नात्यर्थं धार्मिका ये च तान् सर्वान् हन्ति सर्वतः
वर्णव्यत्यासजाताश् च ये च ताननुजीविनः ॥
1.40.m: And those who were not very righteous, he kills them all everywhere, / as well as those born of the confusion of castes and their dependents.

1.40.s:
pravṛttacakro balavān mlecchānāmantakṛtsa tu
adhṛṣyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ cacārātha vasuṃdharām //
1.40.d:
प्रवृत्तचक्रो बलवान् म्लेच्छानामन्तकृत्स तु
अधृष्यः सर्वभूतानां चचाराथ वसुंधराम् ॥
1.40.m: With his wheel set rolling, powerful, the terminator of barbarians, / unassailable by all creatures, he then roamed the earth.

1.40.s:
mānavasya tu so 'ṃśena devasyeha vijajñivān
pūrvajanmani viṣṇostu pramitirnāma vīryavān //
1.40.d:
मानवस्य तु सो ऽंशेन देवस्येह विजज्ञिवान्
पूर्वजन्मनि विष्णोस्तु प्रमितिर्नाम वीर्यवान् ॥
1.40.m: Born here from a portion of Manu, of the god [Viṣṇu]— / he was the heroic one named Pramiti in a former birth of Viṣṇu.

1.40.s:
gotrato vai candramasaḥ pūrṇe kaliyuge prabhuḥ
dvātriṃśe 'bhyudite varṣe prakrānto viṃśatiḥ samāḥ //
1.40.d:
गोत्रतो वै चन्द्रमसः पूर्णे कलियुगे प्रभुः
द्वात्रिंशे ऽभ्युदिते वर्षे प्रक्रान्तो विंशतिः समाः ॥
1.40.m: From the lineage of Candramas, when the Kali yuga was full, the lord, / having arisen in his thirty-second year, advanced for twenty years,

1.40.s:
vinighnansarvabhūtāni śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
kṛtvā bījāvaśeṣāṃ tu pṛthivīṃ krūrakarmaṇaḥ //
1.40.d:
विनिघ्नन्सर्वभूतानि शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः
कृत्वा बीजावशेषां तु पृथिवीं क्रूरकर्मणः ॥
1.40.m: slaying all creatures by the hundreds and thousands; / having reduced the earth to a remnant of seeds, of cruel deeds,

1.40.s:
parasparanimittena kopenākasmikena tu
sa sādhayitvā vṛṣalān prāyaśas tān adhārmikān //
1.40.d:
परस्परनिमित्तेन कोपेनाकस्मिकेन तु
स साधयित्वा वृषलान् प्रायशस् तान् अधार्मिकान् ॥
1.40.m: through mutual causes and sudden fury, / having subdued those base and mostly unrighteous men,

1.40.s:
gaṅgāyamunayormadhye sthitiṃ prāptaḥ sahānugaḥ
tato vyatīte kāle tu sāmātyaḥ sahasainikaḥ //
1.40.d:
गङ्गायमुनयोर्मध्ये स्थितिं प्राप्तः सहानुगः
ततो व्यतीते काले तु सामात्यः सहसैनिकः ॥
1.40.m: he took up residence between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā along with his followers. / Then, when time had elapsed, together with his ministers and his army,

1.40.s:
utsādya pārthivān sarvān mlecchāṃścaiva sahasraśaḥ
tatra saṃdhyāṃśake kāle samprāpte tu yugāntike //
1.40.d:
उत्साद्य पार्थिवान् सर्वान् म्लेच्छांश्चैव सहस्रशः
तत्र संध्यांशके काले सम्प्राप्ते तु युगान्तिके ॥
1.40.m: having eradicated all kings and barbarians by the thousands, / there, when the time of the dusk twilight arrived at the end of the yuga,

1.40.s:
sthitāsvalpāvaśiṣṭāsu prajāsviha kvacitkvacit
apragrahāstatastā vai lobhāviṣṭāstu kṛtsnaśaḥ //
1.40.d:
स्थितास्वल्पावशिष्टासु प्रजास्विह क्वचित्क्वचित्
अप्रग्रहास्ततस्ता वै लोभाविष्टास्तु कृत्स्नशः ॥
1.40.m: when few remaining subjects were situated here and there, / unrestrained, completely seized by greed,

1.40.s:
upahiṃsanti cānyonyaṃ praṇipatya parasparam
arājake yugavaśāt saṃśaye samupasthite //
1.40.d:
उपहिंसन्ति चान्योन्यं प्रणिपत्य परस्परम्
अराजके युगवशात् संशये समुपस्थिते ॥
1.40.m: they injure one another after bowing down before each other; / in a kingless state, by the power of the yuga, when danger has arrived,

1.40.s:
prajāstā vai tataḥ sarvāḥ parasparabhayārditāḥ
vyākulāś ca paribhrāntās tyaktvā dārān gṛhāṇi ca //
1.40.d:
प्रजास्ता वै ततः सर्वाः परस्परभयार्दिताः
व्याकुलाश् च परिभ्रान्तास् त्यक्त्वा दारान् गृहाणि च ॥
1.40.m: all those subjects, tormented by mutual fear, / agitated and wandering about, abandoning wives and homes,

1.40.s:
svānprāṇān anapekṣanto niṣkāruṇyāḥ suduḥkhitāḥ
naṣṭe śraute smārtadharme parasparahatāstadā //
1.40.d:
स्वान्प्राणान् अनपेक्षन्तो निष्कारुण्याः सुदुःखिताः
नष्टे श्रौते स्मार्तधर्मे परस्परहतास्तदा ॥
1.40.m: disregarding their own lives, pitiless, deeply sorrowful, / when the righteousness of Śruti and Smṛti is lost, they are slain by one another.

1.40.s:
nirmaryādā nirākrāntā niḥsnehā nirapatrapāḥ
naṣṭe dharme pratihatāḥ hrasvakāḥ pañcaviṃśakāḥ //
1.40.d:
निर्मर्यादा निराक्रान्ता निःस्नेहा निरपत्रपाः
नष्टे धर्मे प्रतिहताः ह्रस्वकाः पञ्चविंशकाः ॥
1.40.m: Boundless, unrestrained, devoid of affection, shameless, / confounded when righteousness is lost, dwarfish, living twenty-five years,

1.40.s:
hitvā putrāṃś ca dārāṃś ca vivādavyākulendriyāḥ
anāvṛṣṭihatāścaiva vārtāmutsṛjya dūrataḥ //
1.40.d:
हित्वा पुत्रांश् च दारांश् च विवादव्याकुलेन्द्रियाः
अनावृष्टिहताश्चैव वार्तामुत्सृज्य दूरतः ॥
1.40.m: leaving their sons and wives, their senses agitated by dispute, / struck by drought, abandoning agriculture far away,

1.40.s:
pratyantānupasevante hitvā janapadān svakān
saritsāgarakūpāṃste sevante parvatāṃs tathā //
1.40.d:
प्रत्यन्तानुपसेवन्ते हित्वा जनपदान् स्वकान्
सरित्सागरकूपांस्ते सेवन्ते पर्वतांस् तथा ॥
1.40.m: they resort to frontier regions, abandoning their own realms; / they resort to rivers, the ocean, wells, and mountains.

1.40.s:
madhumāṃsairmūlaphalair vartayanti suduḥkhitāḥ
cīrapatrājinadharā niṣkriyā niṣparigrahāḥ //
1.40.d:
मधुमांसैर्मूलफलैर् वर्तयन्ति सुदुःखिताः
चीरपत्राजिनधरा निष्क्रिया निष्परिग्रहाः ॥
1.40.m: They sustain themselves with honey, meat, roots, and fruits, deeply sorrowful, / wearing rags, leaves, and hides, inactive, without possessions,

1.40.s:
varṇāśramaparibhraṣṭāḥ saṃkaṭaṃ ghoramāsthitāḥ
evaṃ kaṣṭamanuprāptā alpaśeṣāḥ prajāstadā //
1.40.d:
वर्णाश्रमपरिभ्रष्टाः संकटं घोरमास्थिताः
एवं कष्टमनुप्राप्ता अल्पशेषाः प्रजास्तदा ॥
1.40.m: fallen from social classes and life stages, entering severe distress. / Thus having attained misery, the subjects remaining in small numbers then,

1.40.s:
jarāvyādhikṣudhāviṣṭā duḥkhānnirvedamānasāḥ
vicāraṇā tu nirvedāt sāmyāvasthā vicāraṇā //
1.40.d:
जराव्याधिक्षुधाविष्टा दुःखान्निर्वेदमानसाः
विचारणा तु निर्वेदात् साम्यावस्था विचारणा ॥
1.40.m: seized by old age, disease, and hunger, have their minds turned to detachment from suffering; / and from detachment comes reflection, and reflection is a state of equanimity.

1.40.s:
sāmyāvasthātmako bodhaḥ saṃbodhāddharmaśīlatā
arūpaśamayuktāstu kaliśiṣṭā hi vai svayam //
1.40.d:
साम्यावस्थात्मको बोधः संबोधाद्धर्मशीलता
अरूपशमयुक्तास्तु कलिशिष्टा हि वै स्वयम् ॥
1.40.m: Spiritual awakening consists of the state of equanimity; from awakening comes devotion to righteousness. / Endowed with tranquility without outward form, those remaining from the Kali [yuga] indeed [awaken] by themselves;

1.40.s:
ahorātrāttadā tāsāṃ yugaṃ tu parivartate
cittasaṃmohanaṃ kṛtvā tāsāṃ vai suptamattavat //
1.40.d:
अहोरात्रात्तदा तासां युगं तु परिवर्तते
चित्तसंमोहनं कृत्वा तासां वै सुप्तमत्तवत् ॥
1.40.m: then the yuga turns around in the span of a day and night, / making their minds bewildered, as if they were asleep or drunk.

1.40.s:
bhāvino 'rthasya ca balāt tataḥ kṛtamavartata
pravṛtte tu tatastasmin punaḥ kṛtayuge tu vai //
1.40.d:
भाविनो ऽर्थस्य च बलात् ततः कृतमवर्तत
प्रवृत्ते तु ततस्तस्मिन् पुनः कृतयुगे तु वै ॥
1.40.m: By the power of what was destined to be, the Kṛta [yuga] then commenced; / and when that Kṛta yuga had begun again,

1.40.s:
utpannāḥ kaliśiṣṭāstu prajāḥ kārtayugāstadā
tiṣṭhanti ceha ye siddhā adṛṣṭā vicaranti ca //
1.40.d:
उत्पन्नाः कलिशिष्टास्तु प्रजाः कार्तयुगास्तदा
तिष्ठन्ति चेह ये सिद्धा अदृष्टा विचरन्ति च ॥
1.40.m: the subjects remaining from the Kali then became people belonging to the Kṛta [yuga]; / and the perfected ones who remain here roam about unseen.

1.40.s:
sapta saptarṣibhiścaiva tatra te tu vyavasthitāḥ
brahmakṣatraviśaḥ śūdrā bījārthaṃ ye smṛtā iha //
1.40.d:
सप्त सप्तर्षिभिश्चैव तत्र ते तु व्यवस्थिताः
ब्रह्मक्षत्रविशः शूद्रा बीजार्थं ये स्मृता इह ॥
1.40.m: The seven remain stationed there along with the Seven Sages; / brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras who are remembered here as the seed,

1.40.s:
kalijaiḥ saha te sarve nirviśeṣāstadābhavan
teṣāṃ saptarṣayo dharmaṃ kathayantītare 'pi ca //
1.40.d:
कलिजैः सह ते सर्वे निर्विशेषास्तदाभवन्
तेषां सप्तर्षयो धर्मं कथयन्तीतरे ऽपि च ॥
1.40.m: they all then became indistinguishable from those born in the Kali [yuga]; / the Seven Sages and others declare righteousness to them,

1.40.s:
varṇāśramācārayutaṃ śrautaṃ smārtaṃ dvidhā tu yam
tatasteṣu kriyāvatsu vardhante vai prajāḥ kṛte //
1.40.d:
वर्णाश्रमाचारयुतं श्रौतं स्मार्तं द्विधा तु यम्
ततस्तेषु क्रियावत्सु वर्धन्ते वै प्रजाः कृते ॥
1.40.m: which consists of the conduct of the social classes and life stages, twofold as Śrauta and Smārta; / then, as they perform their rituals, the subjects indeed multiply in the Kṛta [yuga].

1.40.s:
śrautasmārtakṛtānāṃ ca dharme saptarṣidarśite
keciddharmavyavasthārthaṃ tiṣṭhantīha yugakṣaye //
1.40.d:
श्रौतस्मार्तकृतानां च धर्मे सप्तर्षिदर्शिते
केचिद्धर्मव्यवस्थार्थं तिष्ठन्तीह युगक्षये ॥
1.40.m: In the righteousness performed according to Śruti and Smṛti, revealed by the Seven Sages, / some remain here at the end of the yuga for the sake of establishing righteousness.

1.40.s:
manvantarādhikāreṣu tiṣṭhanti munayastu vai
yathā dāvapradagdheṣu tṛṇeṣviha tataḥ kṣitau //
1.40.d:
मन्वन्तराधिकारेषु तिष्ठन्ति मुनयस्तु वै
यथा दावप्रदग्धेषु तृणेष्विह ततः क्षितौ ॥
1.40.m: Sages indeed remain in charge of the manvantaras; / just as when grasses are burnt by forest fire on the earth,

1.40.s:
vanānāṃ prathamaṃ vṛṣṭyā teṣāṃ mūleṣu saṃbhavaḥ
tathā kārtayugānāṃ tu kalijeṣviha saṃbhavaḥ //
1.40.d:
वनानां प्रथमं वृष्ट्या तेषां मूलेषु संभवः
तथा कार्तयुगानां तु कलिजेष्विह संभवः ॥
1.40.m: the first growth of the woods comes from their roots through rain, / so the appearance of the people of the Kṛta occurs among those born in the Kali.

1.40.s:
evaṃ yugādyugasyeha saṃtānaṃ tu parasparam
vartate ha vyavacchedād yāvanmanvantarakṣayaḥ //
1.40.d:
एवं युगाद्युगस्येह संतानं तु परस्परम्
वर्तते ह व्यवच्छेदाद् यावन्मन्वन्तरक्षयः ॥
1.40.m: Thus the succession from yuga to yuga here proceeds without interruption, / until the end of the manvantara.

1.40.s:
sukhamāyurbalaṃ rūpaṃ dharmo 'rthaḥ kāma eva ca
yugeṣvetāni hīyante trīṃstrīn pādān krameṇa tu //
1.40.d:
सुखमायुर्बलं रूपं धर्मो ऽर्थः काम एव च
युगेष्वेतानि हीयन्ते त्रींस्त्रीन् पादान् क्रमेण तु ॥
1.40.m: Happiness, lifespan, strength, beauty, righteousness, wealth, and desire— / in the yugas, these decline in succession by three quarters at a time.

1.40.s:
sasaṃdhyāṃśeṣu hīyante yugānāṃ dharmasiddhayaḥ
ityeṣā pratisiddhirvai kīrtitaiṣā krameṇa tu //
1.40.d:
ससंध्यांशेषु हीयन्ते युगानां धर्मसिद्धयः
इत्येषा प्रतिसिद्धिर्वै कीर्तितैषा क्रमेण तु ॥
1.40.m: During the twilights, the accomplishments of dharma in the yugas decline; / in this manner, their counter-attainment has been proclaimed in due order.

1.40.s:
caturyugānāṃ sarveṣām anenaiva tu sādhanam
eṣā caturyugāvṛttir ā sahasrād guṇīkṛtā //
1.40.d:
चतुर्युगानां सर्वेषाम् अनेनैव तु साधनम्
एषा चतुर्युगावृत्तिर् आ सहस्राद् गुणीकृता ॥
1.40.m: And the completion of all four-yuga cycles occurs solely by this [measure]; / this cycle of four yugas, multiplied up to a thousand,

1.40.s:
brahmaṇastadahaḥ proktaṃ rātriścaitāvatī smṛtā
anārjavaṃ jaḍībhāvo bhūtānām ā yugakṣayāt //
1.40.d:
ब्रह्मणस्तदहः प्रोक्तं रात्रिश्चैतावती स्मृता
अनार्जवं जडीभावो भूतानाम् आ युगक्षयात् ॥
1.40.m: is declared to be a day of Brahmā, and his night is known to be of the same length. / The crookedness and inertness of living beings lasts until the end of a yuga.

1.40.s:
etadeva tu sarveṣāṃ yugānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ smṛtam
eṣāṃ caturyugāṇāṃ ca guṇitā hyekasaptatiḥ //
1.40.d:
एतदेव तु सर्वेषां युगानां लक्षणं स्मृतम्
एषां चतुर्युगाणां च गुणिता ह्येकसप्ततिः ॥
1.40.m: Indeed, this is considered the characteristic of all the yugas; / and seventy-one of these four-yuga cycles, multiplied together,

1.40.s:
krameṇa parivṛttā tu manorantaram ucyate
caturyuge yathaikasmin bhavatīha yadā tu yat //
1.40.d:
क्रमेण परिवृत्ता तु मनोरन्तरम् उच्यते
चतुर्युगे यथैकस्मिन् भवतीह यदा तु यत् ॥
1.40.m: and revolving in sequence, is called a manvantara. / Just as in one four-yuga cycle whatever occurs here and whenever,

1.40.s:
tathā cānyeṣu bhavati punastadvai yathākramam
sarge sarge yathā bhedā utpadyante tathaiva tu //
1.40.d:
तथा चान्येषु भवति पुनस्तद्वै यथाक्रमम्
सर्गे सर्गे यथा भेदा उत्पद्यन्ते तथैव तु ॥
1.40.m: so it occurs again in the others in due order. / Just as divisions arise in creation after creation,

1.40.s:
pañcaviṃśatparimitā na nyūnā nādhikās tathā
tathā kalpā yugaiḥ sārdhaṃ bhavanti saha lakṣaṇaiḥ //
1.40.d:
पञ्चविंशत्परिमिता न न्यूना नाधिकास् तथा
तथा कल्पा युगैः सार्धं भवन्ति सह लक्षणैः ॥
1.40.m: measured at twenty-five, neither fewer nor more, / so too the kalpas, together with the yugas and their characteristics, come to be.

1.40.s: manvantarāṇāṃ sarveṣām etadeva tu lakṣaṇam //
1.40.d: मन्वन्तराणां सर्वेषाम् एतदेव तु लक्षणम् ॥
1.40.m: This indeed is the characteristic of all the manvantaras.

1.40.s:
yathā yugānāṃ parivartanāni cirapravṛttāni yugasvabhāvāt
tathā tu saṃtiṣṭhati jīvalokaḥ kṣayodayābhyāṃ parivartamānaḥ //
1.40.d:
यथा युगानां परिवर्तनानि चिरप्रवृत्तानि युगस्वभावात्
तथा तु संतिष्ठति जीवलोकः क्षयोदयाभ्यां परिवर्तमानः ॥
1.40.m: Just as the cycles of the yugas have long proceeded by the nature of the yugas, / so the world of living beings endures, revolving through destruction and arising.

1.40.s:
ityetallakṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ yugānāṃ vai samāsataḥ
atītānāgatānāṃ hi sarvamanvantareṣu vai //
1.40.d:
इत्येतल्लक्षणं प्रोक्तं युगानां वै समासतः
अतीतानागतानां हि सर्वमन्वन्तरेषु वै ॥
1.40.m: Thus has this characteristic of the yugas been declared in brief, / for the past and future ones in all manvantaras.

1.40.s:
manvantareṇa caikena sarvāṇyevāntarāṇi ca
vyākhyātāni na saṃdehaḥ kalpaḥ kalpena caiva hi //
1.40.d:
मन्वन्तरेण चैकेन सर्वाण्येवान्तराणि च
व्याख्यातानि न संदेहः कल्पः कल्पेन चैव हि ॥
1.40.m: By one manvantara, all the intervals are explained without doubt, / and kalpa by kalpa as well.

1.40.s:
anāgateṣu tadvacca tarkaḥ kāryo vijānatā
manvantareṣu sarveṣu atītānāgateṣviha //
1.40.d:
अनागतेषु तद्वच्च तर्कः कार्यो विजानता
मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु अतीतानागतेष्विह ॥
1.40.m: In the same manner, inference should be made by one who knows regarding future ones, / in all manvantaras, both past and future here.

1.40.s:
tulyābhimāninaḥ sarve nāmarūpairbhavantyuta
devā hyaṣṭavidhā ye ca ye ca manvantareśvarāḥ //
1.40.d:
तुल्याभिमानिनः सर्वे नामरूपैर्भवन्त्युत
देवा ह्यष्टविधा ये च ये च मन्वन्तरेश्वराः ॥
1.40.m: All possessors of identity are equal in names and forms: / the gods of eight kinds and the lords of the manvantaras,

1.40.s:
ṛṣayo manavaścaiva sarve tulyaprayojanāḥ
evaṃ varṇāśramāṇāṃ tu pravibhāgo yuge yuge //
1.40.d:
ऋषयो मनवश्चैव सर्वे तुल्यप्रयोजनाः
एवं वर्णाश्रमाणां तु प्रविभागो युगे युगे ॥
1.40.m: the sages and the Manus, all have equal purposes. / Thus occurs the division of classes and life-stages in yuga after yuga.

1.40.s:
yugasvabhāvaś ca tathā vidhatte vai tadā prabhuḥ
varṇāśramavibhāgāś ca yugāni yugasiddhayaḥ //
1.40.d:
युगस्वभावश् च तथा विधत्ते वै तदा प्रभुः
वर्णाश्रमविभागाश् च युगानि युगसिद्धयः ॥
1.40.m: And the Lord then ordains the nature of the yuga, / the divisions of classes and life-stages, the yugas, and the accomplishments of the yugas.

1.40.s:
yugānāṃ parimāṇaṃ te kathitaṃ hi prasaṅgataḥ
vadāmi devīputratvaṃ padmayoneḥ samāsataḥ //
1.40.d:
युगानां परिमाणं ते कथितं हि प्रसङ्गतः
वदामि देवीपुत्रत्वं पद्मयोनेः समासतः ॥
1.40.m: The measure of the yugas has been recounted to you incidentally; / I shall now tell in brief of the lotus-born [Brahmā's] being the son of the Goddess.

1.41.s:
indra uvāca
punaḥ sasarja bhagavān prabhraṣṭāḥ pūrvavatprajāḥ
sahasrayugaparyante prabhāte tu pitāmahaḥ //
1.41.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
पुनः ससर्ज भगवान् प्रभ्रष्टाः पूर्ववत्प्रजाः
सहस्रयुगपर्यन्ते प्रभाते तु पितामहः ॥
1.41.m: Indra said: / At the end of a thousand yugas, at dawn, the lord Pitāmaha / once again created the creatures that had disappeared as before.

1.41.s:
evaṃ parārdhe viprendra dviguṇe tu tathā gate
tadā dharāmbhasi vyāptā hy āpo vahnau samīraṇe //
1.41.d:
एवं परार्धे विप्रेन्द्र द्विगुणे तु तथा गते
तदा धराम्भसि व्याप्ता ह्य् आपो वह्नौ समीरणे ॥
1.41.m: When twice a parārdha had thus passed, O best of Brahmins, / the earth was then pervaded by water, and the waters by fire; into the wind,

1.41.s:
vahniḥ samīraṇaścaiva vyomni tanmātrasaṃyutaḥ
indriyāṇi daśaikaṃ ca tanmātrāṇi dvijottama //
1.41.d:
वह्निः समीरणश्चैव व्योम्नि तन्मात्रसंयुतः
इन्द्रियाणि दशैकं च तन्मात्राणि द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.41.m: the fire [dissolved], and the wind dissolved into space along with the subtle elements; / the eleven sense faculties and the subtle elements, O best of twice-born,

1.41.s:
ahaṅkāramanuprāpya pralīnāstatkṣaṇādaho
abhimānastadā tatra mahāntaṃ vyāpya vai kṣaṇāt //
1.41.d:
अहङ्कारमनुप्राप्य प्रलीनास्तत्क्षणादहो
अभिमानस्तदा तत्र महान्तं व्याप्य वै क्षणात् ॥
1.41.m: reached ego and were dissolved at that instant—ah! / Ego, then pervading the Great Principle at that moment,

1.41.s:
mahānapi tathā vyaktaṃ prāpya līno 'bhavaddvija
avyaktaṃ svaguṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ pralīnamabhavadbhave //
1.41.d:
महानपि तथा व्यक्तं प्राप्य लीनो ऽभवद्द्विज
अव्यक्तं स्वगुणैः सार्धं प्रलीनमभवद्भवे ॥
1.41.m: the Great Principle also reached the unmanifest and dissolved, O twice-born. / The unmanifest, along with its own guṇas, was dissolved into Bhava.

1.41.s:
tataḥ sṛṣṭirabhūttasmāt pūrvavatpuruṣācchivāt
atha sṛṣṭāstadā tasya manasā tena mānasāḥ //
1.41.d:
ततः सृष्टिरभूत्तस्मात् पूर्ववत्पुरुषाच्छिवात्
अथ सृष्टास्तदा तस्य मनसा तेन मानसाः ॥
1.41.m: Then, from that Puruṣa, Śiva, creation arose as before. / Thereupon, the mind-born [progeny] created then by him with his mind,

1.41.s:
na vyavardhanta loke 'smin prajāḥ kamalayoninā
vṛddhyarthaṃ bhagavānbrahmā putrairvai mānasaiḥ saha //
1.41.d:
न व्यवर्धन्त लोके ऽस्मिन् प्रजाः कमलयोनिना
वृद्ध्यर्थं भगवान्ब्रह्मा पुत्रैर्वै मानसैः सह ॥
1.41.m: the creatures created by the lotus-born [Brahmā], did not multiply in this world. / For the sake of increase, the lord Brahmā, along with his mind-born sons,

1.41.s:
duścaraṃ vicacāreśaṃ samuddiśya tapaḥ svayam
tuṣṭastu tapasā tasya bhavo jñātvā sa vāñchitam //
1.41.d:
दुश्चरं विचचारेशं समुद्दिश्य तपः स्वयम्
तुष्टस्तु तपसा तस्य भवो ज्ञात्वा स वाञ्छितम् ॥
1.41.m: personally performed severe asceticism directed towards the Lord. / Pleased with his asceticism and knowing what he desired, Bhava,

1.41.s:
lalāṭamadhyaṃ nirbhidya brahmaṇaḥ puruṣasya tu
putrasnehamiti procya strīpuṃrūpo 'bhavattadā //
1.41.d:
ललाटमध्यं निर्भिद्य ब्रह्मणः पुरुषस्य तु
पुत्रस्नेहमिति प्रोच्य स्त्रीपुंरूपो ऽभवत्तदा ॥
1.41.m: bursting forth from the middle of the forehead of the Puruṣa Brahmā, / proclaiming, 'This is love for a son,' became of female and male form at that time.

1.41.s:
tasya putro mahādevo hy ardhanārīśvaro 'bhavat
dadāha bhagavānsarvaṃ brahmāṇaṃ ca jagadgurum //
1.41.d:
तस्य पुत्रो महादेवो ह्य् अर्धनारीश्वरो ऽभवत्
ददाह भगवान्सर्वं ब्रह्माणं च जगद्गुरुम् ॥
1.41.m: His son became Mahādeva, the Lord Who is Half-Woman; / the Lord burned everything, including Brahmā, the teacher of the universe.

1.41.s:
athārdhamātrāṃ kalyāṇīm ātmanaḥ parameśvarīm
bubhuje yogamārgeṇa vṛddhyarthaṃ jagatāṃ śivaḥ //
1.41.d:
अथार्धमात्रां कल्याणीम् आत्मनः परमेश्वरीम्
बुभुजे योगमार्गेण वृद्ध्यर्थं जगतां शिवः ॥
1.41.m: Then, through the path of yoga, Śiva enjoyed that auspicious half-mātrā, / his own Supreme Goddess, for the sake of the increase of the worlds.

1.41.s:
tasyāṃ hariṃ ca brahmāṇaṃ sasarja parameśvaraḥ
viśveśvarastu viśvātmā cāstraṃ pāśupataṃ tathā //
1.41.d:
तस्यां हरिं च ब्रह्माणं ससर्ज परमेश्वरः
विश्वेश्वरस्तु विश्वात्मा चास्त्रं पाशुपतं तथा ॥
1.41.m: Upon her, the Supreme Lord created Hari and Brahmā; / and the Lord of the Universe, the Soul of All, created the Pāśupata weapon.

1.41.s:
tasmādbrahmā mahādevyāś cāṃśajaś ca haris tathā
aṇḍajaḥ padmajaścaiva bhavāṅgabhava eva ca //
1.41.d:
तस्माद्ब्रह्मा महादेव्याश् चांशजश् च हरिस् तथा
अण्डजः पद्मजश्चैव भवाङ्गभव एव च ॥
1.41.m: Therefore, Brahmā and Hari are born from a portion of the Great Goddess; / he is egg-born, lotus-born, and also born from Bhava's body.

1.41.s:
etatte kathitaṃ sarvam itihāsaṃ purātanam
parārdhaṃ brahmaṇo yāvat tāvadbhūtiḥ samāsataḥ //
1.41.d:
एतत्ते कथितं सर्वम् इतिहासं पुरातनम्
परार्धं ब्रह्मणो यावत् तावद्भूतिः समासतः ॥
1.41.m: All this ancient history has been recounted to you, / the extent of Brahmā's prosperity for a parārdha, in brief.

1.41.s:
vairāgyaṃ brahmaṇo vakṣye tamodbhūtaṃ samāsataḥ
nārāyaṇo 'pi bhagavān dvidhā kṛtvātmanastanum //
1.41.d:
वैराग्यं ब्रह्मणो वक्ष्ये तमोद्भूतं समासतः
नारायणो ऽपि भगवान् द्विधा कृत्वात्मनस्तनुम् ॥
1.41.m: I shall tell of Brahmā's detachment arising from darkness, in brief: / the lord Nārāyaṇa, having divided his own body in two,

1.41.s:
sasarja sakalaṃ tasmāt svāṅgādeva carācaram
tato brahmāṇamasṛjad brahmā rudraṃ pitāmahaḥ //
1.41.d:
ससर्ज सकलं तस्मात् स्वाङ्गादेव चराचरम्
ततो ब्रह्माणमसृजद् ब्रह्मा रुद्रं पितामहः ॥
1.41.m: created from that very body of his all that moves and does not move. / Then he created Brahmā; Pitāmaha Brahmā created Rudra.

1.41.s:
mune kalpāntare rudro hariṃ brahmāṇam īśvaram
tato brahmāṇamasṛjan mune kalpāntare hariḥ //
1.41.d:
मुने कल्पान्तरे रुद्रो हरिं ब्रह्माणम् ईश्वरम्
ततो ब्रह्माणमसृजन् मुने कल्पान्तरे हरिः ॥
1.41.m: In another kalpa, O sage, Rudra created Hari and Brahmā, the Lord; / then Hari created Brahmā in another kalpa, O sage;

1.41.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ punarbrahmā brahmāṇaṃ ca punarbhavaḥ
tadā vicārya vai brahmā duḥkhaṃ saṃsāra ityajaḥ //
1.41.d:
नारायणं पुनर्ब्रह्मा ब्रह्माणं च पुनर्भवः
तदा विचार्य वै ब्रह्मा दुःखं संसार इत्यजः ॥
1.41.m: again Brahmā created Nārāyaṇa, and again Bhava created Brahmā. / Then, reflecting that worldly existence is suffering, the unborn Brahmā,

1.41.s:
sargaṃ visṛjya cātmānam ātmanyeva niyojya ca
saṃhṛtya prāṇasañcāraṃ pāṣāṇa iva niścalaḥ //
1.41.d:
सर्गं विसृज्य चात्मानम् आत्मन्येव नियोज्य च
संहृत्य प्राणसञ्चारं पाषाण इव निश्चलः ॥
1.41.m: abandoning creation and fixing himself solely in the Self, / restraining the movement of the breath, motionless like a stone,

1.41.s:
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi samādhistho 'bhavatprabhuḥ
adhomukhaṃ tu yatpadmaṃ hṛdi saṃsthaṃ suśobhanam //
1.41.d:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि समाधिस्थो ऽभवत्प्रभुः
अधोमुखं तु यत्पद्मं हृदि संस्थं सुशोभनम् ॥
1.41.m: the Lord remained absorbed in meditation for ten thousand years. / The lotus that was downward-facing, situated within the heart, most beautiful,

1.41.s:
pūritaṃ pūrakeṇaiva prabuddhaṃ cābhavattadā
tadūrdhvavaktram abhavat kumbhakena nirodhitam //
1.41.d:
पूरितं पूरकेणैव प्रबुद्धं चाभवत्तदा
तदूर्ध्ववक्त्रम् अभवत् कुम्भकेन निरोधितम् ॥
1.41.m: was filled by inhalation alone and then blossomed; / it became turned upward, held restrained by breath-retention.

1.41.s:
tatpadmakarṇikāmadhye sthāpayāmāsa ceśvaram
tadomiti śivaṃ devam ardhamātrāparaṃ param //
1.41.d:
तत्पद्मकर्णिकामध्ये स्थापयामास चेश्वरम्
तदोमिति शिवं देवम् अर्धमात्रापरं परम् ॥
1.41.m: In the middle of the pericarp of that lotus, he established the Lord, / that divine Śiva who is 'Om', higher than the highest, beyond the half-mātrā,

1.41.s:
mṛṇālatantubhāgaikaśatabhāge vyavasthitam
yamī yamaviśuddhātmā niyamyaivaṃ hṛdīśvaram //
1.41.d:
मृणालतन्तुभागैकशतभागे व्यवस्थितम्
यमी यमविशुद्धात्मा नियम्यैवं हृदीश्वरम् ॥
1.41.m: abiding within a hundredth part of a lotus-filament. / Self-restrained, purified by restraints, having thus restrained the Lord within his heart,

1.41.s:
yamapuṣpādibhiḥ pūjyaṃ yājyo hyayajadavyayam
tasya hṛtkamalasthasya niyogāccāṃśajo vibhuḥ //
1.41.d:
यमपुष्पादिभिः पूज्यं याज्यो ह्ययजदव्ययम्
तस्य हृत्कमलस्थस्य नियोगाच्चांशजो विभुः ॥
1.41.m: the sacrificer worshipped the imperishable one who is worthy of worship with the flowers of restraint and the like. / By the command of that one situated in the heart-lotus, the pervasive lord born of a portion,

1.41.s:
lalāṭamasya nirbhidya prādurāsītpitāmahāt
lohito 'bhūt svayaṃ nīlaḥ śivasya hṛdayodbhavaḥ //
1.41.d:
ललाटमस्य निर्भिद्य प्रादुरासीत्पितामहात्
लोहितो ऽभूत् स्वयं नीलः शिवस्य हृदयोद्भवः ॥
1.41.m: bursting forth from his forehead, manifested from Pitāmaha. / He was red and dark blue himself, born from Śiva's heart.

1.41.s:
vahneścaiva tu saṃyogāt prakṛtya puruṣaḥ prabhuḥ
nīlaś ca lohitaścaiva yataḥ kālākṛtiḥ pumān //
1.41.d:
वह्नेश्चैव तु संयोगात् प्रकृत्य पुरुषः प्रभुः
नीलश् च लोहितश्चैव यतः कालाकृतिः पुमान् ॥
1.41.m: Because of the union with fire, the Lord is by nature Puruṣa; / because the Puruṣa is dark blue and red, having the form of Kāla,

1.41.s:
nīlalohita ityuktas tena devena vai prabhuḥ
brahmaṇā bhagavānkālaḥ prītātmā cābhavadvibhuḥ //
1.41.d:
नीललोहित इत्युक्तस् तेन देवेन वै प्रभुः
ब्रह्मणा भगवान्कालः प्रीतात्मा चाभवद्विभुः ॥
1.41.m: the Lord was called Nīlalohita by that god. / The lord Kāla was delighted in soul by Brahmā.

1.41.s:
suprītamanasaṃ devaṃ tuṣṭāva ca pitāmahaḥ
nāmāṣṭakena viśvātmā viśvātmānaṃ mahāmune //
1.41.d:
सुप्रीतमनसं देवं तुष्टाव च पितामहः
नामाष्टकेन विश्वात्मा विश्वात्मानं महामुने ॥
1.41.m: And Pitāmaha praised the well-pleased god, / the Soul of All [praising] the Soul of All with eight names, O great sage.

1.41.s:
pitāmaha uvāca
namaste bhagavan rudra bhāskarāmitatejase
namo bhavāya devāya rasāyāmbumayāya te //
1.41.d:
पितामह उवाच
नमस्ते भगवन् रुद्र भास्करामिततेजसे
नमो भवाय देवाय रसायाम्बुमयाय ते ॥
1.41.m: Pitāmaha said: / Homage to you, O Lord Rudra, whose splendor is immeasurable as the sun! / Homage to Bhava, the god whose nature is taste and water!

1.41.s:
śarvāya kṣitirūpāya sadā surabhiṇe namaḥ
īśāya vāyave tubhyaṃ saṃsparśāya namo namaḥ //
1.41.d:
शर्वाय क्षितिरूपाय सदा सुरभिणे नमः
ईशाय वायवे तुभ्यं संस्पर्शाय नमो नमः ॥
1.41.m: Homage to Śarva, whose form is the earth, ever fragrant! / Homage, homage to Īśa, who is the wind, whose nature is touch!

1.41.s:
paśūnāṃ pataye caiva pāvakāyātitejase
bhīmāya vyomarūpāya śabdamātrāya te namaḥ //
1.41.d:
पशूनां पतये चैव पावकायातितेजसे
भीमाय व्योमरूपाय शब्दमात्राय ते नमः ॥
1.41.m: And to the Lord of Beasts, to the Fire of supreme brilliance; / homage to Bhīma, whose form is space, whose nature is sound alone!

1.41.s:
mahādevāya somāya amṛtāya namo 'stu te
ugrāya yajamānāya namaste karmayogine //
1.41.d:
महादेवाय सोमाय अमृताय नमो ऽस्तु ते
उग्राय यजमानाय नमस्ते कर्मयोगिने ॥
1.41.m: Homage be to Mahādeva, who is Soma, the nectar! / To Ugra, who is the sacrificer, homage to you, the practitioner of karma-yoga!

1.41.s:
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi paitāmahamimaṃ stavam
rudrāya kathitaṃ viprāñ śrāvayedvā samāhitaḥ //
1.41.d:
यः पठेच्छृणुयाद्वापि पैतामहमिमं स्तवम्
रुद्राय कथितं विप्राञ् श्रावयेद्वा समाहितः ॥
1.41.m: Whoever recites or even listens to this hymn composed by Pitāmaha / addressed to Rudra, or recites it with concentrated mind to brahmins,

1.41.s:
aṣṭamūrtestu sāyujyaṃ varṣādekādavāpnuyāt
evaṃ stutvā mahādevam avaikṣata pitāmahaḥ //
1.41.d:
अष्टमूर्तेस्तु सायुज्यं वर्षादेकादवाप्नुयात्
एवं स्तुत्वा महादेवम् अवैक्षत पितामहः ॥
1.41.m: would attain union with the Eight-formed One after one year. / Having praised Mahādeva in this way, Pitāmaha looked around.

1.41.s:
tadāṣṭadhā mahādevaḥ samātiṣṭhatsamantataḥ
tadā prakāśate bhānuḥ kṛṣṇavartmā niśākaraḥ //
1.41.d:
तदाष्टधा महादेवः समातिष्ठत्समन्ततः
तदा प्रकाशते भानुः कृष्णवर्त्मा निशाकरः ॥
1.41.m: Then Mahādeva stood firmly on all sides in eight forms: / then the sun shines forth, [as do] fire and the moon,

1.41.s:
kṣitirvāyuḥ pumānaṃbhaḥ suṣiraṃ sarvagaṃ tathā
tadāprabhṛti taṃ prāhur aṣṭamūrtiritīśvaram //
1.41.d:
क्षितिर्वायुः पुमानंभः सुषिरं सर्वगं तथा
तदाप्रभृति तं प्राहुर् अष्टमूर्तिरितीश्वरम् ॥
1.41.m: earth, wind, the male person, water, and all-pervading space. / From then on, they call that Lord the Eight-formed One.

1.41.s:
aṣṭamūrteḥ prasādena virañciścāsṛjatpunaḥ
sṛṣṭvaitad akhilaṃ brahmā punaḥ kalpāntare prabhuḥ //
1.41.d:
अष्टमूर्तेः प्रसादेन विरञ्चिश्चासृजत्पुनः
सृष्ट्वैतद् अखिलं ब्रह्मा पुनः कल्पान्तरे प्रभुः ॥
1.41.m: By the grace of the Eight-formed One, Viriñca created again. / Having created all this, Lord Brahmā again in another kalpa,

1.41.s:
sahasrayugaparyantaṃ saṃsupte ca carācare
prajāḥ sraṣṭumanās tepe tata ugraṃ tapo mahat //
1.41.d:
सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तं संसुप्ते च चराचरे
प्रजाः स्रष्टुमनास् तेपे तत उग्रं तपो महत् ॥
1.41.m: when the moving and unmoving had fully slept for the span of a thousand yugas, / wishing to create living beings, performed great and fierce austerities.

1.41.s:
tasyaivaṃ tapyamānasya na kiṃcitsamavartata
tato dīrgheṇa kālena duḥkhātkrodho vyajāyata //
1.41.d:
तस्यैवं तप्यमानस्य न किंचित्समवर्तत
ततो दीर्घेण कालेन दुःखात्क्रोधो व्यजायत ॥
1.41.m: While he was thus engaged in austerities, nothing came into being. / Then, after a long time, anger arose out of distress.

1.41.s:
krodhāviṣṭasya netrābhyāṃ prāpatannaśrubindavaḥ
tatastebhyo 'śrubindubhyo bhūtāḥ pretāstadābhavan //
1.41.d:
क्रोधाविष्टस्य नेत्राभ्यां प्रापतन्नश्रुबिन्दवः
ततस्तेभ्यो ऽश्रुबिन्दुभ्यो भूताः प्रेतास्तदाभवन् ॥
1.41.m: From the eyes of him seized by anger, tears fell; / then from those tear-drops, ghosts and departed spirits arose.

1.41.s:
sarvāṃstānagrajāndṛṣṭvā bhūtapretaniśācarān
anindata tadā devo brahmātmānam ajo vibhuḥ //
1.41.d:
सर्वांस्तानग्रजान्दृष्ट्वा भूतप्रेतनिशाचरान्
अनिन्दत तदा देवो ब्रह्मात्मानम् अजो विभुः ॥
1.41.m: Seeing all those firstborn—the ghosts, departed spirits, and night-wanderers— / the unborn, all-pervading divine Brahmā then reproached himself.

1.41.s:
jahau prāṇāṃś ca bhagavān krodhāviṣṭaḥ prajāpatiḥ
tataḥ prāṇamayo rudraḥ prādurāsītprabhormukhāt //
1.41.d:
जहौ प्राणांश् च भगवान् क्रोधाविष्टः प्रजापतिः
ततः प्राणमयो रुद्रः प्रादुरासीत्प्रभोर्मुखात् ॥
1.41.m: Overwhelmed by anger, the Lord, the lord of creatures, gave up his life-breaths. / Then, consisting of life-breath, Rudra manifested from the lord’s mouth,

1.41.s:
ardhanārīśvaro bhūtvā bālārkasadṛśadyutiḥ
tadaikādaśadhātmānaṃ pravibhajya vyavasthitaḥ //
1.41.d:
अर्धनारीश्वरो भूत्वा बालार्कसदृशद्युतिः
तदैकादशधात्मानं प्रविभज्य व्यवस्थितः ॥
1.41.m: having become Ardhanārīśvara, with the brilliance of the rising sun; / then dividing himself elevenfold, he remained.

1.41.s:
ardhenāṃśena sarvātmā sasarjāsau śivāmumām
sā cāsṛjattadā lakṣmīṃ durgāṃ śreṣṭhāṃ sarasvatīm //
1.41.d:
अर्धेनांशेन सर्वात्मा ससर्जासौ शिवामुमाम्
सा चासृजत्तदा लक्ष्मीं दुर्गां श्रेष्ठां सरस्वतीम् ॥
1.41.m: With half of his portion, that Self of all created the auspicious Umā, / and she then created Lakṣmī, Durgā, and the supreme Sarasvatī,

1.41.s:
vāmāṃ raudrīṃ mahāmāyāṃ vaiṣṇavīṃ vārijekṣaṇām
kalāṃ vikiriṇīṃ caiva kālīṃ kamalavāsinīm //
1.41.d:
वामां रौद्रीं महामायां वैष्णवीं वारिजेक्षणाम्
कलां विकिरिणीं चैव कालीं कमलवासिनीम् ॥
1.41.m: Vāmā, Raudrī, Mahāmāyā, lotus-eyed Vaiṣṇavī, / Kalā, Vikiriṇī, Kālī, and she who dwells in the lotus,

1.41.s:
balavikariṇīṃ devīṃ balapramathinīṃ tathā
sarvabhūtasya damanīṃ sasṛje ca manonmanīm //
1.41.d:
बलविकरिणीं देवीं बलप्रमथिनीं तथा
सर्वभूतस्य दमनीं ससृजे च मनोन्मनीम् ॥
1.41.m: the goddess Balavikariṇī, Balapramathinī, / the subduer of all beings, and she created Manonmanī.

1.41.s:
tathānyā bahavaḥ sṛṣṭās tayā nāryaḥ sahasraśaḥ
rudraiścaiva mahādevas tābhistribhuvaneśvaraḥ //
1.41.d:
तथान्या बहवः सृष्टास् तया नार्यः सहस्रशः
रुद्रैश्चैव महादेवस् ताभिस्त्रिभुवनेश्वरः ॥
1.41.m: Likewise many other women were created by her in thousands. / Together with the Rudras and those [women], Mahādeva, the lord of the three worlds,

1.41.s:
sarvātmanaś ca tasyāgre hy atiṣṭhatparameśvaraḥ
mṛtasya tasya devasya brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ //
1.41.d:
सर्वात्मनश् च तस्याग्रे ह्य् अतिष्ठत्परमेश्वरः
मृतस्य तस्य देवस्य ब्रह्मणः परमेष्ठिनः ॥
1.41.m: the Supreme Lord, stood before the Self of all. / When that divine god Brahmā, the highest lord, was dead,

1.41.s:
ghṛṇī dadau punaḥ prāṇān brahmaputro maheśvaraḥ
brahmaṇaḥ pradadau prāṇān ātmasthāṃstu tadā prabhuḥ //
1.41.d:
घृणी ददौ पुनः प्राणान् ब्रह्मपुत्रो महेश्वरः
ब्रह्मणः प्रददौ प्राणान् आत्मस्थांस्तु तदा प्रभुः ॥
1.41.m: the compassionate Maheśvara, the son of Brahmā, gave him back his life-breaths. / The Lord then restored to Brahmā the life-breaths that resided in himself.

1.41.s:
prahṛṣṭo 'bhūttato rudraḥ kiṃcitpratyāgatāsavam
abhyabhāṣata deveśo brahmāṇaṃ paramaṃ vacaḥ //
1.41.d:
प्रहृष्टो ऽभूत्ततो रुद्रः किंचित्प्रत्यागतासवम्
अभ्यभाषत देवेशो ब्रह्माणं परमं वचः ॥
1.41.m: Then Rudra rejoiced; to him whose breath had somewhat returned, / the Lord of Gods addressed a supreme word to Brahmā:

1.41.s:
mā bhairdeva mahābhāga viriñca jagatāṃ guro
mayeha sthāpitāḥ prāṇās tasmāduttiṣṭha vai prabho //
1.41.d:
मा भैर्देव महाभाग विरिञ्च जगतां गुरो
मयेह स्थापिताः प्राणास् तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ वै प्रभो ॥
1.41.m: “Do not fear, fortunate god, Viriñca, teacher of the worlds! / The life-breaths have been established by me here, therefore arise, O Lord!”

1.41.s:
śrutvā vacastatastasya svapnabhūtaṃ manogatam
pitāmahaḥ prasannātmā netraiḥ phullāmbujaprabhaiḥ //
1.41.d:
श्रुत्वा वचस्ततस्तस्य स्वप्नभूतं मनोगतम्
पितामहः प्रसन्नात्मा नेत्रैः फुल्लाम्बुजप्रभैः ॥
1.41.m: Hearing that word of his, which had entered his mind like a dream, / Pitāmaha, his mind serene, with eyes possessing the luster of blossoming lotuses,

1.41.s:
tataḥ pratyāgataprāṇaḥ samudaikṣan maheśvaram
sa udvīkṣya ciraṃ kālaṃ snigdhagaṃbhīrayā girā //
1.41.d:
ततः प्रत्यागतप्राणः समुदैक्षन् महेश्वरम्
स उद्वीक्ष्य चिरं कालं स्निग्धगंभीरया गिरा ॥
1.41.m: his life-breath having returned, then looked upon Maheśvara. / Having gazed at him for a long time, with a deep and affectionate voice,

1.41.s:
uvāca bhagavān brahmā samutthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ
bho bho vada mahābhāga ānandayasi me manaḥ //
1.41.d:
उवाच भगवान् ब्रह्मा समुत्थाय कृताञ्जलिः
भो भो वद महाभाग आनन्दयसि मे मनः ॥
1.41.m: the blessed Brahmā, rising with folded hands, said: / “Hail, hail! Speak, O fortunate one! You delight my mind.

1.41.s:
ko bhavān aṣṭamūrtir vai sthita ekādaśātmakaḥ
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā vyājahāra maheśvaraḥ //
1.41.d:
को भवान् अष्टमूर्तिर् वै स्थित एकादशात्मकः
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा व्याजहार महेश्वरः ॥
1.41.m: Who are you, indeed, the Eight-formed One standing with eleven selves?” / Hearing that speech of his, Maheśvara replied,

1.41.s:
spṛśankarābhyāṃ brahmāṇaṃ sukhābhyāṃ sa surārihā
māṃ viddhi paramātmānam enāṃ māyāmajāmiti //
1.41.d:
स्पृशन्कराभ्यां ब्रह्माणं सुखाभ्यां स सुरारिहा
मां विद्धि परमात्मानम् एनां मायामजामिति ॥
1.41.m: touching Brahmā with his comforting hands, that slayer of the enemies of the gods: / “Know me to be the Supreme Self, and this [goddess] to be unborn Māyā.

1.41.s:
ete vai saṃsthitā rudrās tvāṃ rakṣitumihāgatāḥ
tataḥ praṇamya taṃ brahmā devadevamuvāca ha //
1.41.d:
एते वै संस्थिता रुद्रास् त्वां रक्षितुमिहागताः
ततः प्रणम्य तं ब्रह्मा देवदेवमुवाच ह ॥
1.41.m: These standing here are indeed the Rudras, who have come here to protect you.” / Then, bowing to him, Brahmā spoke to that God of Gods,

1.41.s:
kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā harṣagadgadayā girā
bhagavandevadeveśa duḥkhairākulito hyaham //
1.41.d:
कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा हर्षगद्गदया गिरा
भगवन्देवदेवेश दुःखैराकुलितो ह्यहम् ॥
1.41.m: having joined his hands in reverence, with a voice faltering with joy: / “O Blessed One, Lord of the Gods of Gods! I am indeed distressed by sorrows;

1.41.s:
saṃsārānmoktumīśāna māmihārhasi śaṅkara
tataḥ prahasya bhagavān pitāmahamumāpatiḥ //
1.41.d:
संसारान्मोक्तुमीशान मामिहार्हसि शङ्कर
ततः प्रहस्य भगवान् पितामहमुमापतिः ॥
1.41.m: O Īśāna, O Śaṅkara, you ought to liberate me from worldly existence!” / Then, laughing, the blessed Lord, the husband of Umā,

1.41.s:
tadā rudrairjagannāthas tayā cāntardadhe vibhuḥ
tasmācchilāda lokeṣu durlabho vai tvayonijaḥ //
1.41.d:
तदा रुद्रैर्जगन्नाथस् तया चान्तर्दधे विभुः
तस्माच्छिलाद लोकेषु दुर्लभो वै त्वयोनिजः ॥
1.41.m: the all-pervading lord of the universe vanished then together with the Rudras and with her. / “Therefore, O Śilāda, one who is not born from a womb is indeed difficult to obtain in the worlds.

1.41.s:
mṛtyuhīnaḥ pumānviddhi samṛtyuḥ padmajo 'pi saḥ
kiṃtu deveśvaro rudraḥ prasīdati yadīśvaraḥ //
1.41.d:
मृत्युहीनः पुमान्विद्धि समृत्युः पद्मजो ऽपि सः
किंतु देवेश्वरो रुद्रः प्रसीदति यदीश्वरः ॥
1.41.m: Know that a man is subject to death; even that lotus-born [Brahmā] is subject to death. / But if Rudra, the Lord of Gods, the Lord, is pleased,

1.41.s:
na durlabho mṛtyuhīnas tava putro hyayonijaḥ
mayā ca viṣṇunā caiva brahmaṇā ca mahātmanā //
1.41.d:
न दुर्लभो मृत्युहीनस् तव पुत्रो ह्ययोनिजः
मया च विष्णुना चैव ब्रह्मणा च महात्मना ॥
1.41.m: a son for you, not born from a womb and free from death, is not difficult to obtain. / By me, and by Viṣṇu, and by the great-souled Brahmā,

1.41.s:
ayonijaṃ mṛtyuhīnam asamarthaṃ niveditum
evaṃ vyāhṛtya viprendram anugṛhya ca taṃ ghṛṇī //
1.41.d:
अयोनिजं मृत्युहीनम् असमर्थं निवेदितुम्
एवं व्याहृत्य विप्रेन्द्रम् अनुगृह्य च तं घृणी ॥
1.41.m: [such a son] not born from a womb and free from death cannot be granted.” / Having spoken thus to that best of brahmins and shown grace to him, the compassionate

1.41.s: devairvṛto yayau devaḥ sitenebhena vai prabhuḥ //
1.41.d: देवैर्वृतो ययौ देवः सितेनेभेन वै प्रभुः ॥
1.41.m: lord, surrounded by gods, departed on his white elephant.

1.42.s:
sūta uvāca
gate puṇye ca varade sahasrākṣe śilāśanaḥ
ārādhayanmahādevaṃ tapasātoṣayadbhavam //
1.42.d:
सूत उवाच
गते पुण्ये च वरदे सहस्राक्षे शिलाशनः
आराधयन्महादेवं तपसातोषयद्भवम् ॥
1.42.m: Sūta said: / When the virtuous, boon-granting thousand-eyed [Indra] had departed, Śilāśana, / worshipping Mahādeva, gratified Bhava with tapas.

1.42.s:
atha tasyaivamaniśaṃ tatparasya dvijasya tu
divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu gataṃ kṣaṇamivādbhutam //
1.42.d:
अथ तस्यैवमनिशं तत्परस्य द्विजस्य तु
दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं तु गतं क्षणमिवाद्भुतम् ॥
1.42.m: Then, as that brahmin was constantly intent on that, / a thousand divine years passed like a single wondrous moment.

1.42.s:
valmīkenāvṛtāṅgaś ca lakṣyaḥ kīṭagaṇairmuniḥ
vajrasūcīmukhaiścānyai raktakīṭaiś ca sarvataḥ //
1.42.d:
वल्मीकेनावृताङ्गश् च लक्ष्यः कीटगणैर्मुनिः
वज्रसूचीमुखैश्चान्यै रक्तकीटैश् च सर्वतः ॥
1.42.m: With his limbs covered by an anthill, the sage was pierced by swarms of insects, / and on all sides by blood-sucking insects with mouths like adamantine needles.

1.42.s:
nirmāṃsarudhiratvag vai nirlepaḥ kuḍyavat sthitaḥ
asthiśeṣo 'bhavatpaścāt tamamanyata śaṅkaraḥ //
1.42.d:
निर्मांसरुधिरत्वग् वै निर्लेपः कुड्यवत् स्थितः
अस्थिशेषो ऽभवत्पश्चात् तममन्यत शङ्करः ॥
1.42.m: Free of flesh, blood, and skin, spotless, standing like a wall, / he subsequently became nothing but bones; Śaṅkara regarded him with favor.

1.42.s:
yadā spṛṣṭo munistena kareṇa ca smarāriṇā
tadaiva muniśārdūlaś cotsasarja klamaṃ dvijaḥ //
1.42.d:
यदा स्पृष्टो मुनिस्तेन करेण च स्मरारिणा
तदैव मुनिशार्दूलश् चोत्ससर्ज क्लमं द्विजः ॥
1.42.m: When the sage was touched by that enemy of Smara with his hand, / at that very moment that tiger among sages, the twice-born, cast off his exhaustion.

1.42.s:
tapatastasya tapasā prabhustuṣṭātha śaṅkaraḥ
tuṣṭastavetyathovāca sagaṇaścomayā saha //
1.42.d:
तपतस्तस्य तपसा प्रभुस्तुष्टाथ शङ्करः
तुष्टस्तवेत्यथोवाच सगणश्चोमया सह ॥
1.42.m: As he performed austerities, the Lord Śaṅkara was pleased by his tapas; / together with his retinue and with Umā, he then said, “I am pleased with you!

1.42.s:
tapasānena kiṃ kāryaṃ bhavataste mahāmate
dadāmi putraṃ sarvajñaṃ sarvaśāstrārthapāragam //
1.42.d:
तपसानेन किं कार्यं भवतस्ते महामते
ददामि पुत्रं सर्वज्ञं सर्वशास्त्रार्थपारगम् ॥
1.42.m: What purpose of yours should be accomplished by this tapas, O broad-minded one? / I will grant you an omniscient son who has mastered the meaning of all treatises.”

1.42.s:
tataḥ praṇamya deveśaṃ stutvovāca śilāśanaḥ
harṣagadgadayā vācā somaṃ somavibhūṣaṇam //
1.42.d:
ततः प्रणम्य देवेशं स्तुत्वोवाच शिलाशनः
हर्षगद्गदया वाचा सोमं सोमविभूषणम् ॥
1.42.m: Then, bowing down to the Lord of Gods and praising him, Śilāśana spoke / with a voice trembling with joy to Soma, who is adorned with the moon:

1.42.s:
śilāda uvāca
bhagavandevadeveśa tripurārdana śaṅkara
ayonijaṃ mṛtyuhīnaṃ putramicchāmi sattama //
1.42.d:
शिलाद उवाच
भगवन्देवदेवेश त्रिपुरार्दन शङ्कर
अयोनिजं मृत्युहीनं पुत्रमिच्छामि सत्तम ॥
1.42.m: Śilāda said: / “O Blessed One, Lord of the Gods of Gods, destroyer of Tripura, O Śaṅkara! / I desire a son not born from a womb and free from death, O best of beings.”

1.42.s:
sūta uvāca
pūrvamārādhitaḥ prāha tapasā parameśvaraḥ
śilādaṃ brahmaṇā rudraḥ prītyā paramayā punaḥ //
1.42.d:
सूत उवाच
पूर्वमाराधितः प्राह तपसा परमेश्वरः
शिलादं ब्रह्मणा रुद्रः प्रीत्या परमया पुनः ॥
1.42.m: Sūta said: / Propitiated previously through tapas, the Supreme Lord, Rudra, / who had been praised by Brahmā, spoke again to Śilāda with supreme affection.

1.42.s:
śrīdevadeva uvāca
pūrvamārādhito vipra brahmaṇāhaṃ tapodhana
tapasā cāvatārārthaṃ munibhiś ca surottamaiḥ //
1.42.d:
श्रीदेवदेव उवाच
पूर्वमाराधितो विप्र ब्रह्मणाहं तपोधन
तपसा चावतारार्थं मुनिभिश् च सुरोत्तमैः ॥
1.42.m: The God of Gods said: / “Previously I was propitiated by Brahmā, O brahmin rich in tapas, / and by sages and the best of gods through tapas for the sake of an incarnation.

1.42.s:
tava putro bhaviṣyāmi nandināmnā tvayonijaḥ
pitā bhaviṣyasi mama piturvai jagatāṃ mune //
1.42.d:
तव पुत्रो भविष्यामि नन्दिनाम्ना त्वयोनिजः
पिता भविष्यसि मम पितुर्वै जगतां मुने ॥
1.42.m: I myself shall become your son by the name of Nandin, not born from a womb; / you, O sage, will become the father of me, the father of the worlds!”

1.42.s:
evamuktvā muniṃ prekṣya praṇipatya sthitaṃ ghṛṇī
somaḥ somopamaḥ prītas tatraivāntaradhīyata //
1.42.d:
एवमुक्त्वा मुनिं प्रेक्ष्य प्रणिपत्य स्थितं घृणी
सोमः सोमोपमः प्रीतस् तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥
1.42.m: Having spoken thus and looked upon the sage who stood having prostrated, the compassionate, / delighted Soma, resembling the moon, vanished right there.

1.42.s:
labdhaputraḥ pitā rudrāt prīto mama mahāmune
yajñāṅgaṇaṃ mahatprāpya yajñārthaṃ yajñavittamaḥ //
1.42.d:
लब्धपुत्रः पिता रुद्रात् प्रीतो मम महामुने
यज्ञाङ्गणं महत्प्राप्य यज्ञार्थं यज्ञवित्तमः ॥
1.42.m: [Nandin said:] “Having obtained a son from Rudra, my delighted father, O great sage, / the best knower of sacrifice, reached the great sacrificial courtyard for a sacrifice.

1.42.s:
tadaṅgaṇādahaṃ śaṃbhos tanujastasya cājñayā
saṃjātaḥ pūrvamevāhaṃ yugāntāgnisamaprabhaḥ //
1.42.d:
तदङ्गणादहं शंभोस् तनुजस्तस्य चाज्ञया
संजातः पूर्वमेवाहं युगान्ताग्निसमप्रभः ॥
1.42.m: From that courtyard, by Śambhu’s command, I was born as his son, / having arisen even before, radiant like the fire at the end of a yuga.”

1.42.s:
vavarṣustadā puṣkarāvartakādyā jaguḥ khecarāḥ kinnarāḥ siddhasādhyāḥ
śilādātmajatvaṃ gate mayyupendraḥ sasarjātha vṛṣṭiṃ supuṣpaughamiśrām //
1.42.d:
ववर्षुस्तदा पुष्करावर्तकाद्या जगुः खेचराः किन्नराः सिद्धसाध्याः
शिलादात्मजत्वं गते मय्युपेन्द्रः ससर्जाथ वृष्टिं सुपुष्पौघमिश्राम् ॥
1.42.m: Then the Puṣkarāvarta and other [clouds] rained down; the sky-goers, Kinnaras, Siddhas, and Sādhyas sang; / and when I had become the son of Śilāda, Upendra sent forth a rain mingled with showers of lovely flowers.

1.42.s:
māṃ dṛṣṭvā kālasūryābhaṃ jaṭāmukuṭadhāriṇam
tryakṣaṃ caturbhujaṃ bālaṃ śūlaṭaṅkagadādharam //
1.42.d:
मां दृष्ट्वा कालसूर्याभं जटामुकुटधारिणम्
त्र्यक्षं चतुर्भुजं बालं शूलटङ्कगदाधरम् ॥
1.42.m: Beholding me shining like the sun at the end of time, wearing a crown of matted hair, / three-eyed, four-armed, a boy bearing a trident, an axe, and a mace,

1.42.s:
vajriṇaṃ vajradaṃṣṭraṃ ca vajriṇārādhitaṃ śiśum
vajrakuṇḍalinaṃ ghoraṃ nīradopamaniḥsvanam //
1.42.d:
वज्रिणं वज्रदंष्ट्रं च वज्रिणाराधितं शिशुम्
वज्रकुण्डलिनं घोरं नीरदोपमनिःस्वनम् ॥
1.42.m: wielding a thunderbolt, with adamantine fangs, a child worshipped by the thunderbolt-wielder [Indra], / wearing adamantine earrings, terrible, with a voice resounding like a thundercloud,

1.42.s:
brahmādyāstuṣṭuvuḥ sarve surendraś ca munīśvarāḥ
neduḥ samantataḥ sarve nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ //
1.42.d:
ब्रह्माद्यास्तुष्टुवुः सर्वे सुरेन्द्रश् च मुनीश्वराः
नेदुः समन्ततः सर्वे ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः ॥
1.42.m: Brahmā and all the others, along with the lord of gods and the foremost sages, sang praises; / all made joyful cries on every side, and the celestial nymphs danced.

1.42.s:
ṛṣayo muniśārdūla ṛgyajuḥsāmasaṃbhavaiḥ
mantrairmāheśvaraiḥ stutvā sampraṇemurmudānvitāḥ //
1.42.d:
ऋषयो मुनिशार्दूल ऋग्यजुःसामसंभवैः
मन्त्रैर्माहेश्वरैः स्तुत्वा सम्प्रणेमुर्मुदान्विताः ॥
1.42.m: O tiger among sages, the ṛṣis, filled with joy, praised [me] with hymns belonging to Maheśvara / originating from the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāmavedas, and bowed down in reverence.

1.42.s:
brahmā hariś ca rudraś ca śakraḥ sākṣācchivāṃbikā
jīvaścendurmahātejā bhāskaraḥ pavano 'nalaḥ //
1.42.d:
ब्रह्मा हरिश् च रुद्रश् च शक्रः साक्षाच्छिवांबिका
जीवश्चेन्दुर्महातेजा भास्करः पवनो ऽनलः ॥
1.42.m: Brahmā, Hari, Rudra, and Śakra, Śivā and Ambikā in person, / Jīva [Bṛhaspati], the moon of great brilliance, the sun, the wind, fire,

1.42.s:
īśāno nirṛtiryakṣo yamo varuṇa eva ca
viśvedevās tathā rudrā vasavaś ca mahābalāḥ //
1.42.d:
ईशानो निरृतिर्यक्षो यमो वरुण एव च
विश्वेदेवास् तथा रुद्रा वसवश् च महाबलाः ॥
1.42.m: Īśāna, Nirṛti, the Yakṣa [Kubera], Yama, and Varuṇa, / the Viśvedevas, as well as the Rudras and the mighty Vasus,

1.42.s:
lakṣmīḥ sākṣācchacī jyeṣṭhā devī caiva sarasvatī
aditiś ca ditiścaiva śraddhā lajjā dhṛtis tathā //
1.42.d:
लक्ष्मीः साक्षाच्छची ज्येष्ठा देवी चैव सरस्वती
अदितिश् च दितिश्चैव श्रद्धा लज्जा धृतिस् तथा ॥
1.42.m: Lakṣmī, Śacī in person, Jyeṣṭhā, and goddess Sarasvatī, / Aditi and Diti, Śraddhā, Lajjā, and Dhṛti,

1.42.s:
nandā bhadrā ca surabhī suśīlā sumanās tathā
vṛṣendraś ca mahātejā dharmo dharmātmajas tathā //
1.42.d:
नन्दा भद्रा च सुरभी सुशीला सुमनास् तथा
वृषेन्द्रश् च महातेजा धर्मो धर्मात्मजस् तथा ॥
1.42.m: Nandā, Bhadrā, Surabhi, Suśīlā, and Sumanas, / the splendid bull-lord of great glory, Dharma, and the son of Dharma,

1.42.s:
āvṛtya māṃ tathāliṅgya tuṣṭuvurmunisattama
śilādo 'pi munirdṛṣṭvā pitā me tādṛśaṃ tadā //
1.42.d:
आवृत्य मां तथालिङ्ग्य तुष्टुवुर्मुनिसत्तम
शिलादो ऽपि मुनिर्दृष्ट्वा पिता मे तादृशं तदा ॥
1.42.m: surrounded me and embraced me, singing praises, O best of sages. / My father the sage Śilāda also, seeing me like that at that time,

1.42.s:
prītyā praṇamya puṇyātmā tuṣṭāveṣṭapradaṃ sutam
bhagavandevadeveśa triyaṃbaka mamāvyaya //
1.42.d:
प्रीत्या प्रणम्य पुण्यात्मा तुष्टावेष्टप्रदं सुतम्
भगवन्देवदेवेश त्रियंबक ममाव्यय ॥
1.42.m: the virtuous one bowed down with love and praised his son, the granter of desires: / 'O Lord, Lord of the gods of gods, O three-eyed one, my imperishable one!

1.42.s:
putro 'si jagatāṃ yasmāt trātā duḥkhāddhi kiṃ punaḥ
rakṣako jagatāṃ yasmāt pitā me putra sarvaga //
1.42.d:
पुत्रो ऽसि जगतां यस्मात् त्राता दुःखाद्धि किं पुनः
रक्षको जगतां यस्मात् पिता मे पुत्र सर्वग ॥
1.42.m: Because you are the son of the worlds, indeed their deliverer from sorrow, how much more so mine? / Because you are the protector of the worlds, my father, my son, all-pervading one!

1.42.s:
ayonija namastubhyaṃ jagadyone pitāmaha
pitā putra maheśāna jagatāṃ ca jagadguro //
1.42.d:
अयोनिज नमस्तुभ्यं जगद्योने पितामह
पिता पुत्र महेशान जगतां च जगद्गुरो ॥
1.42.m: O unborn one, homage to you; O origin of the universe, Pitāmaha, / father, son, Maheśāna, guru of the worlds and of the universe!

1.42.s:
vatsa vatsa mahābhāga pāhi māṃ parameśvara
tvayāhaṃ nandito yasmān nandī nāmnā sureśvara //
1.42.d:
वत्स वत्स महाभाग पाहि मां परमेश्वर
त्वयाहं नन्दितो यस्मान् नन्दी नाम्ना सुरेश्वर ॥
1.42.m: O child, child, highly fortunate one, protect me, Supreme Lord! / Because I am made joyful by you, you are named Nandī, O lord of gods!

1.42.s:
tasmānnandaya māṃ nandin namāmi jagadīśvaram
prasīda pitarau me 'dya rudralokaṃ gatau vibho //
1.42.d:
तस्मान्नन्दय मां नन्दिन् नमामि जगदीश्वरम्
प्रसीद पितरौ मे ऽद्य रुद्रलोकं गतौ विभो ॥
1.42.m: Therefore, O Nandin, make me joyful! I bow to the Lord of the universe. / Be gracious, O all-pervading one; my parents have gone to the world of Rudra today,

1.42.s:
pitāmahaś ca bho nandin navatīrṇe maheśvare
mamaiva saphalaṃ loke janma vai jagatāṃ prabho //
1.42.d:
पितामहश् च भो नन्दिन् नवतीर्णे महेश्वरे
ममैव सफलं लोके जन्म वै जगतां प्रभो ॥
1.42.m: as well as my grandfather, O Nandin, now that Maheśvara has descended. / Fruitful indeed is my birth in this world, O Lord of the universe!

1.42.s:
avatīrṇe sute nandin rakṣārthaṃ mahyamīśvara
tubhyaṃ namaḥ sureśāna nandīśvara namo 'stu te //
1.42.d:
अवतीर्णे सुते नन्दिन् रक्षार्थं मह्यमीश्वर
तुभ्यं नमः सुरेशान नन्दीश्वर नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
1.42.m: Now that you have descended as my son, O Nandin, for my protection, O Lord! / Homage to you, ruler of gods, O lord Nandīśvara, homage be to you!

1.42.s:
putra pāhi mahābāho devadeva jagadguro
putratvameva nandīśa matvā yatkīrtitaṃ mayā //
1.42.d:
पुत्र पाहि महाबाहो देवदेव जगद्गुरो
पुत्रत्वमेव नन्दीश मत्वा यत्कीर्तितं मया ॥
1.42.m: O son, protect me, mighty-armed one, God of gods, Teacher of the universe! / Whatever has been praised by me, considering you merely as a son, O lord of Nandī,

1.42.s:
tvayā tatkṣamyatāṃ vatsa stavastavya surāsuraiḥ
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi mama putraprabhāṣitam //
1.42.d:
त्वया तत्क्षम्यतां वत्स स्तवस्तव्य सुरासुरैः
यः पठेच्छृणुयाद्वापि मम पुत्रप्रभाषितम् ॥
1.42.m: let that be forgiven by you, dear child, who are to be praised with hymns by gods and asuras. / Whoever recites or listens to this spoken by my son,

1.42.s:
śrāvayedvā dvijān bhaktyā mayā sārdhaṃ sa modate
evaṃ stutvā sutaṃ bālaṃ praṇamya bahumānataḥ //
1.42.d:
श्रावयेद्वा द्विजान् भक्त्या मया सार्धं स मोदते
एवं स्तुत्वा सुतं बालं प्रणम्य बहुमानतः ॥
1.42.m: or causes the twice-born to hear it with devotion, rejoices together with me.' / Having thus praised the young child and bowed down with great respect,

1.42.s:
munīśvarāṃś ca samprekṣya śilāda uvāca suvrataḥ
paśyadhvaṃ munayaḥ sarve mahābhāgyaṃ mamāvyayaḥ //
1.42.d:
मुनीश्वरांश् च सम्प्रेक्ष्य शिलाद उवाच सुव्रतः
पश्यध्वं मुनयः सर्वे महाभाग्यं ममाव्ययः ॥
1.42.m: and beholding the foremost sages, Śilāda of noble vows said: / 'Look, all you sages, at my immense fortune! The imperishable

1.42.s:
nandī yajñāṅgaṇe devaś cāvatīrṇo yataḥ prabhuḥ
matsamaḥ kaḥ pumāṃlloke devo vā dānavo 'pi vā //
1.42.d:
नन्दी यज्ञाङ्गणे देवश् चावतीर्णो यतः प्रभुः
मत्समः कः पुमांल्लोके देवो वा दानवो ऽपि वा ॥
1.42.m: Lord Nandī, the divine ruler, has descended into my sacrificial courtyard! / Who is equal to me in this world, whether human, god, or even Dānava,

1.42.s: eṣa nandī yato jāto yajñabhūmau hitāya me //
1.42.d: एष नन्दी यतो जातो यज्ञभूमौ हिताय मे ॥
1.42.m: since this Nandī has been born upon the sacrificial ground for my welfare?'

1.43.s:
nandikeśvara uvāca
mayā saha pitā hṛṣṭaḥ praṇamya ca maheśvaram
uṭajaṃ svaṃ jagāmāśu nidhiṃ labdhveva nirdhanaḥ //
1.43.d:
नन्दिकेश्वर उवाच
मया सह पिता हृष्टः प्रणम्य च महेश्वरम्
उटजं स्वं जगामाशु निधिं लब्ध्वेव निर्धनः ॥
1.43.m: Nandikeśvara said: / Joyful along with me, and having bowed to Maheśvara, my father / went quickly to his hermitage, like a poor man who has obtained a treasure.

1.43.s:
yadāgato 'hamuṭajaṃ śilādasya mahāmune
tadā vai daivikaṃ rūpaṃ tyaktvā mānuṣyam āsthitaḥ //
1.43.d:
यदागतो ऽहमुटजं शिलादस्य महामुने
तदा वै दैविकं रूपं त्यक्त्वा मानुष्यम् आस्थितः ॥
1.43.m: When I had arrived at the hermitage of Śilāda, O great sage, / then having abandoned my divine form, I assumed human nature.

1.43.s:
naṣṭā caiva smṛtirdivyā yena kenāpi kāraṇāt
mānuṣyamāsthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā pitā me lokapūjitaḥ //
1.43.d:
नष्टा चैव स्मृतिर्दिव्या येन केनापि कारणात्
मानुष्यमास्थितं दृष्ट्वा पिता मे लोकपूजितः ॥
1.43.m: And divine memory was lost, for whatever reason. / Seeing me having assumed human nature, my father, revered by the world,

1.43.s:
vilalāpātiduḥkhārtaḥ svajanaiś ca samāvṛtaḥ
jātakarmādikāścaiva cakāra mama sarvavit //
1.43.d:
विललापातिदुःखार्तः स्वजनैश् च समावृतः
जातकर्मादिकाश्चैव चकार मम सर्ववित् ॥
1.43.m: lamented, overwhelmed with deep sorrow, surrounded by his kinsfolk. / Then, all-knowing, he performed the birth rites and other ceremonies for me.

1.43.s:
śālaṅkāyanaputro vai śilādaḥ putravatsalaḥ
upadiṣṭā hi tenaiva ṛkśākhā yajuṣas tathā //
1.43.d:
शालङ्कायनपुत्रो वै शिलादः पुत्रवत्सलः
उपदिष्टा हि तेनैव ऋक्शाखा यजुषस् तथा ॥
1.43.m: Śilāda, the son of Śālaṅkāyana, devoted to his son, / taught me the branches of the Ṛgveda and the branches of the Yajurveda,

1.43.s:
sāmaśākhāsahasraṃ ca sāṅgopāṅgaṃ mahāmune
āyurvedaṃ dhanurvedaṃ gāndharvaṃ cāśvalakṣaṇam //
1.43.d:
सामशाखासहस्रं च साङ्गोपाङ्गं महामुने
आयुर्वेदं धनुर्वेदं गान्धर्वं चाश्वलक्षणम् ॥
1.43.m: and the thousand branches of the Sāmaveda together with the limbs and secondary limbs, O great sage, / as well as Āyurveda, Dhanurveda, Gāndharvaveda, the signs of horses,

1.43.s:
hastināṃ caritaṃ caiva narāṇāṃ caiva lakṣaṇam
sampūrṇe saptame varṣe tato 'tha munisattamau //
1.43.d:
हस्तिनां चरितं चैव नराणां चैव लक्षणम्
सम्पूर्णे सप्तमे वर्षे ततो ऽथ मुनिसत्तमौ ॥
1.43.m: the nature of elephants, and the bodily marks of men. / Then, when the seventh year was completed, two foremost sages,

1.43.s:
mitrāvaruṇanāmānau tapoyogabalānvitau
tasyāśramaṃ gatau divyau draṣṭuṃ māṃ cājñayā vibhoḥ //
1.43.d:
मित्रावरुणनामानौ तपोयोगबलान्वितौ
तस्याश्रमं गतौ दिव्यौ द्रष्टुं मां चाज्ञया विभोः ॥
1.43.m: named Mitra and Varuṇa, endowed with the power of asceticism and yoga, / divine ones, came to his hermitage to see me by the command of the Lord.

1.43.s:
ūcatuś ca mahātmānau māṃ nirīkṣya muhurmuhuḥ
tāta nandyayamalpāyuḥ sarvaśāstrārthapāragaḥ //
1.43.d:
ऊचतुश् च महात्मानौ मां निरीक्ष्य मुहुर्मुहुः
तात नन्द्ययमल्पायुः सर्वशास्त्रार्थपारगः ॥
1.43.m: Looking at me again and again, the two great-souled ones said: / 'O father, this Nandi, who has mastered the meaning of all the scriptures, is short-lived.

1.43.s:
na dṛṣṭamevamāścaryam āyurvarṣādataḥ param
ityuktavati viprendraḥ śilādaḥ putravatsalaḥ //
1.43.d:
न दृष्टमेवमाश्चर्यम् आयुर्वर्षादतः परम्
इत्युक्तवति विप्रेन्द्रः शिलादः पुत्रवत्सलः ॥
1.43.m: No life beyond a year from now is seen; this is a wondrous thing.' / When they had spoken thus, the foremost among the twice-born, Śilāda, affectionate toward his son,

1.43.s:
samāliṅgya ca duḥkhārto rurodātīva visvaram
hā putra putra putreti papāta ca samantataḥ //
1.43.d:
समालिङ्ग्य च दुःखार्तो रुरोदातीव विस्वरम्
हा पुत्र पुत्र पुत्रेति पपात च समन्ततः ॥
1.43.m: embraced [me] and, overcome with sorrow, wept in an extremely altered voice: / 'Alas, my son, my son, my son!' and fell to the ground on all sides.

1.43.s:
aho balaṃ daivavidher vidhātuśceti duḥkhitaḥ
tasya cārtasvaraṃ śrutvā tadāśramanivāsinaḥ //
1.43.d:
अहो बलं दैवविधेर् विधातुश्चेति दुःखितः
तस्य चार्तस्वरं श्रुत्वा तदाश्रमनिवासिनः ॥
1.43.m: Sorrowful, [he cried]: 'Ah, the power of divine destiny and the Creator!' / Hearing his distressed cry, the dwellers of that hermitage

1.43.s:
nipeturvihvalātyarthaṃ rakṣāścakruś ca maṅgalam
tuṣṭuvuś ca mahādevaṃ triyaṃbakamumāpatim //
1.43.d:
निपेतुर्विह्वलात्यर्थं रक्षाश्चक्रुश् च मङ्गलम्
तुष्टुवुश् च महादेवं त्रियंबकमुमापतिम् ॥
1.43.m: gathered, greatly distressed, and performed protective and auspicious rites; / they also praised Mahādeva, the three-eyed Lord of Umā.

1.43.s:
hutvā triyaṃbakenaiva madhunaiva ca saṃplutām
dūrvāmayutasaṃkhyātāṃ sarvadravyasamanvitām //
1.43.d:
हुत्वा त्रियंबकेनैव मधुनैव च संप्लुताम्
दूर्वामयुतसंख्यातां सर्वद्रव्यसमन्विताम् ॥
1.43.m: Having offered oblations with the Tryambaka mantra, [offering] dūrvā grass / numbering ten thousand, soaked in honey and accompanied by all proper substances,

1.43.s:
pitā vigatasaṃjñaś ca tathā caiva pitāmahaḥ
viceṣṭaś ca lalāpāsau mṛtavannipapāta ca //
1.43.d:
पिता विगतसंज्ञश् च तथा चैव पितामहः
विचेष्टश् च ललापासौ मृतवन्निपपात च ॥
1.43.m: my father lost consciousness, as did my grandfather; / motionless, he lamented and fell down as if dead.

1.43.s:
mṛtyor bhīto 'ham acirāc chirasā cābhivandya tam
mṛtavatpatitaṃ sākṣāt pitaraṃ ca pitāmaham //
1.43.d:
मृत्योर् भीतो ऽहम् अचिराच् छिरसा चाभिवन्द्य तम्
मृतवत्पतितं साक्षात् पितरं च पितामहम् ॥
1.43.m: Frightened of imminent death, I bowed my head to him, / to my father and grandfather who had fallen in person like dead men,

1.43.s:
pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ca taṃ rudrajāpyarato 'bhavam
hṛtpuṇḍarīke suṣire dhyātvā devaṃ triyaṃbakam //
1.43.d:
प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य च तं रुद्रजाप्यरतो ऽभवम्
हृत्पुण्डरीके सुषिरे ध्यात्वा देवं त्रियंबकम् ॥
1.43.m: and circumambulated them, and became devoted to the muttered prayer to Rudra, / having meditated in the cavity of the heart-lotus upon the divine three-eyed god,

1.43.s:
tryakṣaṃ daśabhujaṃ śāntaṃ pañcavaktraṃ sadāśivam
saritaścāntare puṇye sthitaṃ māṃ parameśvaraḥ //
1.43.d:
त्र्यक्षं दशभुजं शान्तं पञ्चवक्त्रं सदाशिवम्
सरितश्चान्तरे पुण्ये स्थितं मां परमेश्वरः ॥
1.43.m: three-eyed, ten-armed, peaceful, five-faced Sadāśiva. / While I stood within a sacred river, the Supreme Lord,

1.43.s:
tuṣṭo 'bravīnmahādevaḥ somaḥ somārdhabhūṣaṇaḥ
vatsa nandinmahābāho mṛtyorbhītiḥ kutastava //
1.43.d:
तुष्टो ऽब्रवीन्महादेवः सोमः सोमार्धभूषणः
वत्स नन्दिन्महाबाहो मृत्योर्भीतिः कुतस्तव ॥
1.43.m: gratified, Mahādeva, Soma, adorned with the crescent moon, spoke: / 'Child Nandin, mighty-armed one, whence this fear of death for you?

1.43.s:
mayaiva preṣitau viprau matsamastvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
vatsainattava dehaṃ ca laukikaṃ paramārthataḥ //
1.43.d:
मयैव प्रेषितौ विप्रौ मत्समस्त्वं न संशयः
वत्सैनत्तव देहं च लौकिकं परमार्थतः ॥
1.43.m: It was by me that the two twice-born ones were sent; you are equal to me, of this there is no doubt. / Child, this body of yours is worldly in ultimate reality;

1.43.s:
nāstyeva daivikaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śilādena purā tava
